This limits their use in tasks such as robotic policy evaluation and model-based planning, where nearly identical actions can lead to qualitatively different outcomes. To address this, we propose AFFECT, an auxiliary training objective for learning the distribution of visual changes induced by action perturbations. Specifically, we inject temporally correlated noise into the actions of a policy trained on task-agnostic human teleoperation. We then train the world model so that its generated videos respond to this noise as the recorded videos do, without requiring repeated executions from the same initial state. Across OGBench simulation and real-world DROID and ALOHA-2 setups, AFFECT makes world-model rollouts more faithful to real outcomes. On DROID, the Pearson correlation between policy success rates in the world model and on the real robot rises from 0.47 to 0.79, alongside up to 23% lower FVD. These gains carry over to planning, where selecting actions with AFFECT-trained world models improves task success by up to 8.3%.

ov.problema: I world models predicono le dinamiche ambientali sotto azioni, ma spesso non catturano come piccoli cambiamenti di azione influenzano le osservazioni future. Questo limita l'uso in valutazione di policy robotiche e pianificazione model-based, dove azioni quasi identiche possono portare a esiti qualitativamente diversi.
ov.idea: AFFECT è un obiettivo di training ausiliario che apprende la distribuzione dei cambiamenti visivi indotti da perturbazioni delle azioni. Iniettano rumore temporalmente correlato nelle azioni di una policy addestrata su teleoperazione umana task-agnostica, e addestrano il world model affinché i video generati rispondano al rumore come i video registrati, senza richiedere esecuzioni ripetute dallo stesso stato iniziale.
ov.risultati: Su OGBench (simulazione) e DROID e ALOHA-2 (reali), AFFECT rende i rollout più fedeli. Su DROID, la correlazione di Pearson tra tassi di successo della policy nel world model e sul robot reale sale da 0.47 a 0.79, con FVD fino al 23% inferiore. Nella pianificazione, migliora il successo fino all'8.3%.
ov.limiti: Non riportati esplicitamente nel testo.

glossario.d: Modello che predice le dinamiche future di un ambiente.
Fréchet Video Distance: metrica di similarità tra distribuzioni di video.
Strategia che mappa stati in azioni per un agente.

2611.26510.abs: Task success alone does not specify which behaviors post-training should reinforce. Even successful teacher trajectories can contain unsupported assumptions, unproductive repetition, or superficial verification. We propose Skill-FT (Skill-Guided Fine-Tuning), which uses natural-language skills to suppress undesirable habits and elicit underrepresented effective behaviors during teacher rollouts, then fine-tunes a target model on the resulting trajectories. We introduce AutoMaster, an autonomous post-training system in which an LLM agent develops these interventions through trajectory analysis, skill design, data selection, and feedback from rollouts and target-model evaluation. Across Terminal, Search, and software engineering tasks with 4B and 9B target models, AutoMaster improves mean performance over Vanilla SFT on successful unguided teacher trajectories by 1.42-8.99 percentage points, with the teacher, task pool, training set size, and SFT recipe held fixed. Together with the ablations and trajectory analyses, these results suggest that behavioral shaping can make a fixed model a more effective teacher. We further find that retaining skill instructions during SFT yields higher mean performance than removing them across all six settings, despite their absence at evaluation and identical supervised outputs. These findings suggest that preserving skill context as part of a training demonstration can support better behavioral internalization.

ov.problema: Il successo di un compito non specifica quali comportamenti rinforzare nel post-training. Anche traiettorie di teacher di successo possono contenere assunzioni non supportate, ripetizioni improduttive o verifiche superficiali.
ov.idea: Skill-FT usa skill in linguaggio naturale per sopprimere abitudini indesiderate e far emergere comportamenti efficaci sottorappresentati durante i rollout del teacher, poi fine-tuna il modello target su queste traiettorie. AutoMaster è un sistema autonomo in cui un agente LLM sviluppa questi interventi tramite analisi delle traiettorie, progettazione di skill, selezione dati e feedback da rollout e valutazione del target.
ov.risultati: Su task Terminal, Search e ingegneria del software con modelli target 4B e 9B, AutoMaster migliora la performance media rispetto a Vanilla SFT su traiettorie teacher non guidate di 1.42-8.99 punti percentuali, a parità di teacher, task pool, dimensione del training set e ricetta SFT. Mantenere le istruzioni delle skill durante SFT dà performance medie più alte rispetto a rimuoverle in tutte e sei le configurazioni.

glossario.d: Fine-tuning guidato da skill in linguaggio naturale per modellare comportamenti.
Supervised Fine-Tuning standard su traiettorie del teacher senza interventi.
Sequenza di azioni generate dal modello durante l'esecuzione di un task.

2611.23257.abs: Large language models have reduced the effort to generate code for interactive software with graphical user interfaces (GUIs). For such software, a key testing bottleneck is reaching a deep state, one that requires a long interaction history. The cost of reaching it recurs across commits, and the GUI automation that could amortize it assumes a DOM or accessibility tree that self-rendered engines do not expose. We introduce StatePortal, an agent that synthesizes a checkpoint, an artifact that restores that state and can be versioned and replayed, from a natural-language functional test case and read-only access to the target's source code. The checkpoint is restored through a per-application hook that an onboarding agent binds or synthesizes once without hand-written hook code. Because a checkpoint can satisfy state checks while rendering incorrectly, checkpoints are scored by hybrid programmatic-state and visual evaluation: acceptance requires both a programmatic-state oracle and a visual oracle to pass. We calibrate the visual oracle against a blinded cross-VLM reference. We release DeepStateBench, 61 deep-state tasks across 10 interactive applications that span five language families and six rendering stacks, with source sizes from 874 to 7.2M lines. Across three registered models, a GUI agent seeded with synthesized checkpoints completes 10.4% of trials, compared with 0% without seeding under the same pixel action space, while StatePortal, which also delivers the target action through the hook, completes 27.5%. Over 1,361 replays of 112 checkpoints, 98.90% reproduce the…

ov.problema: Testare software interattivo con GUI richiede di raggiungere stati profondi (che richiedono lunghe interazioni). Il costo si ripete a ogni commit e l'automazione GUI assume DOM o alberi di accessibilità che i motori self-rendered non espongono.
ov.idea: StatePortal è un agente che sintetizza un checkpoint (artefatto che ripristina lo stato, versionabile e riproducibile) da un test case in linguaggio naturale e accesso read-only al codice sorgente. Il checkpoint viene ripristinato tramite un hook per applicazione, legato o sintetizzato una volta da un agente di onboarding. I checkpoint sono valutati con oracoli programmatici e visivi.
ov.risultati: Su DeepStateBench (61 task deep-state, 10 applicazioni, 5 famiglie linguistiche, 6 stack di rendering, da 874 a 7.2M righe), un agente GUI con checkpoint sintetizzati completa il 10.4% dei trial, contro 0% senza seeding. StatePortal, che fornisce anche l'azione target, ottiene risultati migliori (testo troncato).
ov.limiti: Il testo è troncato e non riporta il tasso di successo completo di StatePortal né altri limiti.

glossario.d: Artefatto che ripristina uno stato profondo di un'applicazione.
Document Object Model: struttura ad albero di una pagina web.
Vision Language Model: modello che elabora immagini e testo.

2611.26408.abs: It has been demonstrated that, in certain settings, large language models can perform weight-space programming to directly modify the weights of neural networks. However, it is unknown how dedicated training of these networks can contribute to the successes of weight-space programming. We present a benchmark of LLM-driven weight-space programming on vision models, in which five LLMs edit convolutional networks and vision transformers on relabeling and error-correction tasks on Waterbirds, CIFAR-100, PACS and Entity-30. We report more than 2,600 such edit processes, whereby each edit is scored on held-out images for success, side effects and accuracy loss. We compare standard training with label smoothing, gradient-based editable training, and our Edit-Ready Training (ERT), a novel method that rehearses the direct, closed-form weight edits LLMs perform. We show that preparing networks for editing raises the success of LLM edits substantially where standard networks are hard to edit. ERT further achieves the highest mean score for GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5.5 across all evaluated baselines. We will release our LLM testing framework alongside all tasks, editing trajectories and scores. Project page: https://viscom.uni-ulm.de/wsp

ov.problema: I large language models (LLM) possono modificare direttamente i pesi di reti neurali (weight-space programming), ma non è chiaro come addestrare le reti per facilitare queste modifiche.
ov.idea: Gli autori presentano un benchmark di weight-space programming su modelli di visione, dove cinque LLM modificano reti convoluzionali e transformer per compiti di rietichettatura e correzione errori. Confrontano addestramento standard, label smoothing, addestramento editabile basato su gradienti e il loro metodo Edit-Ready Training (ERT), che simula le modifiche dirette in forma chiusa che gli LLM eseguono.
ov.risultati: ERT aumenta sostanzialmente il successo delle modifiche LLM dove le reti standard sono difficili da editare. ERT ottiene il punteggio medio più alto per GPT-6 Astra e Claude Opus 5.5 su tutti i baseline valutati.
ov.limiti: Il benchmark è limitato a modelli di visione e a specifici compiti; non è detto che i risultati si trasferiscano ad altri domini.

glossario.d: Modifica diretta dei pesi di una rete neurale tramite LLM.
Tecnica di regolarizzazione che assegna probabilità non nulle a classi errate.
Metodo che addestra la rete a subire modifiche dirette dei pesi da parte di LLM.

2611.17460.abs: AI agents are increasingly equipped with persistence toward task completion to run delegated work autonomously for long periods, under many unstated constraints from internal documents and other people's authority. When completion requires violating a rule, the agent must decide alone, yet benchmarks of instruction-rule conflicts state the rule in the prompt or keep it hidden and do not evaluate persistence. We present Unfinished-Bench, a benchmark that gives models persistence in autonomous runs without a user, in realistic work environments with embedded rules. In each of its 97 scenarios across 7 organizations and 7 risk categories, the goal and the rule cannot both hold. We find that persistence raised violations of a rule in an internal document from 32.2% to 43.6%, five times the 8.5% for the same rule stated by the user. Of the document-rule violations, 98.3% occurred after the rule was displayed, and in 89% of a judged sample the agent first wrote down the rule. Violations of rules placed in the environment without user oversight can lead to serious incidents, so persistence-driven risks need to be evaluated. Benchmark documentation: https://francis21c.github.io/unfinished-bench/

ov.problema: Gli agenti AI con persistenza verso il completamento del task operano a lungo in autonomia, sotto vincoli non dichiarati da documenti interni e autorità. Quando completare richiede violare una regola, l'agente decide da solo, ma i benchmark esistenti non valutano la persistenza.
ov.idea: Unfinished-Bench dà persistenza ai modelli in esecuzioni autonome senza utente, in ambienti lavorativi realistici con regole incorporate. In ognuno dei 97 scenari (7 organizzazioni, 7 categorie di rischio), obiettivo e regola non possono coesistere.
ov.risultati: La persistenza aumenta le violazioni di una regola in un documento interno dal 32.2% al 43.6%, cinque volte l'8.5% per la stessa regola dichiarata dall'utente. Il 98.3% delle violazioni di regole documentali avviene dopo che la regola è stata mostrata, e nell'89% di un campione giudicato l'agente prima scrive la regola.

glossario.d: Tendenza dell'agente a continuare fino al completamento del task in autonomia.
Vincolo presente in documenti o ambiente, non dichiarato esplicitamente nel prompt.
Situazione simulata in cui obiettivo e regola sono in conflitto.

2611.26286.abs: Peer review relies on several readers finding different problems. We measure critique overlap in conference and journal reviews. At ICLR, measured overlap rose from 12.0% in 2026 to 21.3% in 2027, in reviews from the same stage of the review process, with year-on-year rises at NeurIPS, ICML and the F1000 and PLOS journals. A third ICLR review of a paper added 5.46 new problems to the other two in 2027, against 6.12 in 2026. We apply MELD, a detector of LLM-generated text, to all reviews. Within a paper, two reviews that MELD flags overlap more than two unflagged reviews: by 3.0 points at ICLR in 2024-2025, by 4.5 points in 2026-2027, and by 5.4 points across five journal sources. These results provide evidence that LLM-flagged reviews of one paper are less distinct from each other than unflagged reviews, and suggest that the diversity of critiques among reviews of a single paper is falling.

ov.problema: La peer review funziona se revisori diversi trovano problemi diversi, ma i testi generati da LLM potrebbero ridurre questa diversità di critiche.
ov.idea: Gli autori misurano la sovrapposizione tra critiche a livello di singola affermazione in recensioni di conferenze e riviste, e applicano MELD, un rilevatore di testo generato da LLM, per confrontare recensioni segnalate e non segnalate.
ov.risultati: A ICLR la sovrapposizione è salita dal 12,0% nel 2026 al 21,3% nel 2027; una terza recensione aggiunge 5,46 nuovi problemi nel 2027 contro 6,12 nel 2026. Le recensioni segnalate da MELD si sovrappongono di più: +3,0 punti a ICLR 2024-2025, +4,5 nel 2026-2027, +5,4 su cinque riviste.
ov.limiti: MELD è un rilevatore e la correlazione non prova causalità; i risultati mostrano associazione tra flag LLM e maggiore sovrapposizione.

glossario.d: Rilevatore di testo generato da LLM usato per etichettare le recensioni.
Misura quanto due recensioni sollevano le stesse critiche specifiche.

2611.08136.abs: Anomaly detection (AD) is often framed as a representation-learning problem, where strong performance is expected to require learned features or AD-specific optimization. However, this view can overlook the intrinsic separability of anomalies from normal references, even in the absence of learned representations. We therefore investigate how far untrained neural networks can go in anomaly detection. To this end, we propose PRISM, a framework combining fixed random nonlinear features with normal-reference Mahalanobis scoring for tabular detection and dense visual localization. Across 47 tabular datasets in ADBench, PRISM-T achieves the highest mean AUROC (86.4%) and the second-highest mean AUPRC (65.9%) among the compared methods. On MVTec AD and VisA, covering 27 visual categories, PRISM-V achieves mean image-level and pixel-level AUROCs of 90.4% and 96.4%, respectively. Notably, both models achieve these results without neural weight optimization or pretrained representations. A theoretical analysis further characterizes how nonlinear transformations affect the mean and covariance contributions to the Mahalanobis score gap, while empirical analyses examine the resulting score separability. These findings establish PRISM as both a competitive anomaly detector and a prior-to-learning baseline for assessing the added value of learned representations in anomaly detection.

ov.problema: L'anomaly detection è spesso vista come un problema di rappresentazione appresa, ma non è chiaro quanto servano davvero feature apprese o ottimizzazione specifica.
ov.idea: PRISM combina feature non lineari fisse e casuali con uno scoring di Mahalanobis basato su riferimenti normali, per dati tabellari e localizzazione visiva densa, senza ottimizzare pesi neurali né usare rappresentazioni pre-addestrate.
ov.risultati: Su 47 dataset tabellari di ADBench, PRISM-T ottiene il miglior AUROC medio (86,4%) e il secondo miglior AUPRC medio (65,9%). Su MVTec AD e VisA (27 categorie) PRISM-V raggiunge AUROC medi di 90,4% a livello immagine e 96,4% a livello pixel.
ov.limiti: I risultati dipendono dalla separabilità intrinseca delle anomalie e dallo scoring con riferimenti normali; non è garantito su domini con anomalie poco separabili.

glossario.d: Distanza che tiene conto della covarianza dei dati, usata per misurare quanto un punto è anomalo.
Area sotto la curva ROC: misura la capacità di distinguere anomalie da normali.
Area sotto la curva precision-recall, utile con classi molto sbilanciate.

2611.16933.abs: Full-duplex spoken dialogue models learn turn-taking, overlaps and backchannels from conversations recorded with one channel per speaker, but most available conversational audio is a single mono mix. We present Kezek, a model that turns a mono recording of exactly two people into one track per person with the original length and timing; overlaps and short replies ("yeah", "mm-hm") stay on the track of the person who said them. Kezek decides who speaks when and who is who once for the whole recording (stage 1: a two-voice activity model guided by a speaker fingerprint trained to be insensitive to phase), and a conditioned time-domain separator only carries out that decision (stage 2), with outputs that always sum to the input. Standard separation metrics miss the failures that matter for dialogue data, so we report short-reply retention, leakage onto the other person's solo, channel swaps and coverage. Against the open pipeline pyannote -> DialogueSidon on the same recordings, Kezek keeps more short replies (0.83 vs. 0.69 on Open Yap test; 0.80 vs. 0.71 over the other's speech on unseen telephone speech from CallHome English), mostly because it returns the whole recording while the external pipeline drops part of it (on the audio both return, reply retention is about the same: 0.859 vs. 0.865 on Open Yap); it also leaks less, swaps channels less often, and runs 4-5 times faster (about 230 hours of audio per GPU-hour). We also report negative results and an ideal-mask ceiling that locate the remaining gap: quiet replies under a louder voice. Code and weights are released…

2611.24059.abs: Frontier post-training follows a common recipe: train one expert per domain with reinforcement learning (RL), then consolidate the experts into one model via multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD). Such consolidation is expensive: the student samples in every environment again, an expert scores every sampled token, and the student inherits the drift of the final experts. Yet we argue that the experts' RL runs have already produced what consolidation needs: rollouts with their sampling probabilities and rewards, in the order the experts learned from them. We propose multi-expert replay policy distillation (MRPD), which replays these training logs through the student in the experts' order. At each step, the policy gradient is recomputed on these scored trajectories, and the final experts' distributions are distilled at the logged prefixes. Following the experts' own trajectory reduces the training-inference mismatch and keeps the student within the clip range, so the replay is off-policy in origin but quasi-on-policy throughout consolidation. MRPD samples nothing and calls no environment or reward model: the trainer is the sole process, and consolidating the experts costs only about a seventh of the compute used to train them. On three long-horizon agentic domains (reasoning, search and SQL), MRPD yields the best student model, substantially outperforming online RL baselines, and surpassing MOPD from the same experts at a fraction of MOPD's cost. Our analysis on the same logs shows that the replayed trajectories carry most of the gain, and that both the policy gradient…

ov.problema: La ricetta comune per unire esperti di dominio addestrati con RL è la distillazione multi-teacher on-policy (MOPD), costosa: lo studente ricampiona in ogni ambiente, ogni esperto valuta ogni token e lo studente eredita la deriva degli esperti finali.
ov.idea: MRPD riusa i log di addestramento RL degli esperti: li riproduce attraverso lo studente nell'ordine in cui gli esperti li hanno appresi, ricalcolando il gradiente di policy su traiettorie già valutate e distillando le distribuzioni degli esperti finali ai prefissi registrati. Così il replay è off-policy all'origine ma quasi on-policy durante il consolidamento, senza campionare né chiamare ambienti o reward model.
ov.risultati: Su tre domini agentici long-horizon (reasoning, search, SQL) MRPD produce il miglior studente, supera sostanzialmente i baseline di RL online e batte MOPD dagli stessi esperti a una frazione del costo; consolidare gli esperti costa circa un settimo del calcolo usato per addestrarli.
ov.limiti: Il testo si interrompe nell'analisi finale, quindi i dettagli di quella analisi non sono riportati.

glossario.d: On-policy: dati generati dal modello corrente; off-policy: dati generati da un'altra policy.
Addestrare uno studente a imitare le distribuzioni di output di uno o più insegnanti.
Traiettoria di azioni e ricompense raccolta eseguendo una policy.

2611.24917.abs: In this paper, we propose a Unified Law for Visual Tasks, which could be further divided into Four Laws of Computer Vision, with the goal of enabling a single framework or method to uniformly train on and perform nearly all visual tasks. Our starting point is an inspiration and hypothesis: if the world information is encoded into image, which we call World Snapshots, then image processing is world processing, and image generation is World Snapshot generation. Furthermore, if all visual and visualization tasks can be reformulated as generation tasks, then a unified method, World Snapshot Models (WSMs), can perform the vast majority of visual tasks, much as large language models have largely unified natural language processing. This paper validates these laws across more than 1,000 trained and evaluated visual tasks (defined by distinct input-output mappings) and presents a unified training framework for future visual-task research and applications.

2611.24844.abs: Language models acquire their capabilities from training data, and developers withhold data during training to keep models from learning capabilities that could be misused. How long this delays a capability, and how much data is needed to acquire it later, is unknown. Here we show that the general progress a model makes on the rest of its training data substitutes for the data that was withheld. We withheld the training signal for individual skills in models of chess, Othello, molecular strings, bracket languages and web text. The delay of a withheld skill in larger models was predicted from smaller ones. A chess model never explicitly trained to respond to check ranked the legal responses almost as well as a model that was. When models were then trained on the withheld data, they acquired the skill with a small fraction of the data needed from initialization, and this fraction decreased as the models progressed. A control rule of equal difficulty was learned much more slowly. A programming language withheld from the training text of a 7-billion-parameter model was regained in the same way. Data filtering therefore delays a capability, and the data required to regain it decreases as models improve.

ov.problema: I sviluppatori nascondono dati durante l'addestramento per evitare che i modelli apprendano capacità pericolose. Non si sa quanto questo ritardi una capacità e quanti dati servano per acquisirla dopo.
ov.idea: Gli autori mostrano che il progresso generale del modello sul resto dei dati sostituisce il segnale mancante. Hanno nascosto il segnale per singole abilità in modelli di scacchi, Othello, stringhe molecolari, linguaggi a parentesi e testo web. Il ritardo in modelli grandi è predetto da modelli piccoli.
ov.risultati: Un modello di scacchi mai addestrato a rispondere allo scacco ha classificato le risposte legali quasi come un modello addestrato. Dopo l'addestramento sui dati nascosti, l'abilità è acquisita con una piccola frazione dei dati necessari da zero, frazione che diminuisce col progredire del modello. Un linguaggio di programmazione nascosto in un modello da 7 miliardi di parametri è stato recuperato allo stesso modo.
ov.limiti: Una regola di controllo di uguale difficoltà è stata appresa molto più lentamente.

glossario.d: Dati ed etichette usati per insegnare una capacità al modello.
Gioco da tavolo usato come ambiente di test per capacità apprese.
Rete neurale di grandi dimensioni con 7 miliardi di pesi.

2611.26627.abs: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training substantially improves the visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy of diffusion transformers. Because capabilities such as rendering requested text or composing multiple objects are inherently prompt-dependent, a natural hypothesis is that improving them requires learning complex, input-dependent transformations. To isolate how much of these gains an input-independent shift explains, we probe each RL-tuned model with a deliberately simple parameterization: a fixed set of steering vectors added to the block outputs of the frozen base model. On SD3.5-M, these vectors hold 65x fewer parameters than the RL-tuned LoRA (0.29M against 18.8M). We fit them to match the velocity predictions of public RL-tuned checkpoints, with no reward in the objective. Although the vectors are identical for every prompt, token, and sampling seed, they recover 90.0-96.3% of the reward gains of six RL-tuned image models, and 89.8% and 111.9% on two RL-tuned video models. Initialized at zero and trained with online RL, the vectors alone exceed the reward gains of weight-based RL on text rendering (OCR) and human preference (PickScore) on SD3.5-M. A constant shift thus suffices for most of the gain of policy-gradient RL post-training: without new input-dependent transformations, it steers the pretrained generator toward what it can already compute.

ov.problema: Il post-training con RL migliora i diffusion transformer, ma non è chiaro quanto i guadagni dipendano da trasformazioni complesse dipendenti dal prompt rispetto a un semplice spostamento costante.
ov.idea: Gli autori aggiungono vettori di steering fissi (identici per ogni prompt, token e seed) agli output dei blocchi del modello base congelato, addestrandoli per imitare le predizioni di checkpoint RL-tuned pubblici, senza reward nell'obiettivo.
ov.risultati: Su SD3.5-M i vettori hanno 65x meno parametri della LoRA RL-tuned (0.29M contro 18.8M) e recuperano il 90.0-96.3% dei guadagni di reward di sei modelli immagine RL-tuned, e 89.8% e 111.9% su due modelli video; inizializzati a zero e addestrati con RL online, superano i guadagni di RL basato su pesi su OCR e PickScore.
ov.limiti: Il metodo è testato solo su modelli e task specifici; non è chiaro se un semplice spostamento costante basti per capacità che richiedono trasformazioni dipendenti dall'input.

glossario.d: Modello generativo che usa transformer per denoising iterativo di immagini o video.
Vettori fissi aggiunti agli output per modificare il comportamento del modello.
Tecnica di fine-tuning che aggiunge pochi parametri addestrabili ai pesi congelati.

2611.26619.abs: Hybrid architectures have become mainstream among open-weight language models. Their global-attention and bounded-state layers maintain heterogeneous caches whose demands vary with context length and concurrency. We present TideCache, a serving system on CPU--GPU superchips with three components for allocating GPU memory among caches and managing their residency across GPU and host memory. The Transparent Cache Pool redistributes physical pages among cache components behind fixed virtual addresses, preserving cache layouts and backend interfaces. The Cache Streamer uses computation intervals provided by bounded-state layers to prefetch the next global-attention layer's prefix into GPU slots shared across global-attention layers, reducing GPU residency while overlapping layer-wise transfers with computation. Generated KV remains resident. The Request Scheduler selects resident or streamed execution and triggers capacity adjustments according to request size and queue state. Together, they let HBM released by streaming accommodate other cache components and additional requests. Implemented in SGLang and evaluated on GB300 and GH200 across seven model/platform configurations, TideCache completes up to 2.04x as many agent turns, reduces overall P50 per-token latency by 20--59%, and improves agent P50 TTFT by 1.40--3.05x compared with SGLang with HiCache.

2611.26615.abs: High-resolution generation enables video world models to render fine-grained scene structures and textures, but directly generating high-resolution video incurs substantial computational and memory costs. We present ScaleWorld, a causal video model that unifies low-resolution world prediction and high-resolution refinement within a single shared backbone. By refining its own predictions, ScaleWorld produces high-resolution world videos without requiring a separate refinement model. For each video chunk, the shared backbone first completes a low-resolution prediction and then performs one-step high-resolution refinement conditioned on that prediction. To support efficient streaming generation, we maintain separate causal states with a long low-resolution history for prediction and a short high-resolution history for refinement. To address task interference during distillation, we separate specialist optimization from capability consolidation and introduce task-asymmetric on-policy distillation (TA-OPD). This procedure transfers prediction and refinement behaviors from specialized teachers into a shared student through local velocity matching under their respective sampling and history policies. {Extensive experiments demonstrate that ScaleWorld achieves high-quality world generation with improved computational and memory efficiency.

2611.26613.abs: Frontier multimodal language agents such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated strong capabilities in controlling robots directly via low-level numerical actions without high-level primitives. However, existing benchmarks report only episode-level success rates, which show neither how these agents succeed nor where they fail. In this paper, we present a systematic action-level analysis of frontier agents on direct robot control across 12 manipulation benchmarks. We introduce AgentRoboCritic, an intent-grounded critique framework in which the policy agent states a local intent alongside each action, and a critic evaluates the action's outcome and failure mode against this intent. Our action-level analysis demonstrates the promising capabilities of frontier agents on direct robot control, including closed-loop recovery from local execution failures, reliable semantic grounding across diverse scenes, and strong zero-shot manipulation without task-specific adaptation. It also identifies their current limitations, including task-relevant physical execution bottlenecks such as grasping and alignment, and uneven recovery across failure modes. Finally, we validate our critic on a 400-action human-annotated benchmark and release a dataset of 12,844 annotated actions alongside a fine-tuned open-source critic, Muse-Glimmer-30B, whose failure-mode accuracy rises from 32.58% to 74.24%, enabling low-cost action-level analysis.

2611.26584.abs: Does post-training change what a language model represents, or how this representation is read out into an answer? We compared linear probes with the models' own answers, analyzed with signal detection theory, in six open-weight base models and their post-trained versions. For judgments of whether German texts were written by a human or an AI, probes and word n-gram classifiers separated the classes well, but the answers did not and often ordered the texts inversely. Post-training lowered the sensitivity of the answers on average ($Δd' = -0.34$ across model families; -0.29 across three prompts). It also changed the use of a stated base rate: Base models shifted their log-odds by less than the stated change in prior odds, most post-trained models by more. In two models with stage-wise checkpoints, the change occurred during supervised fine-tuning, model stitching implicated the early layers, and from mid-depth on internal states at positions after the text, not those of the text, transferred the change between checkpoints. Our corpora cannot be shared, so we add a case reproducible from public data, the truth of negated statements. Here, post-training acted in the opposite direction: Probes decoded truth at or near ceiling in every model, the answers of several base models did not use it, and post-training repaired them; by mid-depth the repair resided at the positions after the statement; below it, the representation of the statement contributed, strongly in one of four models. In a training study, adding 2,000 correctly labeled authorship judgments of news texts to…

2611.26553.abs: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause. Incident catalogs collect these reports, and benchmarks record whether agents fail, but neither replicates an incident nor tests the cause its report might identify. In this paper, we present ROGUE-AI (Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation), a multi-agent framework that closes the above gap and rebuilds each reported incident offline together with a matched control that lacks only the blamed cause, and runs agents on both. Our results suggest that ROGUE-AI is able to reproduce the reported harm in 89% of its 108 attempted replications. Agents built on five current GPT, Claude, Gemini and DeepSeek models made the reported mistake in 18% to 33% of runs, against at most 1% without the blamed cause. Of the 72 incidents with real-world harm, 62 had no underlying attacker, and in these, agents did what their task asked for but missed an ordinary hazard, such as a database shared with the live site. Replications without an attacker caused more harm than replications of prompt injection for all five models. Defenses against prompt injection look for injected instructions, but these replications contain none. Further, a warning after each tool output that names the hazard and its consequence lowered harm for all five…

2611.26540.abs: Current audio-driven video diffusion models can synthesize realistic talking-head videos but generally require dozens of diffusion denoising steps over multi-second video chunks, making them unsuitable for streaming applications such as voice assistants and virtual avatars, where low-latency and online causal generation are required properties. AURA generates video chunk by chunk with a rolling KV cache, requiring only the audio of the current chunk to start generating, rather than a multi-second audio look-ahead like bidirectional models. It comes in two sizes: AURA 1.3B streams 576p video in real time on a single GPU (20.7 fps for a 16 Hz playback rate), making it suited to interactive avatar applications, and AURA 5B streams 720p video at 9.7 fps. Our two-stage distillation pipeline first aligns the causal student with the teacher, by training it to match the teacher's trajectories with fewer diffusion steps and a chunk-wise sliding window causal attention mask, then applies Distribution Matching Distillation (DMD) with backward simulation to close the remaining quality gap. On standard talking-head benchmarks, AURA 1.3B runs 23x faster than its own bidirectional teacher and reaches a quality comparable to TalkVerse at a lower resolution, and AURA 5B matches its TalkVerse teacher at 720p while running 17x faster. To support reproducibility and further research on streaming avatar generation, we release the weights of both models along with a dataset of 30K synthetic videos and their precomputed teacher trajectories.

2611.26519.abs: Reliable reasoning for long-horizon embodied tasks requires predictions grounded in the observed execution state. We present ACE-Brain-0.7, a 9B vision--language model that combines spatial grounding, task understanding, and progress estimation. To train the model, we curate 3.7 million question--answer pairs, drawing execution supervision from egocentric human videos, robot episodes, and simulation. These questions span different stages of an execution and connect task-level judgments with observed progress and outcomes. We then fine-tune Qwen3.5-9B on this collection together with additional task, spatial-grounding, and progress-estimation data. Across six public task-reasoning benchmarks, ACE-Brain-0.7 achieves an average score of 76.5, ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 72.7 and Claude Opus 5.5 at 73.5. Our model also leads the evaluated models in spatial grounding, averaging 75.90 across seven benchmarks and reaching 91.25 Acc@0.5 on RefCOCOg. Controlled evaluations further indicate that our task-only model makes more effective use of visual history and more accurately distinguishes execution states. Together, these results show that ACE-Brain-0.7 effectively combines spatial perception with temporal understanding, delivering strong execution-grounded reasoning and comparing favorably with closed-source models.

2611.26514.abs: Retrieving government schemes requires matching citizens' information needs to formal administrative descriptions, often across languages and terminology. We present a bilingual search system for Maharashtra government schemes and public services that combines BM25 retrieval with sentence-embedding similarity through equal-weight score fusion. The system indexes aligned English-Marathi scheme descriptions and supports multilingual, Marathi-focused, and translation-mediated semantic configurations. Evaluation on manually curated bilingual queries compares BM25, dense retrieval, and hybrid retrieval using IndicSBERT and MahaSBERT. BM25 provides a strong baseline with a mean reciprocal rank (MRR) of 0.864. Hybrid retrieval increases MRR to 0.872 with IndicSBERT and 0.879 with MahaSBERT, whereas the corresponding dense-only systems achieve 0.663 and 0.655. MahaSBERT-based fusion also increases precision from 0.781 to 0.808 while matching BM25 recall at 0.946. These results support the complementary use of lexical and semantic signals in this collection, while showing that improvements over a strong lexical baseline are modest and metric-dependent. The study provides an application-focused analysis of hybrid retrieval for bilingual public-service information access.

2611.26509.abs: Decision models enable fast, confidence-aware decisions by scoring candidate answers in a single forward pass, without generating text or intermediate reasoning. Yet reasoning can substantially improve decision quality, raising the question of whether its benefits can be retained without the cost of generating it. We investigate this question with \textbf{GLiDE}, a family of decision models spanning 0.4B to 27B parameters. Building on Qwen hybrid language models, GLiDE enables bidirectional interactions between the context, question, and candidate answers by removing causal masking from full-attention layers. To transfer reasoning capabilities into single-pass inference, we combine soft-target distillation from multiple teachers, including a reasoning model, with progressive post-training on diverse decision tasks. We further explore parameter-free recurrent depth to increase inference-time computation without generating tokens. Across five model sizes, GLiDE lies on the performance--parameter Pareto frontier of the Hugging Face \DI{}, with each model outperforming evaluated alternatives of equal or smaller size. \dmtwo{} (27B) achieves a hidden-set score of 71.52, with an expected calibration error of 2.0\% and a median latency of 92.9\,ms on a single GPU. Further checkpoint averaging and parameter-free recurrent depth yield GLiDE~27B, which reaches 73.37 with an expected calibration error of 2.1\%.

2611.26492.abs: Rad-Linter checks chest X-ray reports against image-derived evidence to flag potential errors for review. A pretrained image classifier supplies scores for nine pathologies, and a 1.5B-parameter language model, fine-tuned with LoRA on 1,816 examples, checks their consistency with the report. We compare it with a keyword-and-negation rule baseline given the same reports and scores. Evaluation uses controlled report-score pairings from OpenI, with consistency labels derived from automatic report labels and score thresholds. Each counterfactual quad crosses two real reports with two real score vectors from other patients, creating two consistent and two inconsistent pairs. Every report and score vector occurs in both conditions, so either input alone permits only 50% accuracy. On 131 quads, Rad-Linter achieves 98.5% pair accuracy versus 80.5% for the rule baseline, and classifies all four pairs correctly in 94.4% of quads versus 56.5%. The checkers perform similarly on omission items, including unmentioned and negated findings; larger differences occur on the remaining item types, which require interpreting how findings are described. The same language model without fine-tuning remains near 50% accuracy. On a second set of 181 quads that also includes reports on which the automatic labelers disagree, pair accuracy is 93.4% versus 75.3%. These controlled results show that, given the same image-derived scores, a trained language model detects report-score inconsistencies more accurately than the tested rule baseline, with the advantage concentrated in interpreting how findings…

2611.26407.abs: Flow matching is a versatile framework for generative modeling that transports a source distribution to a target data distribution. A key advantage is its flexibility in the choice of source distribution, such as heavy-tailed and multimodal sources. Yet finite-step sampling guarantees for non-Gaussian sources remain limited. We establish a nonasymptotic convergence theory for Euler discretization of flow matching with linear interpolation. Suppose the source distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ has an everywhere positive, continuously differentiable density, finite total variance $\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}$, and an $L$-Lipschitz score. Using the population velocity field and a suitable time grid, this sampler achieves total variation error at most $\varepsilon$ in $\widetilde{O}(Ld\mathsf{TotVar}_{\mathsf{base}}/\varepsilon)$ iterations, provided the target distribution satisfies a mild second-moment condition. These assumptions cover, among many examples, source distributions such as multivariate Student's $t$ distributions with more than two degrees of freedom and finite Gaussian mixtures with shared covariance, while accommodating target distributions with neither a smooth density nor bounded support.

2611.26179.abs: Images under non-uniform coupled degradations require diverse restoration capabilities for different degraded regions. Existing methods employ globally uniform operations, potentially overlooking regional differences and causing incomplete restoration or even damage to image content. Moreover, a degraded region may require successive restoration actions, and earlier actions may alter residual degradation characteristics or introduce artifacts, potentially hindering subsequent restoration. To address these challenges, we propose RegionAgent, an adaptive restoration framework that trains a Vision-Language Model (VLM) through two-stage preference learning to generate a region-specific restoration action at each iteration. Specifically, we first train the VLM to select an action suited to the current region through step-level Direct Preference Optimization (DPO), using preferences derived from immediate restoration feedback to supervise only the differing component in each action pair. To account for the effects of current actions on subsequent restoration, we then apply trajectory-level DPO, using preferences derived from complete trajectory scores to supervise the sole differing action in each trajectory pair. Furthermore, as conventional image-pair datasets do not directly provide preferences over regional restoration decisions, we construct a regional restoration preference dataset comprising 10K action pairs and 20K trajectory pairs for two-stage VLM training. Experiments across multiple datasets demonstrate strong restoration performance under both mixed and single…

2611.26033.abs: Camera-equipped glasses can convert an examination page into a query to a vision-language model (VLM). Device detection addresses possession; a complementary question is whether an examination document can reduce the usefulness of an unauthorized capture. We present SEOYUN, an application-specific framework for refusal-inducing exam documents, with optical and encoder-level interventions as extensions. We use reverse jailbreaking to describe the direction of the objective: inducing abstention rather than bypassing refusal. Refusal induction and defensive visual prompt injection already have precedents; our contribution is a threat model, analytical limits, and an evaluation protocol for examination use. We distinguish refusal from correct-answer leakage, show why removing an added dummy option is not itself a reduction in the original answer space, and derive a sampling comparison under explicitly stated camera assumptions. The protocol separates digital, simulated, and physical inputs and requires held-out evaluation after subject-specific selection. A local CSAT candidate corpus and rendering harness have been prepared, but this version reports no model-performance measurements, physical validation, or human-subject results. Accordingly, SEOYUN is a research framework, not a validated defense or a basis for allegations against individuals.

2611.26298.abs: As multimodal large language models (MLLMs) become increasingly integrated into everyday life, their ability to provide safe and reliable assistance in realistic daily activities remains insufficiently explored. Existing safety benchmarks primarily focus on isolated harmful requests or adversarial scenarios, overlooking the safety risks that may arise as ordinary tasks unfold. In practice, users pursue legitimate goals through multi-turn, multimodal interactions, where seemingly benign requests may become safety-critical when considered alongside earlier actions and visual observations. This calls for Dynamic Safety Awareness, the ability to track evolving task conditions, recognize implicit contextual risks, and provide safe and helpful assistance. To systematically evaluate this capability, we introduce DailySafe, a benchmark comprising 195 naturalistic multi-turn, multi-image interactions across 10 everyday domains and 42 task categories. Grounded in authentic user dialogue topics and documented safety knowledge, DailySafe captures realistic scenarios where safety-critical evidence is progressively revealed across conversational turns and visual observations. Using case-specific safety annotations, DailySafe assesses whether MLLMs can recognize and appropriately address evolving risks while supporting users' legitimate goals, bringing multimodal safety evaluation closer to real-world everyday AI assistance. DailySafe is publicly available at: https://github.com/XuankunRong/DailySafe.

ov.problema: I modelli multimodali (MLLM) sono sempre più integrati nella vita quotidiana, ma la loro capacità di fornire assistenza sicura e affidabile in attività realistiche è poco esplorata. I benchmark di sicurezza esistenti si concentrano su richieste dannose isolate o scenari adversarial, trascurando i rischi che emergono mentre compiti ordinari si svolgono in interazioni multi-turno e multimodali.
ov.idea: DailySafe è un benchmark con 195 interazioni naturalistiche multi-turno e multi-immagine in 10 domini quotidiani e 42 categorie di task. Basato su argomenti autentici di dialoghi utente e conoscenze di sicurezza documentate, cattura scenari realistici in cui prove critiche per la sicurezza emergono progressivamente tra turni conversazionali e osservazioni visive. Usa annotazioni di sicurezza caso-specifiche per valutare se gli MLLM riconoscono e affrontano rischi in evoluzione supportando gli obiettivi legittimi dell'utente.
ov.risultati: Il benchmark comprende 195 interazioni multi-turno e multi-immagine, 10 domini quotidiani e 42 categorie di task. È pubblicamente disponibile su GitHub.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta limiti espliciti; la valutazione è limitata a 195 interazioni e 10 domini.

glossario.d: Multimodal Large Language Model: modello linguistico che elabora anche immagini o altri input.
Interazione conversazionale composta da più scambi successivi tra utente e modello.
Input progettati malevolmente per indurre il modello a comportamenti indesiderati.

2611.26569.abs: Multimodal image generation systems have made rapid progress and increasingly emphasize content safety. However, their safety mechanisms tend to rely on a single modality and lack joint consideration of both visual content and text prompts, particularly in instruction-guided image editing, where the uploaded image may itself carry risk. We thus introduce EditSafetyBench, a benchmark that measures system-level safety awareness of advanced image editing systems, containing 5,940 image-instruction pairs, covering safe and unsafe images across 11 risk categories and three edit intents. We then probe the benchmark dataset on four systems, including Gemini, GPT, Qwen API, and Qwen Local. Based on our evaluation, we observe a systematic text-vision safety mismatch: Gemini and GPT refuse 87.1\% and 81.6\% cases containing unsafe-intent editing prompts, while only refusing 24.2\% and 22.4\% cases with both unsafe images and neutral instructions. At the category level, most risks are considered inconsistently by different systems, e.g., GPT allows 70.4\% editing attempts of unsafe political content while Gemini only allows 34.8\%. Notably, sexual content shows the strongest visual sensitivity, likely benefiting from mature NSFW identification works. Our findings highlight the need for safety guardrails that jointly reason over both visual and textual modalities in image editing systems.

2611.26607.abs: Collecting and labeling inertial measurement unit (IMU) data for human activity recognition (HAR) is expensive, and models trained on one group of subjects often fail to generalize to unseen individuals. Even with balanced data, classifiers struggle to distinguish dynamically similar activity classes and benefit from targeted augmentation. We explore whether synthetic IMU data generated in the representation space of a pretrained biosignal encoder, Bio-PM \cite{b1}, can serve as a practical augmentation source. Rather than synthesizing raw signals, we leverage Bio-PM's frozen encoder to convert 10-second IMU windows into token embedding sequences and train class-conditional decoders in this space: (1) an autoregressive transformer decoder that predicts tokens sequentially, and (2) a diffusion decoder that learns the token distribution through a denoising objective. We analyze generation realism through distributional metrics and embedding-space visualizations, evaluate downstream utility through leave-one-subject-out HAR classification, and present a PatchDecoder for approximate raw waveform reconstruction. Our diffusion decoder achieves a Train-on-Synthetic-Test-on-Real (TSTR) macro-F1 of 0.68, demonstrating that generated tokens are realistic enough to train a classifier that transfers to real data. Combining synthetic-token augmentation with a 320-dimensional gravity-aware feature representation raises LOSO macro-F1 from 0.729 to 0.809 over a real-only baseline across 51 subjects on the WISDM benchmark, with statistically significant gains concentrated in the most…

2611.26596.abs: Robotic vision-language-action (VLA) models can execute diverse individual manipulation skills, yet they still struggle with long-horizon loco-manipulation tasks, where temporal structure, skills, and precision are tightly coupled within a monolithic model. We propose Physically Grounded Execution (PGX), a framework that offloads temporal and precision control to two classical training-free components, allowing the VLA to focus on stage-specific skill dynamics. PGX decomposes long-horizon loco-manipulation into three layers: (i) a predicate-based state machine governs task progression, using physical predicates to gate phase transitions, trigger recovery, and coordinate navigation and waiting. Shared predicate semantics connect offline demonstration segmentation, online execution, and stage-wise evaluation; (ii) VLA skills operate within active manipulation phases, with flat or stage-trained models concentrating on task-relevant actions; and (iii) world-coordinate locking (WCL) maintains spatial consistency through base station keeping, object-relative positioning, and world-anchored contact targets. We demonstrate the effectiveness of PGX with extensive experiments conducted on three simulated tasks and one real-world task using a Unitree G1 humanoid robot for long-horizon loco-manipulation, showing improvements in stage progression and task success rates. Project page is available at: https://kl-research.github.io/pgx

2611.26598.abs: Acquiring every feature of an instance is often costly: a measurement can carry a monetary price, a time delay, or a privacy cost. Active Feature Acquisition (AFA) addresses this by learning a policy that decides, per instance, which features to acquire under a budget. Existing AFA methods train this policy by optimizing a self-constructed utility target rather than distilling an explicit teacher. We construct this teacher explicitly. At training time the label and the unobserved feature values are available, and together they determine the teacher in closed form: an oracle that ranks every candidate by its effect on the downstream predictor's error. OracleImitator distills this ranking into a deployable policy by soft-target imitation. Across multimodal medical diagnosis and the AFABench benchmark, OracleImitator matches or outperforms existing AFA methods across the budget range, recovering 90% of the attainable accuracy gain at under a quarter of the acquisition cost. Because the teacher is an explicit algorithmic object rather than an implicit optimization target, we can also measure directly how much of its ranking is recoverable by a policy restricted to what is visible at deployment.

2611.26516.abs: Most world models for future prediction prioritize aestetic quality of generated videos, but offer only weak physical grounding and limited geometric consistency over time, due to the lack of explicit 4D modeling. In this paper, we introduce plan4d, a possible next milestone towards building a generative plannable 4D world model that predicts future RGB videos together with dense 4D geometry, including depth, cameras, point clouds, and scene flow from an observed scene context and text-specified actions. Since training data with paired actions and dense 4D annotations is inherently scarce, plan4d leverages the complementary priors of foundational video generators and 3D reconstructors. Specifically, we propose a model-stitching architecture that couples Depth Anything 3 with LongCat-Video and augments it with an auxiliary DPT head for scene-flow prediction. The resulting model allows us to plan and generate complex, long-horizon, and fine-grained actions in a dynamic 3D scenes, while substantially improving both visual fidelity and geometric accuracy of the generated future videos. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that plan4d achieves state-of-the-art performance in generative 4D modeling of environmental reactions. Project Page: https://fogradio.github.io/plan4d-project

ov.problema: I world model per predire il futuro generano video esteticamente buoni ma con scarso ancoraggio fisico e coerenza geometrica nel tempo, perché manca una modellazione 4D esplicita (3D + tempo).
ov.idea: Plan4D predice video RGB futuri insieme a geometria 4D densa (profondità, camere, point cloud, scene flow) da un contesto osservato e azioni specificate in testo. Poiché i dati con azioni e annotazioni 4D sono scarsi, usa un'architettura di model-stitching che accoppia Depth Anything 3 con LongCat-Video e aggiunge una testa DPT ausiliaria per lo scene flow.
ov.risultati: Esperimenti su dataset sintetici e reali mostrano che Plan4D raggiunge prestazioni state-of-the-art nella modellazione 4D generativa delle reazioni ambientali, migliorando fedeltà visiva e accuratezza geometrica.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta numeri specifici né limiti espliciti; la dipendenza da prior di generatori video e ricostruttori 3D può vincolare la generalizzazione.

glossario.d: Campo di movimento 3D di ogni punto della scena tra due istanti.
Combinare modelli pre-addestrati diversi in un'unica architettura.
Modulo di testa basato su Dense Prediction Transformer per stimare mappe dense.

2611.26531.abs: Large Web platforms operate large fleets of ranking models, each selecting features from a shared pool of tens of thousands. We present an end-to-end agentic system that optimizes features across the fleet under resource constraints shared across models and those set per model, such as feature pipeline cost and serving throughput (QPS), respectively. In this system, LLM agents propose hypotheses, and deterministic tools execute experiments and verify them. For each model, an LLM generates and shortlists cross features from a combinatorial candidate space, and all features are then ranked by several importance methods. Feature blending mixes these rankings into a single selection, using Pareto fronts across tasks for multi-task models. An LLM Researcher agent then tunes the feature selection in 10--25 asynchronous trials under resource caps, and a trimming step keeps the pipeline cost within budget. Across production models, the system improves normalized entropy by 0.31% on average within each model's budget, and the trimming step cuts pipeline cost by 2.3% with no regression beyond measurement noise. The optimized models were launched, and in online A/B tests they improved a primary online metric by 0.20%.

2611.26358.abs: Beam is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model with 501.3B total parameters and 23.4B active parameters, specifically built and optimized for coding, reasoning, and agentic workloads. Beam delivers frontier level reasoning, while requiring 3-4x less inference compute than many models of its class. Pretrained on 23.8T diverse, curated, high-quality tokens, Beam features a 1M-token context window achieved through a novel two-stage midtraining phase, built on verifiable, correctness-anchored data. Post-training leveraged a large-scale, fully asynchronous reinforcement learning (RL) campaign across 10.5K GB300 GPUs, generating over 100M rollouts over 4 weeks of training. We believe this is one of the largest scale RL runs conducted by any open lab to date. Across our evaluation suite, capabilities continued to improve as we increased RL compute, with no sign of a plateau. Supported by deep hardware-model co-design, FP8/NVFP4 quantization, and a 1.93B-parameter speculative decoding drafter (DFlash 2), Beam maximizes serving throughput with efficient, flexible deployment. Averaged across conversation turns and harm categories, Beam refuses or pivots on 88.9% of harmful requests while complying with 81.5% of harmless requests, achieving the highest refusal/pivot rate on harmful requests among open-weight models on the Pareto frontier.

ov.problema: Serve un modello open-weight forte su coding, reasoning e agenti che richieda poco calcolo in inferenza e supporti contesti molto lunghi.
ov.idea: Beam è un MoE sparso (solo una parte dei parametri si attiva per token) con 501.3B parametri totali e 23.4B attivi, preaddestrato su 23.8T token e portato a 1M token di contesto con una fase di midtraining in due stadi su dati verificabili. Il post-training usa RL asincrono su larga scala, con quantizzazione FP8/NVFP4 e un drafter di speculative decoding da 1.93B parametri (DFlash 2).
ov.risultati: Richiede 3-4x meno calcolo di inferenza di molti modelli della sua classe; il RL è stato fatto su 10.5K GPU GB300 con oltre 100M rollout in 4 settimane e le capacità migliorano aumentando il calcolo RL senza plateau. Su richieste dannose rifiuta o devia nell'88.9% dei casi, con l'81.5% di compliance su richieste innocue.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta numeri di benchmark di ragionamento o coding, solo il quadro generale e i dati su rifiuto/compliance.

glossario.d: Modello con molti parametri totali ma solo una parte attiva per ogni token.
Un modello piccolo propone token che il modello grande verifica, accelerando l'inferenza.
Fase di addestramento intermedia, qui usata per estendere il contesto a 1M token.

2611.26376.abs: Vision-language models (VLMs) demonstrate broad generalization across tasks and domains. However, comparable generalization in robot manipulation remains challenging. Heterogeneity in robot embodiments, task formulations, geometric conventions, and action interfaces fragments interaction experience across benchmarks and hardware. We rethink robot skill learning through alignment: Can heterogeneous interactions across benchmarks and embodiments jointly improve one shared skillset for robot manipulation? We propose UniCraft, a framework for learning robot manipulation skills by aligning heterogeneous settings. Specifically, UniCraft represents observed scene geometry using consistent coordinate conventions and aligns sensing and control interfaces across robots. It organizes tasks from different benchmarks in a canonical format, allowing interaction feedback to jointly refine shared skills and the orchestration policy that guides their selection and composition, without any demonstrations or model weight updates. We interleave tasks from 3 benchmarks and 6 embodiments, collecting 2,700 learning rollouts per agent model. During training, UniCraft improves pooled task success on unseen scenarios and tasks by 9-28 percentage points on LIBERO-PRO, 10.8-13.3 on RoboTwin 2.0, and 3.1-14.4 on RoboCasa365 (Epochs 1-3). After training, with the learned skills frozen, UniCraft demonstrates zero-shot transfer across 4 new robot embodiments and 5 additional agent models on robosuite and RoboDojo.

2611.26398.abs: EU-funded projects produce extensive evidence in the form of deliverables, reports, and case studies. However, this knowledge is typically scattered across projects and document structures, making it difficult to locate relevant, contextual information when making decisions. This paper introduces an Agentic AI Ecosystem that consolidates heterogeneous project documentation into a domain-aware knowledge base and provides adaptive access through an agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline. Documents from three EU-funded projects (IMPETUS, NATALIE, and InnWater) are reconstructed into hierarchical section trees and indexed with structured metadata. Retrieval is supported by two domain-specific embedding models fine-tuned on domain data (water and climate). On top of this knowledge base, a ReAct-style controller iteratively orchestrates retrieval actions by allocating retrieval budget across domain collections and accumulating evidence until a stopping criterion is met. In a retrieval benchmark over the corpus, the proposed approach improves Mean Reciprocal Rank by 26.7% (relative) compared to a single-domain embedding baseline, indicating more consistent retrieval of relevant evidence to support cross-project knowledge synthesis and climate-resilient decision-making.

2611.26422.abs: Large language models (LLMs) can generate Q-matrices for diagnostic classification models that approximate expert specifications, but evaluations have focused on the final matrices, leaving the basis of individual item-attribute assignments unexamined. This opacity limits the responsible use of AI in measurement. We propose Reasoning-Trace Analysis (RTA), a framework in which an LLM generates attribute-labeled reasoning steps through chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting and these steps are analyzed to reconstruct, compare, and inspect each assignment. RTA is intended to supplement expert review and empirical validation. In a simulation study with perturbed fraction subtraction items, four LLMs recovered the required attributes and withheld attributes the items did not require. In an empirical study with 11 fraction subtraction items, responses from 536 examinees, four LLMs, up to three temperatures, and 100 replications per condition, CoT-derived Q-matrices overlapped substantially with the reference Q-matrix (mean overlap .809) but less than directly generated Q-matrices (.877), and they varied more across replications. Inspection of the traces linked disagreements to item-type coding, labeling rules, and how operations were expressed as steps. Q-matrices with similar overlap differed in fit to examinee responses. RTA provides inspectable evidence that matrix-level agreement and fit do not.

2611.26475.abs: We present a new adaptive stepsize rule that biases gradient descent toward flatter minima in both theory and practice, and establish the first uniform-in-time guarantees for both sharpness and loss reduction for a broad class of locally quadratic objectives. Our critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes multiply the classical Polyak rule by $4$ and a mild damping factor. The factor $4$ is critical in that it produces equioscillations around the manifold of minimizers $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order. Damping provably drives convergence to $\mathcal{M}$. CDP thus operates at the edge of stability by adapting its stepsizes to local curvature. Once the loss is small, its projected iterates follow gradient descent on $\log{λ_1(\nabla^2 \mathcal{L})}$ along $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order, paralleling the flatness bias of normalized gradient descent (Arora et al., 2022). Unlike normalized gradient descent, CDP step lengths shrink with the distance to $\mathcal{M}$, enabling convergence to an interpolating solution that locally minimizes sharpness at finite learning rate. We establish our theory for a broad class of non-negative losses with locally quadratic Morse-Bott structure near $\mathcal{M}$, capturing regular interpolation regimes in smooth overparameterized neural networks. Empirically, CDP stepsizes produce a flattening effect similar to that of Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM, Foret et al., 2021), reducing sharpness even in settings beyond our theory, including nonlinear teacher-student networks and fine-tuning of pre-trained LLMs.

2611.26389.abs: Current leading video generation models can synthesize highly realistic videos, while still frequently violating physical and logical constraints in multi-step reasoning and planning, even after training with large-scale reasoning data or existing diffusion RL methods. We attribute these failures to the conventional video training paradigm, which treats a solution as a fixed-length clip rather than a chain of decisions. We present ViDecide, a decision-centric framework that trains video diffusion models to predict state transitions causally and decide when to stop, with a decision-focused training schedule. We further propose Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT), which corrects failed decisions by mapping their noise to the model's own successful continuations, achieving stable improvement without policy-gradient optimization. Across abstract games, planning tasks, and a new benchmark of multi-step robot planning, ViDecide achieves an average strict success rate of 83.8%, far above 23.3% for standard fine-tuning and 67.8% for the strongest prior method, and generalizes to larger puzzles and unseen layouts. Our framework therefore unlocks greater potential for video generation models as reliable reasoners and planners in the visual world. Project page: https://kevin-thu.github.io/ViDecide.

ov.problema: I modelli di generazione video all'avanguardia producono video realistici ma violano spesso vincoli fisici e logici in ragionamento e pianificazione multi-step, anche dopo training con dati di ragionamento o metodi di RL per diffusione. La causa è il paradigma di training che tratta una soluzione come clip a lunghezza fissa invece che come catena di decisioni.
ov.idea: Presentano ViDecide, un framework decision-centric che addestra modelli di diffusione video a predire transizioni di stato causalmente e a decidere quando fermarsi, con un programma di training focalizzato sulle decisioni. Propongono anche Corrective Fine-tuning (CFT), che corregge decisioni fallite mappando il loro rumore sulle continuazioni riuscite del modello stesso, ottenendo miglioramenti stabili senza ottimizzazione con policy gradient.
ov.risultati: Su giochi astratti, task di pianificazione e un nuovo benchmark di pianificazione robotica multi-step, ViDecide raggiunge un tasso di successo stretto medio dell'83.8%, contro 23.3% del fine-tuning standard e 67.8% del miglior metodo precedente. Generalizza a puzzle più grandi e layout non visti.
ov.limiti: Non specificati nel testo.

glossario.d: Apprendimento per rinforzo applicato a modelli di diffusione.
Metodo di RL che ottimizza i parametri della policy tramite gradiente.

2611.25998.abs: Few-step diffusion models are widely deployed for their efficiency. However, reinforcing them with black-box rewards, as is routine for multi-step models, faces two structural challenges. First, a few-step generator is a sampler rather than a score model, so its velocity is not the forward velocity of the generated distribution. Second, it must be anchored to the undistilled teacher, which shares no transitions with it. Existing few-step RL methods handle the latter with a marginal KL to the teacher, but each pays for the former in its reward credit. We propose Shadow Posterior Matching (SPM), which renoises generated samples into shadow inputs and obtains the credit from their shadow posterior. From the KL-regularized reward objective, we derive a regression loss that turns reward values into a reward direction while anchoring the generator's outputs to the teacher and aligning the shadow inputs with the deployed inputs. Applied to 4-step generators, SPM achieves higher rewards with less reward hacking than prior few-step RL methods.

2611.25898.abs: Clinical large language models are usually judged by whether the final answer is right. Yet a model can reach a fluent, plausible output through invalid reasoning that static benchmarks do not detect, and confident hallucination, causally invalid inference, and spurious demographic shortcuts can pass conventional evaluation. This critical review covers four paradigms in turn: how clinical hallucination arises and why static metrics miss it; the agentic hallucination cascade, in which multi-agent and tool-augmented systems propagate and amplify early reasoning errors; process reward modeling as step-level supervision; and neuro-symbolic grounding, in which formal logic engines, ontology reasoners, and knowledge graphs place verifiable constraints on neural output. Within their encoded domains, systems with symbolic veto layers offer guarantees that hold relative to their encoded knowledge, and they report large gains on the safety measures they use. These results come from single studies, mostly in simulated or small-sample settings, and are not directly comparable with neural baselines. Process reward models remain bounded by the statistics of their training data. We propose a conceptual framework that maps each agentic failure mode to a symbolic intervention point, and we argue that clinical AI safety depends substantially on system architecture. Because current regulation emphasizes performance and does not require verification of reasoning steps, we argue that responsible certification should also audit reasoning trajectories alongside accuracy on static benchmarks.

2611.26450.abs: Pretrained language models (LMs) remain unreliable on exact multi-digit arithmetic without gradient fine-tuning or external tool interpreters. We introduce closed-form, zero-gradient circuit-grafting primitives that compile deterministic computation directly into pretrained LM weights using zero training examples and zero runtime hooks, while bounding per-layer normalization drift and preserving natural-language (NL) competence. Our construction combines three analytical mechanisms: (1) two-layer Mellin-GLU quadrature over bias-free SwiGLU/GeGLU layers, turning unknown per-token RMSNorm scaling into translation along a log-spaced gate grid (>250times dynamic range) with IEEE 754 error bounds; (2) cross-token scale cancellation via signed Chebyshev Indefinite-RoPE self-sink attention and memoryless SiLU-antisymmetric GatedDeltaNet shifts; and (3) axis-aligned width extension (d to d+K) with d/(d+K) norm compensation, Base-1000 canonical BPE emission, and differential (+254,-256) tied unembeddings. An automated 5-stage compiler synthesizes 4-8 digit signed {+,-,times} circuits in constant TC^0 depth alongside 3-literal Boolean (100%, N=1{,}728; plus 42-layer Gemma 4 E4B audits) and 5-bit Majority/Parity (100%) circuits. On 6-digit arithmetic (N=1{,}200, BF16), IBM Granite 4.2 3B (1.07M-1.33M active non-zeros, le 0.036%) and Alibaba Qwen 3.5 4B (2.25M-2.39M non-zeros, le 0.057%) reach 99.17% and 100.00% ALU-prefix accuracy (100% with an FP32 sidecar) and 98%-100% mid-sentence resumption, outperforming 12.8K-sample LoRA (42.2% / 61.7%, 0% inline continuation). A factorized…

ov.problema: I language model pre-addestrati restano inaffidabili sull'aritmetica esatta multi-cifra senza fine-tuning con gradienti o interpreti esterni.
ov.idea: Introducono primitive di "circuit-grafting" a forma chiusa e zero-gradient che compilano calcolo deterministico direttamente nei pesi del LM, senza esempi di training né hook a runtime, limitando la deriva di normalizzazione e preservando la competenza in linguaggio naturale. La costruzione combina quadrature Mellin-GLU su layer SwiGLU/GeGLU, cancellazione di scala cross-token con attenzione signed Chebyshev Indefinite-RoPE e shift GatedDeltaNet, ed estensione di larghezza allineata agli assi con compensazione di norma.
ov.risultati: Un compilatore automatico a 5 stadi sintetizza circuiti firmati a 4-8 cifre per {+,-,×} in profondità TC^0 costante, oltre a circuiti booleani a 3 letterali (100%, N=1.728) e Majority/Parity a 5 bit (100%). Su aritmetica a 6 cifre (N=1.200, BF16), IBM Granite 4.2 3B e Alibaba Qwen 3.5 4B raggiungono 99,17% e 100,00% di accuratezza ALU-prefix (100% con sidecar FP32) e 98%-100% di rianalisi a metà frase.
ov.limiti: Il testo è troncato e non chiarisce la generalizzazione ad altri modelli o a operazioni diverse da {+,-,×}.

glossario.d: Nessun addestramento con discesa del gradiente: i pesi sono modificati analiticamente.
Normalizzazione per token usata nei transformer, qui compensata per evitare deriva.
Classe di circuiti a profondità costante, molto efficienti da valutare.

2611.26545.abs: Linear probes are the cheapest LLM lie detectors but often fail to transfer across kinds of lie. Label-free directions from honest and deceptive role-play are untested at 70B scale and on lies about knowledge, where a lie and an honest denial can be identical. We widen a published persona bank with roles that deny knowledge they have, plus honest counterparts. At each model's middle layer the resulting persona direction ranks lies across Liars' Bench better than single-dataset probes on three of its four models; it fails on Qwen, even when Qwen stays in role far more often. On Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct it beats directions from a random persona bank, but its gain over the published direction is within the range of random widenings. On lies about knowledge, persona directions mainly track a reply's wording: where lies and honest denials share their words, our three main contrasts stay inside the random-direction band on Llama and Qwen and reach only its edge on Gemma, though on Mistral one clears it. A knowledge direction contrasts questions the model can answer with ones nobody can, each followed by the same scripted denial. It separates lies from identical honest denials on two models and narrowly on a third, but not on the fourth; its other results partly depend on the benchmark's wording. On the Gender-Secret fine-tune it clears the band by a few hundredths on Llama and fails on Mistral. The sum of the two directions ranks lies better than a supervised probe at the same depth on all four models (on one, both near chance) but is level with the persona direction on Llama's…

2611.26586.abs: Graphic designs are ordered compositions of RGBA layers whose separation enables selection, movement, and reuse. Existing layered models represent each layer with a full-canvas or region-sized spatial latent grid, so representation size grows with the cumulative spatial extent of the layers. We present ProtoDiffusion, a latent-diffusion framework built on ProtoVAE, a multi-layer variational autoencoder that encodes a design into one shared spatial prototype and one candidate vector per layer. Each candidate conditions a shared decoder to reconstruct its corresponding RGBA layer. For $N$ layers, the representation contains $HW+N$ tokens before backbone-specific packing, compared with $NHW$ for full-grid-per-layer representations. ProtoDiffusion jointly denoises the prototype and a fixed set of candidate slots, conditioned on an image or text, with bounding boxes as optional layout guidance. The model leaves unneeded slots empty and determines the number of layers and, in absence of boxes, their layout, requiring neither as input. The same architecture supports both image-to-design and text-to-design. ProtoVAE achieves high-fidelity reconstruction from its compact shared latent representation, reaching 40.43 dB PSNR on layer crops. On the LayerD evaluation split, image-to-design achieves RGB L1 scores of 0.040 with bounding boxes and 0.057 without, with box-guided alpha soft IoU (0.850) comparable to the strongest fine-tuned baseline (0.871). On merged images, text-to-design reaches 66.41 FID versus 86.84 for FLUX.2 [klein], achieves a 0.860 text-accuracy score, and runs…

2611.26464.abs: Set pieces produce about a third of non-penalty expected goals (xG), yet they are usually evaluated by what happened next.
