Together, these results separate interpretable, physical association from causal utility and establish sparse features as experimental coordinates for auditing and intervening on learned weather dynamics.

ov.problema: I modelli meteo appresi sono usati in contesti critici, ma non è chiaro se le loro rappresentazioni interne causalmente rilevanti abbiano un significato fisico.
ov.idea: Usano feature di un sparse autoencoder di GraphCast per testare se la rilevanza causale richieda semantica fisica. Ablano o amplificano direzioni latenti associate a fenomeni fisici durante il rollout per vedere l'effetto sulle previsioni.
ov.risultati: Ablare una feature legata alla mesh computazionale di GraphCast aumenta l'errore globale di altezza geopotenziale. Sopprimere feature associate a convezione e vorticità di basso livello indebolisce l'approfondimento dei cicloni tropicali, mentre amplificarle riduce l'errore di intensità, con una riduzione mediana del 51% su sette tempeste.

glossario.d: Rete che estrae feature sparse e interpretabili da attivazioni.
Rimozione di una componente per studiarne l'effetto.
Esecuzione sequenziale delle previsioni del modello.

2611.25328.abs: Analog layout generators provide a programmable interface for design reuse and process migration, but their coverage is limited by handcrafted libraries. The designer knowledge embedded in complete layouts remains implicit in their geometry, making it difficult to capture in reusable generator libraries. We present ReLay, a bidirectional layout-code framework that recovers generator programs from existing layouts, enabling cross-PDK portability and parametric resizing of existing designs. Constructions that recur across recovered programs are promoted to library functions, so the library evolves as layouts accumulate. We also introduce the first layout-code benchmark: 1,050 hand-drawn layouts from 27 circuit families across three open-source PDKs, ranging from primitive cells to full chips. Learned functions account for 53-66% of layout-building calls in held-out layouts, demonstrating reuse beyond the learning corpus. Frontier LLM agents use ReLay to produce new layouts at 64-77% lower API cost per completed task than direct geometry generation, with comparable completion rates and electrical quality.

2611.25252.abs: Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) now help develop many models published as general solutions. Should generality instead reside in the agent that builds a model for each new task? We examine this question in prognostics and health management (PHM), where every model must work on unseen equipment. Our deployment-style benchmark, NextUnit-Bench, covers 24 public datasets split into 58 folds that hold out units or operating conditions; each agent has two hours to deliver an executable predictor, then run on the hidden units. First, frontier agents outperform AutoML, which reaches less than half the best agent's score, and faithful implementations of published methods on four datasets, of which only 6 of 30 beat the strongest agent's own design; published accuracies, where reproducible, rest on the papers' own conventions, and a single convention, capping the remaining life of test engines, can halve the reported error. Second, the agents' advantage is a design made on each machine's data; once made, a plain-text plan of a few hundred words carries most of the gap between two frontier agents, and given a weaker agent's plan, the strongest agent falls to that agent's level, often to identical predictions. Before touching the data, however, it matters little whose plan an agent carries out, and domain toolkits appear to help neither: what sets the strongest apart is how much it learns from the data. Third, such designs reach only implementers that can execute them: given the strongest agent's designs, a locally deployable open-weight model delivers half as…

ov.problema: Nel prognostico e gestione della salute (PHM), i modelli devono funzionare su apparecchiature mai viste. I modelli generali pubblicati spesso non si adattano a nuovi contesti, e serve capire se la generalità debba risiedere nel modello o nell'agente che lo costruisce.
ov.idea: Gli autori propongono un benchmark chiamato NextUnit-Bench, in cui agenti basati su LLM devono consegnare un predittore eseguibile per ogni nuovo compito, con due ore di tempo. L'idea è che la generalità stia nell'agente che progetta il modello per ogni specifica macchina, piuttosto che in un modello unico.
ov.risultati: Gli agenti frontier superano AutoML (che raggiunge meno della metà del punteggio del miglior agente) e le implementazioni fedeli di metodi pubblicati (solo 6 su 30 battono il design dell'agente più forte). Il vantaggio degli agenti deriva da un design fatto sui dati di ciascuna macchina; un piano testuale di poche centinaia di parole cattura gran parte del divario tra due agenti frontier.
ov.limiti: I design raggiungono solo implementatori in grado di eseguirli; toolkit di dominio non sembrano aiutare.

glossario.d: Prognostica e gestione della salute: predire guasti e vita utile di macchine.
Automazione della selezione e ottimizzazione di modelli di machine learning.
Sistema autonomo che pianifica ed esegue azioni per raggiungere un obiettivo.

2611.25567.abs: An assistant monitoring a person performing a procedure is most useful when it can detect mistakes while there is still time to recover. This requires judging actions against task instructions as the video unfolds, identifying the attempted step, locating it in time, and assessing its execution. Existing online detectors do not use the instruction text, while instruction-conditioned methods operate offline. In this paper, we study online, instruction-conditioned mistake detection in egocentric videos. Using only observed video, task instructions, and prior predictions, our model identifies and localizes completed action attempts and classifies them as correct, modified, slip, corrections, or additions; omitted steps are determined after the video ends. We compare a modular pipeline, with separate step identification, temporal localization, and execution verification, to a joint model that predicts all outputs in a single step. To support supervised learning from mistakes, we repartition EgoPER to include erroneous videos in all splits. The approaches achieve similar step-segmentation F1@0.5 (93.6% and 92.1%), while the joint model achieves higher binary mistake-detection F1@0.5 (84.1% vs. 80.7%), with its largest gain on slips (56.4% vs. 37.5%). Component-level analysis suggests that error propagation between stages contributes to the modular approach's lower detection score. On test videos containing mistakes, both designs outperform released AEM and ESTANet checkpoints under our evaluation protocol.

ov.problema: Un assistente che monitora una persona durante una procedura è più utile se rileva errori mentre c'è ancora tempo per rimediare. Questo richiede di giudicare le azioni rispetto alle istruzioni del task mentre il video si svolge, identificando il passo tentato, localizzandolo nel tempo e valutandone l'esecuzione. I rilevatori online esistenti non usano il testo delle istruzioni, mentre i metodi condizionati dalle istruzioni operano offline.
ov.idea: Gli autori studiano il rilevamento online di errori condizionato dalle istruzioni in video egocentrici. Usando solo video osservato, istruzioni del task e predizioni precedenti, il modello identifica e localizza i tentativi di azione completati e li classifica come corretti, modificati, slip, correzioni o aggiunte; le omissioni sono determinate dopo la fine del video. Confrontano una pipeline modulare con un modello congiunto che predice tutti gli output in un singolo passo.
ov.risultati: Gli approcci raggiungono F1@0.5 simile per la segmentazione dei passi (93.6% e 92.1%), mentre il modello congiunto ottiene F1@0.5 più alto per il rilevamento binario di errori (84.1% vs. 80.7%), con il maggior guadagno sugli slip (56.4% vs. 37.5%). L'analisi a livello di componente suggerisce che la propagazione degli errori tra stadi contribuisce al punteggio di rilevamento inferiore dell'approccio modulare.
ov.limiti: Le omissioni sono determinate solo dopo la fine del video, quindi non sono rilevate online.

glossario.d: Misura di precisione e richiamo con soglia di sovrapposizione 0.5.
Errore di esecuzione di un passo, come versare troppo.
Video registrato dal punto di vista della persona che agisce.

2611.21885.abs: Language models are trained once, frozen and deployed: improving one again takes another training run, and a prompt, a scaffold or extra computation at inference is gone once the task ends. A frontier model has been shown to edit the weights of a much smaller one. We ask whether a model can rewrite its own weights to make itself better, and find that it can, by its own reasoning, with no gradients and no training; we call this self-rewriting. Given its weights, graded answers and the ability to run itself, a 27B model diagnoses its failure and edits the weights behind it. It surpasses itself: its own edit makes it 6.6 points more accurate on 490 problems it never saw, in a test fixed in advance, and another session's edit also makes it significantly better. It keeps getting better: it submits an edit only when its own tests support it, each edit replacing the last, and over its first eight such sessions its accuracy only rises. Unlike test-time scaling, the gain persists in its weights and adds no cost per answer; unlike training, it needs no pre- or post-training infrastructure, only an open model and hours on one GPU. It repairs a damaged copy of itself: it locates the corrupted matrix and rewrites it with values of its own, never reading the undamaged weights; found on text math problems alone, the repair lifts the copy on six image benchmarks it never saw from 7% to 70% accuracy, 83% of the undamaged model's. And the ability emerges with scale: across four sizes of one family, the 2B model makes no edit and the 4B and 9B models break themselves; only the 27B model…

ov.problema: I modelli linguistici vengono addestrati una volta e poi congelati: migliorarli richiede un altro addestramento, e un prompt o uno scaffold (impalcatura di ragionamento) sparisce a fine task. È difficile perché non si può correggere il modello senza gradienti né training.
ov.idea: Un modello può riscrivere i propri pesi da solo, con il proprio ragionamento, senza gradienti né training: si chiama self-rewriting. Dati i pesi, risposte valutate e la capacità di eseguire se stesso, un modello da 27B diagnostica il fallimento e modifica i pesi. L'edit viene inviato solo quando i test interni lo supportano, e ogni edit sostituisce il precedente.
ov.risultati: Su 490 problemi mai visti, l'edit del modello lo rende più accurato di 6,6 punti; un edit di un'altra sessione lo migliora significativamente. Nelle prime otto sessioni l'accuratezza sale sempre. Ripara una copia danneggiata di sé: trova la matrice corrotta e la riscrive senza leggere i pesi intatti, portando la copia dal 7% al 70% di accuratezza su sei benchmark di immagini mai visti (83% del modello intatto).
ov.limiti: Richiede un modello aperto e ore su una singola GPU; i risultati mostrati si fermano alle prime otto sessioni e a un modello da 27B.

glossario.d: Il modello modifica i propri pesi usando solo il suo ragionamento, senza gradienti né addestramento.
Aumentare la potenza di calcolo al momento della risposta, senza cambiare i pesi del modello.
Informazioni usate dall'addestramento classico per aggiornare i pesi tramite discesa del gradiente.

2611.25604.abs: End-to-end autonomous driving increasingly depends on scaling training demonstrations, yet data growth does not guarantee proportional gains. However, additional data do not guarantee better policies: a demonstration that benefits one planner may be redundant or harmful to another. Existing curation methods typically infer data value from intrinsic sample properties or training-dependent proxies that do not measure downstream policy utility. To address this, we introduce Policy-Aware Data Valuation (PAD), a framework that assigns each candidate demonstration a utility specific to the target driving policy. PAD combines scene-level calibration feedback with projected policy gradients and a regularized approximation of local training geometry, producing scalable influence-based values for the policy. A controlled group-removal study establishes the directional fidelity of these values, while cross-planner analysis shows that the same candidate pool induces markedly different rankings across planner families. On DiffusionDrive, PAD improves EPDMS over real-only training by 3.5 points on NavTest and 5.0 points on NavHard. Policy-specific curation consistently outperforms real-only and full-pool training across diffusion-, regression-, and flow-matching-based planners while substantially reducing scene-level regressions. These results establish policy-aware data valuation as a basis for replacing indiscriminate data accumulation with targeted policy improvement, enabling more efficient and reliable scaling of autonomous-driving systems.

2611.26232.abs: Learning and inference on time series can pose significant statistical challenges, including autocorrelated observations, distribution shift over time, and the curse of dimensionality. These challenges complicate the practical application of causal discovery algorithms, which already suffer from high computational and sample complexity in the general case. To mitigate these issues, this work introduces Iterative Temporal Parent Discovery (ITPD): a sound and complete constraint-based procedure for causal structure learning on multivariate time series with causal nonstationarity. ITPD takes a local-to-global learning approach that discovers the global graph by sequentially discovering the parent set for each variable. ITPD exploits temporal structural priors, graph partitioning, and the local Markov condition to swap higher-order conditional independence tests for lower-order alternatives. With an exact oracle, ITPD performed the least number of tests and used the smallest average conditioning set sizes relative to baselines. In benchmarking simulations, ITPD sat on the Pareto frontier with respect to F1 and wall-clock time and was faster than baselines on large graphs (geq 1000 nodes). For graphs with 2000 nodes, ITPD ran 2.3times, 9.1times, and 40.9times faster than iterative IAMB, DF-PC, and PCMCI, respectively.

2611.25200.abs: Experimentation teams must decide which proposed website changes to test with live traffic. We evaluated whether forecasts from simulated shoppers could inform that choice. We screened 412 historical website A/B tests and evaluated four systems on the 318 that ran longer than 21 days. Each system predicted an original win, a variant win, or an inconclusive result. Page roles were masked and recorded outcomes were withheld during inference. Squoosh UX-1, a model fine-tuned on human browsing data, simulated 1,000 shoppers per arm and correctly classified 267 of 318 outcomes (84.0%, 95% Wilson interval 79.5-87.6%, treating experiments as independent). Qwen3 Next 80B, the strongest general-purpose configuration on outcome accuracy, correctly classified 196 of 318 (61.6%). UX-1 favored the variant in 126 experiments. In the live tests, 118 of those variants won (93.7%), four lost, and four had inconclusive results. The remaining 192 experiments included 19 additional variant wins.

2611.15941.abs: Image vectorization reconstructs raster images as compact scalable vector graph- ics (SVG), providing a structured and editable code representation of images. However, most existing vectorization methods optimize for pixel-level render- ing fidelity, often producing SVGs that lack alignment with human-perceived object-part hierarchies, making them difficult to manipulate. To address this, we propose Lang-SVG, which introduces an explicit tree structure to organize SVG primitives with semantic labels and parent-child relationships. Lang-SVG incorporates granularity-controllable and open-vocabulary segmentation priors to initialize object-part hierarchies and leverages multimodal large language models (MLLMs) with SVG tree context to assign semantic labels to unlabeled nodes. To reduce redundancy, we introduce depth-adaptive simplification to reduce shape complexity and Tree-Guided Pruning and Merging to eliminate redundant SVG nodes. L1-SAM-Prompting further recovers missing regions to improve recon- struction fidelity and structural completeness. Beyond reconstruction fidelity, we introduce a new evaluation protocol that measures structural quality and semantic part alignment. Experiments demonstrate that Lang-SVG achieves state-of-the-art performance in both rendering fidelity and structural quality. Project website: https://xiliu8006.github.io/Lang-SVG/.

2611.27193.abs: Manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC) extends residual connections to multiple streams and stabilizes residual propagation by constraining stream-mixing residual matrices to the Birkhoff polytope, the set of doubly stochastic matrices. In this work, we investigate how to effectively mix residual streams within the Birkhoff polytope. We reveal a mixing trade-off: when under-mixed residual matrices stay close to the vertices of the Birkhoff polytope, hyper-connections will degenerate into a set of nearly independent streams; when over-mixed residual matrices are concentrated around the uniform barycenter of the polytope, streams will become less distinguishable from each other. We theoretically validate our findings by bounding the cumulative residual mixing, stream difference and gradient difference of mixing coefficients across layers. Motivated by these findings, we propose Contraction for Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (cmHC), an exact doubly stochastic method which geometrically contracts the Birkhoff polytope toward its interior. This contraction mitigates under-mixing by forcing the residual matrices to explore deeper into the polytope, with a provable stream mixing bound and no new parameterization. Moreover, we apply a moderate contraction at the shallow layers to prevent over-mixing, enabling stable gradient propagation on extremely large-scale model pretraining. Extensive experiments across dense and mixture-of-experts models at various parameter scales demonstrate the effectiveness and scalability of cmHC. We also develop fused operators for cmHC…

ov.problema: Le iper-connessioni vincolate alla varietà (mHC) estendono le connessioni residue a più flussi e le stabilizzano vincolando le matrici di mescolamento al politopo di Birkhoff (matrici doppiamente stocastiche). Tuttavia, non è chiaro come mescolare efficacemente i flussi residui all'interno di questo politopo.
ov.idea: Gli autori rivelano un compromesso: se il mescolamento è troppo debole, i flussi restano quasi indipendenti; se è troppo forte, i flussi diventano indistinguibili. Propongono cmHC, che contrae geometricamente il politopo di Birkhoff verso l'interno, forzando le matrici a esplorare più a fondo il politopo e bilanciando il mescolamento, con un limite dimostrabile e senza nuovi parametri.
ov.risultati: Esperimenti su modelli densi e mixture-of-experts a varie scale mostrano che cmHC migliora l'addestramento stabile su modelli molto grandi.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta limiti espliciti.

glossario.d: Insieme delle matrici doppiamente stocastiche, usate per mescolare flussi.
Connessioni che sommano l'input all'output di un layer, facilitando il gradiente.
Architettura che usa più esperti specializzati attivati selettivamente.

2611.27963.abs: We study a new problem of preventing object penetration in interactive video world models. To understand how existing models handle this, we introduce NoPeBench, a benchmark that evaluates how world models respond to physical obstacles. Our evaluation reveals that none of the open-source models can reliably prevent such failures. Surprisingly, however, these models already encode the information needed to predict such violations. We find that the hidden states of diffusion transformers (DiTs) can predict whether a candidate action will penetrate an obstacle. Building on this, we introduce NoPeWorld, a lightweight framework that detects and prevents penetration. Specifically, we train a small prediction head on top of a frozen DiT's hidden states to read out if a candidate action is safe or not. Unsafe actions are then replaced with safe ones that best preserve the original intent. Despite its simplicity, NoPeWorld substantially reduces the physical violation rate, averaged over six video world models, from 74% to 16%. Remarkably, our method shows zero-shot generalization to open-domain imagery, third-person viewpoints, and moving obstacles. We publicly release our code, the NoPeBench benchmark, and model weights. Project Page: https://nopeworld.github.io .

ov.problema: I modelli video interattivi (world models) spesso fanno penetrare gli oggetti tra loro, un fallimento fisico che nessun modello open-source riesce a evitare in modo affidabile.
ov.idea: Gli autori mostrano che gli stati nascosti dei diffusion transformer (DiT, reti che generano video) contengono già l'informazione per prevedere se un'azione causerà una penetrazione. Aggiungono una piccola testa di previsione sopra un DiT congelato per leggere se un'azione è sicura; le azioni non sicure vengono sostituite con alternative sicure che mantengono l'intento originale.
ov.risultati: NoPeWorld riduce il tasso medio di violazioni fisiche dal 74% al 16% su sei modelli video, con generalizzazione zero-shot a immagini open-domain, viste in terza persona e ostacoli in movimento.
ov.limiti: Il metodo si basa su una testa di previsione addestrata e non modifica il modello base; la generalizzazione è dimostrata solo su alcuni scenari.

glossario.d: Modello che simula la dinamica di un ambiente generando video interattivi.
Rete neurale che genera dati (es. video) tramite diffusione, basata su transformer.
Capacità di generalizzare a casi mai visti durante l'addestramento.

2611.15449.abs: Text-aware image super-resolution (TAISR) aims to recover high-resolution images from low-resolution inputs while preserving textual content. Existing methods treat this as a visual restoration problem, yet severely degraded text often cannot be read from local visual evidence alone. Humans instead read it by reasoning over image context, logical patterns, and prior knowledge. This raises a fundamental question: Does TAISR need reasoning? To answer this, we introduce two diagnostic tools. The first, ReasonText, is a human-curated benchmark that separates reasoning-required text from locally recoverable text. The second, Ground-Truth Text-Crop Accuracy (GTTCA), is a recognition-based metric that measures text restoration quality without text detection errors. Evaluating twelve recent super-resolution (SR) models, we find a consistent and substantial performance drop on reasoning-required text, revealing a systematic blind spot. Two observations point to a remedy. One is that text-conditioned SR models restore text substantially better when given ground-truth text. The other is that multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can read degraded text in low-resolution images through reasoning. We therefore propose Reasoning Transfer via Captioning (RTC), a training-free plug-in that uses an external MLLM to infer the degraded text and feeds the resulting caption to a text-conditioned SR model. RTC consistently improves all six text-conditioned SR models we evaluate, especially on reasoning-required text. Surprisingly, a real-world SR model with RTC can even outperform the TAISR…

ov.problema: La super-risoluzione di immagini con testo (TAISR) deve recuperare testo leggibile da input a bassa risoluzione. I metodi esistenti trattano il problema come puro restauro visivo, ma il testo molto degradato non è leggibile solo dall'evidenza locale.
ov.idea: Gli autori introducono due strumenti diagnostici: ReasonText, un benchmark che separa testo che richiede ragionamento da testo localmente recuperabile, e GTTCA, una metrica basata sul riconoscimento. Propongono RTC (Reasoning Transfer via Captioning), un plug-in training-free che usa un MLLM esterno per inferire il testo degradato e passarlo a un modello SR text-conditioned.
ov.risultati: Su 12 modelli SR recenti, si osserva un calo consistente sulle porzioni che richiedono ragionamento. RTC migliora tutti e sei i modelli SR text-conditioned valutati, specialmente sui casi che richiedono ragionamento.
ov.limiti: RTC dipende da un MLLM esterno e non è addestrato end-to-end; le prestazioni possono variare con la qualità del captioning.

glossario.d: Text-aware image super-resolution: ricostruisce immagini ad alta risoluzione preservando il contenuto testuale.
Modello linguistico multimodale, capace di elaborare testo e immagini insieme.
Metrica che misura la qualità del testo ricostruito basandosi sul riconoscimento, evitando errori di rilevamento.

2611.27973.abs: Deploying large language models (LLMs) in long-horizon and continual interactions requires maintaining reusable memory states for future inference, posing challenges for existing architectures. Standard Transformers accumulate layer-wise, token-level KV caches, incurring linear GPU memory growth and quadratic computational complexity as the context expands. In contrast, linear-time architectures compress history into fixed-size states, but struggle to retain fine-grained details. We introduce MemOnce, a foundation architecture that learns scalable memory states for language models. MemOnce is based on two core designs: (a) Memory encoder-decoder: it caches only a small subset of final-layer hidden states as compact memory representations and dynamically decodes them back into KV caches for attention layers; (b) Memory sparse attention: for each continual input, MemOnce adaptively retrieves relevant memory representations, with the sparse indices computed only once across layers. Coupling these two designs enables efficient on-the-fly memory loading and KV cache decoding, drastically reducing the GPU memory footprint and achieving linear-time complexity. We conduct extensive experiments to show that MemOnce outperforms Transformers and other architectures across varying model sizes, context lengths, and training paradigms (pretraining and post-training adaptation). In particular, adapting Qwen3.5-4B with MemOnce reduces memory state cache by 1313times and prefill latency by 6.9times at 1M context, and improves throughput by 3.5times and overall memory performance by +5.77%.…

ov.problema: I Transformer standard accumulano cache KV (chiavi-valori) che crescono linearmente con il contesto, causando un uso di memoria GPU elevato e complessità quadratica. Le architetture a tempo lineare comprimono la storia in stati fissi ma perdono dettagli fini.
ov.idea: MemOnce è un'architettura che impara stati di memoria scalabili: un encoder-decoder di memoria memorizza solo un piccolo sottoinsieme degli stati nascosti dell'ultimo layer come rappresentazione compatta e li decodifica dinamicamente in cache KV per i layer di attenzione. Inoltre, un'attenzione sparsa recupera adattivamente le memorie rilevanti, con indici sparsi calcolati una sola volta per tutti i layer.
ov.risultati: Adattando Qwen3.5-4B con MemOnce si riduce la cache di memoria di 1313 volte e la latenza di prefill di 6 volte, superando Transformer e altre architetture in varie dimensioni, lunghezze di contesto e paradigmi di addestramento.
ov.limiti: Il testo non specifica limiti o condizioni particolari.

glossario.d: Memoria delle chiavi e valori usata dai Transformer per l'attenzione, cresce col contesto.
Fase iniziale in cui il modello elabora il prompt prima di generare.
Meccanismo che considera solo una parte degli elementi, riducendo i calcoli.

2611.25773.abs: Full-duplex interaction models exhibit strong conversational agency, enabling natural, low-latency turn-taking, backchannels, and interruptions. However, completing tasks further requires task agency: timely tool invocation and argument revision following user corrections. Frontend-backend agents separate initiation from execution: the frontend decides whether and what to request, while the backend determines how. Execution can be offloaded, but unsent requests cannot be executed, and incomplete ones can misdirect the backend. On Full-Duplex-Bench v3 (FDB v3), most failures of Realtime-Venus-Audio + Harness in our streaming pipeline occur before a domain tool executes. We introduce Duopra, a full-duplex interaction model that learns task execution alongside conversational control. Duopra treats the backend as a tool, accepting a self-contained natural-language request. Direct calls and backend delegation share an action interface and requirements for faithful initiation and correct execution. Its three-stage training combines protocol SFT, full-duplex RL rewarding timely and complete execution, and projector-only repair of talker conditioning after thinker updates. With the same backend, Pass@1 rises from 4.7% to 44.7%; Duopra achieves 47.7% calling tools directly (26.0% after SFT) and 49.3% with a DeepSeek backend. It improves three FDB v1.0 takeover rates over the base model. These results show that task agency can coexist with key conversational agency.

ov.problema: I modelli conversazionali full-duplex (che parlano e ascoltano insieme) gestiscono bene i turni di parola, ma faticano a completare compiti: chiamare strumenti al momento giusto e correggere gli argomenti quando l'utente li corregge. Nei sistemi frontend-backend, se la richiesta non viene mai inviata o è incompleta, il backend non può eseguirla.
ov.idea: Duopra è un modello full-duplex che impara l'esecuzione del compito insieme al controllo della conversazione. Tratta il backend come uno strumento: sia le chiamate dirette sia la delega al backend usano la stessa interfaccia d'azione. L'addestramento in tre fasi combina SFT sul protocollo, RL full-duplex che premia esecuzioni tempestive e complete, e una riparazione solo del projector dopo gli aggiornamenti del 'thinker'.
ov.risultati: Con lo stesso backend, Pass@1 sale dal 4.7% al 44.7%. Duopra raggiunge il 47.7% chiamando gli strumenti direttamente (26.0% dopo SFT) e il 49.3% con un backend DeepSeek. Migliora tre tassi di takeover di FDB v1.0 rispetto al modello base.
ov.limiti: I risultati dipendono dal backend usato e sono misurati su FDB v3 e FDB v1.0; il testo non chiarisce la generalizzazione ad altri domini.

glossario.d: Interazione in cui il modello ascolta e parla contemporaneamente, senza turni rigidi
Percentuale di volte in cui il primo tentativo del modello è corretto
Supervised Fine-Tuning: addestramento supervisionato su esempi etichettati

2611.27915.abs: Vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit strong semantic understanding but remain limited in their ability to reason about metric 3D space in the physical world. Existing VLMs typically infer 3D scene structure from one or more images without known camera calibration or cross-view geometric constraints. This makes metric 3D inference inherently ambiguous and leaves it unclear whether their spatial predictions are grounded in visual evidence or driven primarily by semantic priors. In contrast, calibrated stereo provides explicit cross-view geometry that resolves this ambiguity and offers a more reliable foundation for metric 3D perception and geometric generalization. We investigate how VLMs can learn transferable 3D representations directly from calibrated binocular observations. To this end, we introduce StereoVLM, the first geometry-aware binocular VLM for metric 3D spatial reasoning. StereoVLM follows a hierarchical learning paradigm spanning from cross-view correspondence and disparity estimation to calibration-conditioned metric depth perception and semantic spatial reasoning. We further find that disparity supervision generalizes substantially better than direct binocular depth supervision on unseen environments. To evaluate these capabilities, we introduce Stereo3D-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark across three levels, from point-level geometry to object-level spatial reasoning. StereoVLM-8B achieves 95.17% depth accuracy (δ_1) and a 66.98 average object-level score on Stereo3D-Bench. Intervention results further indicate that the model's performance on Stereo3D-Bench…

ov.problema: I modelli visione-linguaggio (VLM) hanno una buona comprensione semantica ma sono limitati nel ragionamento spaziale 3D metrico (con misure reali). Spesso inferiscono la struttura 3D da immagini senza calibrazione della camera, rendendo ambigua la stima delle distanze.
ov.idea: StereoVLM è il primo VLM binoculare (con due viste) geometry-aware per il ragionamento spaziale 3D metrico. Usa un paradigma di apprendimento gerarchico: corrispondenza tra viste, stima della disparità (differenza di posizione tra pixel corrispondenti), profondità metrica condizionata dalla calibrazione e ragionamento spaziale semantico. La supervisione sulla disparità generalizza meglio della supervisione diretta sulla profondità binoculare.
ov.risultati: StereoVLM-8B raggiunge il 95.17% di accuratezza sulla profondità (δ_1) e un punteggio medio di 66.98 a livello di oggetto su Stereo3D-Bench.

glossario.d: Differenza di posizione di un oggetto tra due immagini stereo.
Determinazione dei parametri della camera per misure accurate.
Percentuale di pixel con errore di profondità entro una soglia.

2611.22343.abs: Identity matching asks whether two records denote the same identity, yet the answer depends on the target granularity. Two records may match at the base level but not at the variant level: they share an underlying design while differing in attributes such as color or size. Final matching accuracy does not separately characterize the capabilities involved. To study this problem, we use e-commerce as a challenging real-world domain. We introduce PURE, a diagnostic benchmark for multi-granularity multimodal identity matching covering four capability dimensions: Perception, Understanding, Reasoning, and Evidence-grounded Judgment. The benchmark comprises 1,457 multiple-choice questions across 14 tasks, derived from real-world matching pairs and verified by two domain experts. Across ten recent MLLMs, overall scores range from 47.1% to 86.0%. Understanding receives the highest mean score and Judgment the lowest, with weaknesses in visual difference localization and variant-level rule judgment. Modality ablations show that models benefit from multimodal evidence but can incorrectly identify conflicts between matching records. In direct matching, most models recognize matching pairs more reliably than non-matching pairs at the base level, whereas the reverse holds at the variant level. PURE therefore reveals what aggregate matching accuracy hides: not only whether models judge a pair correctly, but where they struggle to interpret evidence and apply matching criteria.

ov.problema: L'identità matching (stabilire se due record si riferiscono alla stessa entità) dipende dalla granularità: due record possono corrispondere a livello base ma non a livello variante (stesso design ma attributi diversi come colore o taglia). L'accuratezza finale non distingue le capacità coinvolte.
ov.idea: PURE è un benchmark diagnostico per il matching multimodale multi-granularità, con quattro dimensioni di capacità: Percezione, Comprensione, Ragionamento e Giudizio basato su evidenze. Comprende 1.457 domande a scelta multipla su 14 compiti, derivate da coppie reali e verificate da esperti.
ov.risultati: Su dieci MLLM recenti, i punteggi totali vanno dal 47.1% all'86.0%. La Comprensione ha il punteggio medio più alto, il Giudizio il più basso, con debolezze nella localizzazione delle differenze visive e nel giudizio a livello di variante. Le ablazioni mostrano che i modelli beneficiano di evidenze multimodali ma possono identificare erroneamente conflitti.

glossario.d: Modello linguistico multimodale, che elabora testo e immagini.
Tecnica per valutare l'importanza di una componente rimuovendola.
Livello di dettaglio nella corrispondenza tra record.

2611.27229.abs: Prompt enhancement (PE) refines concise user prompts into detailed descriptions to improve the compositional aesthetics of generated images while preserving user intent. A common practice constructs supervised fine-tuning (SFT) pairs by deriving short, user-like prompts from dense captions, implicitly assuming that captions that improve image generation also provide effective supervision. In this paper, however, we uncover a counterintuitive finding: PE models trained on caption pairs with substantial generation gains perform comparably to those trained on pairs with only marginal gains. We argue that dense captions can impose redundant supervision by requiring PE models to reproduce image-specific details weakly related to user intent. Motivated by this discrepancy, we introduce Prune to Expand (P2E), a simple text-only method that refines dense-caption supervision by selectively removing redundant sentences under a per-example deletion bound while preserving explicit user requirements and informative visual structure. Extensive experiments under identical training configurations demonstrate that P2E improves alignment with human preferences and visual quality over conventional dense-caption SFT across diverse image categories and visual generators.

2611.27978.abs: This study examines one-day-ahead forecasting of the S&P 500 closing level using a 2006-2025 dataset that includes fundamental price data, macroeconomic indicators, and engineered technical features. We benchmark three model families, namely linear regression, vanilla recurrent neural networks (RNN), and long short-term memory networks (LSTM), within a unified preprocessing and chronological evaluation pipeline. A central contribution of this work is a methodological audit of common practices in the deep-learning-for-stock-prediction literature. We identify three sources of result inflation that frequently appear in published methodologies: wavelet-denoised evaluation targets, the absence of a naive persistence baseline, and best-of-N replicate reporting. We then re-evaluate all model families under a corrected protocol that controls for each. Performance is reported using root mean squared error, mean absolute percentage error, and the Pearson correlation coefficient, averaged across N = 30 independent replicates per configuration. We compare models on accuracy, stability across replicates, and architectural depth sensitivity, using the naive persistence forecast (predicting today's close as tomorrow's close) as a primary baseline against which all candidate models must demonstrate improvement.

2611.27962.abs: Machine learning has largely kept separate the choice of architecture and the process of training. A classic Transformer, for instance, trains a fixed set of attention and MLP sublayers at every layer, in the same order, and optimizes the weights within. This uniformity is a convention rather than a principled design choice, and it is likely suboptimal: the best architecture for a given task may be smaller, more efficient, and far from uniform. We believe that, ideally, training itself should shape the model's topology. To this end, we introduce Model Carving, which learns both a Transformer's weights and its architecture in a single run. By applying learnable, scalar gates to each sublayer, we allow the training loss to remove the model's own components during training -- freeing a smaller heterogeneous network inside. We evaluate Model Carving by pre-training standard Transformers from 140M to 2.7B parameters and looped Transformers from 140M to 1.3B. At equal training compute, carved models reach a lower validation loss than dense models trained with up to 1.7 times more compute. Furthermore, carved models also outperform size-matched models produced by pruning or distillation, suggesting that the best way to obtain small models for edge devices is to carve them during training, not to compress a large one afterwards. This advantage both grows with scale and carries over to downstream tasks such as few-shot evaluation and generation. Because the removed sublayers no longer run, carved models also cost up to 34% fewer FLOPs per token and decode up to 1.6 times faster…

ov.problema: Tradizionalmente, l'architettura di un Transformer è fissa e il training ottimizza solo i pesi. Questa uniformità è una convenzione, non una scelta di principio, e potrebbe essere subottimale: l'architettura migliore per un compito potrebbe essere più piccola, efficiente e non uniforme.
ov.idea: Model Carving impara sia i pesi che l'architettura in una singola esecuzione. Applica gate scalari apprendibili a ogni sotto-livello, permettendo alla loss di training di rimuovere componenti del modello durante l'addestramento, liberando una rete eterogenea più piccola.
ov.risultati: Pre-addestrando Transformer standard da 140M a 2.7B parametri e Transformer looped da 140M a 1.3B, i modelli carved raggiungono una validation loss inferiore rispetto a modelli densi addestrati con fino a 1.7 volte più calcolo. I modelli carved superano anche modelli di pari dimensioni prodotti da pruning o distillazione.
ov.limiti: Non specificati nel testo.

glossario.d: Architettura di rete neurale basata su meccanismi di attenzione.
Rimozione di connessioni o neuroni da una rete neurale.
Addestramento di un modello piccolo per imitare uno più grande.

2611.27939.abs: When a robot is damaged, it must decide which routes it can still afford, and the amount of risk it may accept can change from one mission to the next. We argue that whether a learned model helps such a robot depends on its decision interface, that is, on what the model hands to the planner. A decision policy tells the planner what to do, whereas an outcome model, a kind of world model, predicts the consequences of each route. We study simulated Unitree Go2 quadrupeds and H1 humanoids with weakened motors, added payloads, or reduced foot friction. We compare four interfaces. The first is a decision policy, and the second is the same policy trained with fixed penalties for infeasible routes. The third is an outcome model that predicts the feasibility and travel time of each route. The fourth, which we call a capability contract, is an outcome model that predicts the chance of success and the travel time of the robot on each terrain and composes them along a route. All share the same collected experience, matched tuning and risk calibration, and an uncertainty guard. Two comparatively low-risk probes let the capability contract rank hazardous terrains about as well as four new trials on every hazard. At a calibrated 5% limit on selecting empirically infeasible routes, outcome models cut declined missions from about 32% to 7-8% on Go2 and from 57% to 35-36% on H1 compared with the plain policy. Fixed penalties narrow this gap, but the best penalty changes with the risk target. Predicting outcomes lets the planner preserve missions by changing routes as risk requirements…

2611.27917.abs: Cardiovascular imaging offers several ways to measure blood flow, but each provides an incomplete, resolution-limited, or noisy view of the underlying dynamics. Reconstructing the missing information is inherently ambiguous because several flow fields may be compatible with the same observation. Here, we investigate generative diffusion models as tools for cardiovascular-flow generation and reconstruction using a fully controlled state-of-the-art dataset from a digital twin of a healthy human left heart. First, we show how unconditional samples reproduce the changing anatomy and the highly fluctuating statistical properties of the flow throughout the cardiac cycle. Second, we test the conditional inference of our generative model by reconstructing an entire 2D planar section of geometry and flow configurations from a limited portion. Repeated reconstructions allow us to represent a range of plausible completions, going beyond a single deterministic estimate, while their mean retains the principal features of the reference flow. Comparison with a Gaussian process regression baseline on the same reduced domain highlights the main advantage of diffusion models: their reconstructed ensembles capture a broader range of velocity and gradient fluctuations, better encompassing ground-truth features that the baseline distributions can miss. Our results provide a quantitative proof of concept for probabilistic reconstruction of incomplete cardiovascular-flow measurements and demonstrate the potential for groundbreaking applications to the augmentation of in-vivo cardiovascular…

2611.27911.abs: Transformer performance scales with depth, but layer count merely counts the opportunities for sequential computation: layers could still behave as nearly independent refinements that barely depend on one another. We study how transformers develop functional depth during pretraining, introducing an exact inclusion-exclusion decomposition that isolates the connected component, i.e., the computation that appears only when a specified set of layers acts together under identity ablation. Tracking this quantity across public checkpoints of Pythia, OLMo, and Amber yields three findings. First, write-relative connected coordination strengthens from its initialization or earliest-checkpoint baseline as pretraining proceeds, across all measured interaction orders. Second, these connected components are behaviorally consequential under direct intervention: deleting them damages perplexity more than deleting a norm-matched random direction at the same site in all 35 measured model-order cells. Third, pairwise representation similarity is consistently negatively correlated with pairwise connected coordination across seven models, yet the two signals are not interchangeable: similarity- and coordination-based block-removal criteria often agree in Pythia but diverge on Amber. Together, these results suggest that architectural depth provides the opportunity for sequential computation, while pretraining progressively organizes cross-layer dependencies within that depth.

ov.problema: Le prestazioni dei transformer crescono con la profondità, ma il numero di layer conta solo le opportunità di calcolo sequenziale: i layer potrebbero comportarsi come raffinamenti quasi indipendenti. Non è chiaro come si sviluppi la 'profondità funzionale' durante il pretraining.
ov.idea: Gli autori introducono una decomposizione esatta per inclusione-esclusione che isola la 'componente connessa', cioè il calcolo che emerge solo quando un insieme di layer agisce insieme sotto ablazione identità. Tracciano questa quantità nei checkpoint pubblici di Pythia, OLMo e Amber.
ov.risultati: Tre risultati: il coordinamento connesso relativo alla scrittura si rafforza durante il pretraining in tutti gli ordini di interazione misurati; cancellare queste componenti danneggia la perplessità più di una direzione casuale a norma uguale in tutte le 35 celle modello-ordine misurate; la similarità tra rappresentazioni a coppie è negativamente correlata al coordinamento connesso in sette modelli, ma i due segnali non sono intercambiabili.
ov.limiti: Lo studio è limitato a modelli e checkpoint pubblici specifici; non è chiaro quanto generalizzi ad architetture o scale diverse.

glossario.d: sostituire l'output di un componente con l'input, per vedere cosa cambia
misura di quanto il modello è incerto nel predire il testo; più bassa è meglio
parte del calcolo che appare solo quando più layer agiscono insieme

2611.27901.abs: Streaming visual geometry transformers retain historical key-value (KV) states as cross-view geometric memory, but growing caches constrain long-sequence inference. We systematically characterize KV quantization in streaming geometry and uncover two linked challenges: Nonuniform Geometric Sensitivity and Cache-Geometry Mismatch. Quantization sensitivity varies across precision choices and cache locations, while perturbed retrieval changes geometry-head inputs and propagates through subsequent predictions and KV writes. Guided by these findings, we propose QuantStream3D, to our knowledge the first dedicated KV quantization framework for streaming visual geometry transformers. Geometry-Guided Mixed-Precision KV Quantization protects sensitive cross-view evidence, while Geometry-Aligned Quantization-Aware Distillation jointly adapts transformer blocks and geometry heads on student-generated quantized history. Across five benchmarks and two backbones, QuantStream3D achieves near-lossless geometric accuracy in most settings with predominantly 2-bit KV caches, and many configurations surpass unquantized inference. Compared with LLM-oriented KV quantizers, it reduces TUM absolute trajectory error and NeuralRGBD completeness error by up to 57.4% and 69.7%, respectively. Integration with existing native cache-pruning methods further pushes compression while improving reconstruction quality on NeuralRGBD. Our optimized StreamVGGT backend achieves $5.05\times$ physical KV compression and 23.1% lower latency at batch size one. Under a fixed memory budget on the same GPU, it supports…

ov.problema: I transformer per la geometria visiva in streaming conservano stati key-value (KV) come memoria geometrica tra viste diverse, ma la cache cresce e limita l'inferenza su sequenze lunghe. La quantizzazione della KV in questo contesto presenta sfide specifiche.
ov.idea: Gli autori caratterizzano la quantizzazione KV nella geometria in streaming e individuano due problemi collegati: sensibilità geometrica non uniforme e disallineamento tra cache e geometria. Propongono QuantStream3D, con quantizzazione KV a precisione mista guidata dalla geometria (protegge le evidenze cross-view sensibili) e distillazione quantization-aware allineata alla geometria (adatta blocchi transformer e teste geometriche sulla storia quantizzata generata dallo studente).
ov.risultati: Su cinque benchmark e due backbone, QuantStream3D ottiene accuratezza geometrica quasi senza perdite nella maggior parte dei casi con cache KV prevalentemente a 2 bit, e molte configurazioni superano l'inferenza non quantizzata. Rispetto ai quantizzatori KV per LLM, riduce l'errore di traiettoria assoluta TUM e l'errore di completezza NeuralRGBD fino al 57.4% e 69.7%. Il backend StreamVGGT ottimizzato raggiunge una compressione fisica della KV di 5.05×.
ov.limiti: I risultati sono specifici per transformer di geometria visiva in streaming e per i benchmark considerati; il testo non discute la generalizzazione ad altri tipi di modello.

glossario.d: Memoria degli stati chiave-valore usata per evitare di ricalcolare i token passati
Riduzione della precisione numerica dei valori per risparmiare memoria e calcolo
Addestramento di un modello studente per imitare un modello insegnante

2611.27899.abs: Sustaining user experience (UX) quality in large-scale web search requires scalable evaluation. Traditional surveys are slow and bottleneck rapid A/B testing, while automated metrics often lack the granularity to diagnose visual-spatial UX anomalies. To address this, we introduce the Dual-Tier Sentiment Framework, a novel industrial architecture for automated UX attribution. Tier 1 (Macro System) acts as a scalable user sentiment regression detector, utilizing a fine-tuned encoder-decoder LLM (based on Gemini XS) on telemetry features. Through multi-task regularization and contextual feature engineering, this tier achieves a +9.8% PR-AUC gain on over 500,000 held-out records, matching baseline recall on all validated regressions with $\sim$20% relative precision gain among the 12 held-out experiments. In production, it reduces measurement latency from weeks to hours and cuts survey overhead by over 40%. Tier 2 (Micro System) provides granular diagnostics by employing a Multimodal LLM (Gemini 3.0 Pro) to natively assess visual renderings and spatial layout of web result blocks, quantifying "User Toil" as the estimated effort required to reach a satisfactory result. Enhanced by RL-based automated prompt optimization and an AI judge for win/loss patterns, the MLLM yields a $>$6.5% F1 score improvement, offering deep insights into content quality and layout friction. Ultimately, this framework enables scalable, accurate, and diagnostic UX attribution, processing O(100k) live experiment queries daily.

2611.27876.abs: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline. We introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that performs this read end to end without task-specific training. It operates frozen 3D models as tools, acts in 3D through coordinate-labelled views, remembers every lesion across visits in a registry, verifies every model output it relies on, and leaves every number to a deterministic guideline engine. On four public longitudinal CT datasets, LesionAgent tracks more lesions and measures them more accurately than every automatic baseline, and where the same 3D models chained by fixed rules call progression falsely at 33 of 56 follow-ups, it does so twice. On clinical follow-up CTs, it agrees with the radiologists' response at 20 of 23 follow-ups, including every change in response, and without training on DeepLesion, it retrieves more of its lesions than every tracker trained on it (89.0% vs. 87.4%). Its harness, not its LLM, makes the difference: given the same LLM and 3D models but not the harness, Claude Code reaches a detection F1 of 41% and LesionAgent 78%, and an open-weight LLM that can run inside the hospital rises from 6% to 73%. LesionAgent and a napari reading app for any LLM are available at…

ov.problema: Nelle CT longitudinali, i radiologi decidono quali lesioni sono le stesse nel tempo e se una nuova macchia indica progressione, applicando linee guida complesse. I modelli 3D foundation non leggono le scansioni come un radiologo.
ov.idea: LesionAgent è un agente LLM che esegue questa lettura end-to-end senza addestramento specifico. Usa modelli 3D congelati come strumenti, agisce in 3D tramite viste con coordinate etichettate, ricorda ogni lesione in un registro, verifica ogni output e lascia i numeri a un motore deterministico di linee guida.
ov.risultati: Su quattro dataset CT longitudinali pubblici, traccia più lesioni e le misura più accuratamente di ogni baseline automatico. Dove modelli 3D incatenati da regole fisse chiamano falsamente progressione in 33 su 56 follow-up, lui lo fa due volte. Su CT clinici, concorda con i radiologi in 20 su 23 follow-up, incluso ogni cambiamento di risposta, e senza addestramento su DeepLesion recupera più lesioni di ogni tracker addestrato su di esso (89,0% vs 87,4%). Il suo harness, non l'LLM, fa la differenza: con stesso LLM e modelli 3D ma senza harness, Claude Code raggiunge F1 di rilevamento del 41% e…

glossario.d: Codice che media l'interazione dell'agente con strumenti e ambiente.
Metrica che combina precisione e richiamo in un unico valore.

2611.27858.abs: Nautical charts encode safety-critical maritime information through standardized symbols, attributes, text, and heterogeneous geometries. Interpreting these charts and assessing the navigational significance of successive chart updates requires recognizing nautical features, determining their spatial relationships, and applying navigational knowledge. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer a promising approach to nautical-chart interpretation, yet systematic evaluation of their fine-grained nautical feature recognition, chart-based spatial reasoning, and application of navigational knowledge to assessing chart changes remains limited. We introduce ENC-QA, a diagnostic benchmark comprising 77,312 questions derived from 6,612 National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Electronic Navigational Charts (ENCs). The benchmark evaluates four complementary capabilities: ENC Perception, Spatial Reasoning, Joint Perception and Spatial Reasoning, and Application. Of these, 8,227 questions form a progressive subset that decomposes selected chart-change cases into linked questions progressing from change detection to criticality assessment, enabling case-level analysis of how models use perceptual and spatial evidence to determine the navigational significance of chart changes. Evaluations of 10 open-weight VLMs reveal substantial limitations in fine-grained nautical feature recognition and feature-grounded spatial reasoning. Controlled evidence interventions show that relevant perceptual and spatial information improves change-criticality accuracy. Our findings establish ENC-QA…

2611.27835.abs: Financial documents combine narrative disclosures, accounting metrics, corporate structures, management commentary, and time-dependent facts, making them difficult to represent using conventional chunk-based retrieval-augmented generation systems. This paper presents an auditable, schema-driven methodology for constructing temporal financial knowledge graphs from page-delimited documents parsed using a general purpose document intelligence service. Overlapping document windows undergo phased large language model extraction of structural entities, quantitative observations, and domain-specific relationships. Candidate graph elements are validated against predefined schemas and consolidated through scope-aware exact, normalized, fuzzy, embedding-based, and LLM-assisted entity resolution. Temporal merge constraints, deterministic edge deduplication, conflict-aware property management, and fine-grained provenance preserve issuer identity, reporting-period validity, and traceability to source evidence. The contributions of this work comprise the proposed methodology for financial knowledge graph construction, the creation of an evidence-grounded temporal knowledge graph from heterogeneous financial documents, and an intrinsic framework for evaluating the quality of the resulting graph. The evaluation framework assesses seven weighted dimensions, two hard validation gates, and structural diagnostics. By separating graph-quality assessment from downstream retrieval and answer generation, the framework supports systematic diagnosis and iterative refinement of the constructed graph.

2611.27810.abs: Audio language models (ALMs) can answer clinical questions from speech, outperforming baselines built on handcrafted acoustic features. Reasoning ALMs generate a chain of thought that refers to properties of the speaker's voice before predicting. Each statement the model makes about the voice needs to be checked against clinicians' perceptual ratings of the same recording. On clinical speech, existing evaluations score only the final answer. We introduce Speech Language Pathologist Bench (SLP-Bench), a benchmark grading each acoustic claim in the chain of thought against clinicians' perceptual ratings of the same recording. It covers five clinician-rated datasets and 25 perceptual dimensions, and assesses claims for factuality, stability under resampling, and consistency across reworded and different questions. Across ten open-weight reasoning ALMs evaluated zero-shot, claim balanced accuracy ranges from 0.52 to 0.58, claims change under resampling and rewording, and the most consistent models are not the most factual. Fine-tuning a 7B ALM with GRPO on a reward for claims that agree with clinicians raises its claim balanced accuracy from 0.54 to 0.60 and its mean kappa from 0.39 to 0.61, while preserving answer accuracy on per-dimension questions. SLP-Bench is available upon request, subject to approval by the providers of each dataset.

2611.27648.abs: Training a humanoid motion tracker by backpropagating imagined returns through a learned world model is fast, because the model gives a first-order policy gradient. We ask how much of that gradient holds in the simulator. On a tracker for the Unitree G1, the $0.5\%$ of imagined rollouts with the largest gradients carry $22\%$ of the summed gradient norm, yet neither a second rollout from the same state nor the simulator confirms them. When the actions are moved along the model's gradient, the simulator returns 94% of the predicted change in return where the gradient norm is below the batch median, 48% between 3 and 10 times the median, and 1% above 30 times; the part of a gradient that either check confirms stops growing at a few times the median. We therefore cap each rollout's action-gradient norm at 10 times the batch median, draw imagination starts in proportion to their predicted gradient norm so that the cap removes less, and reset episodes where the world model and critic predict the lowest return. Trained on 223 hours of motion and tested on 353 motions that no actor performed in training, the method raises the normalized return of SuperMimic, the baseline it builds on, from 0.953 to 0.967 and the lowest $1\%$ of test clips from 0.65 to 0.76, halves the test clips that fall persistently, from 15--18 to 7--10, and reaches the baseline's final return in 40% of the baseline's iterations and half its training time. On LAFAN1, trained and evaluated on the same clips as prior work, it reaches 0.935 against 0.906.

2611.27504.abs: Large language models behave differently across languages, and are noticeably less safe in lower-resource languages. This gap is well established behaviorally, but not mechanistically. Directions in activation space, including the assistant persona direction, are almost always extracted from English and assumed to generalize across languages. We extract the assistant persona direction in 31 languages in Qwen3-32B, and find that the resulting axes differ substantially: their cosine similarity to the English axis ranges from 0.378 to 0.911. Moreover, each language's assistant persona direction and its magnitude are correlated with the language's resource level. We also find that the model's default assistant state is farther from the helpful assistant pole in lower-resource languages. Finally, steering against a language's own axis amplifies persona-based jailbreak more than steering against the English axis. These results indicate that the model does not carry a single assistant representation across languages. More broadly, the assistant persona may need to be an explicit target of multilingual alignment.

ov.problema: I modelli linguistici si comportano diversamente a seconda della lingua e sono meno sicuri in lingue a basse risorse. Questa differenza è nota a livello comportamentale, ma non se ne conosce il meccanismo interno.
ov.idea: Gli autori estraggono la direzione della 'persona assistente' (una direzione nello spazio delle attivazioni che rappresenta il comportamento da assistente) in 31 lingue su Qwen3-32B. Scoprono che gli assi differiscono sostanzialmente: la similarità coseno con l'asse inglese va da 0.378 a 0.911. Inoltre, la direzione e la sua magnitudine correlano con il livello di risorse della lingua.
ov.risultati: Il modello non ha una singola rappresentazione di assistente per tutte le lingue; guidare contro l'asse di una lingua amplifica il jailbreak basato sulla persona più che guidare contro l'asse inglese.
ov.limiti: Il testo non riporta limiti espliciti.

glossario.d: Vettore nello spazio delle attivazioni che rappresenta una caratteristica.
Misura della somiglianza tra due vettori, da -1 a 1.
Tecnica per aggirare le restrizioni di sicurezza di un modello.

2611.27398.abs: We introduce Transformation Tracking and Understanding (TTU), extending video object tracking to environments where objects undergo physical assemblies and disassemblies. TTU requires continuously tracking objects through transformations, identifying new entities, maintaining a state graph of their relationships, and assigning semantic labels to transformations. While foundation models (e.g., SAM 2/3) maintain tracklets through appearance changes, they cannot update semantic identities as objects physically evolve. Prior work addresses only disassemblies, relying on expensive searches triggered only when tracking fails. We propose Tracking Instances via Proposals and Overlaps (TIPO), a training-free framework that continuously infers transformations via a generate-evaluate-judge pipeline. TIPO generates split and merge proposals from disjoint mask components, scores them against mask-decoder priors using inner and external overlap, and queries an MLLM on the top proposal for visual verification and semantic labeling. To benchmark TTU, we curate Video Instances, States, and Transformation Annotations (VISTA), a dataset including state graphs with 124 assembly and 132 disassembly events across 50 sequences and over 26,000 frames. TIPO achieves state-of-the-art tracking and state-graph accuracy on VISTA, while operating 6times to 15times faster than prior methods. Project page: https://davidegardenal.github.io/tipo-tracking

ov.problema: Il tracciamento di oggetti in video deve gestire trasformazioni fisiche come assemblaggi e disassemblaggi, mantenendo l'identità semantica degli oggetti. I modelli foundation mantengono tracce attraverso cambiamenti di aspetto, ma non aggiornano le identità semantiche quando gli oggetti si trasformano.
ov.idea: TIPO è un framework training-free che inferisce continuamente trasformazioni tramite una pipeline genera-valuta-giudica. Genera proposte di split e merge da componenti di maschere disgiunte, le valuta rispetto a prior del decoder di maschere usando sovrapposizione interna ed esterna, e interroga un MLLM sulla proposta migliore per verifica visiva ed etichettatura semantica.
ov.risultati: Su VISTA, TIPO raggiunge accuratezza allo stato dell'arte nel tracciamento e nei grafi di stato, operando da 6 a 15 volte più velocemente dei metodi precedenti.

glossario.d: Sequenza di rilevamenti dello stesso oggetto nel tempo.
Modello linguistico multimodale, capace di elaborare testo e immagini.
Metodo che non richiede addestramento aggiuntivo.

2611.27288.abs: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has become an important component in the post-training of diffusion models. In practice, however, standard RL often improves the target reward without reliably preserving holistic generation quality, leading to unstable reward-quality trade-offs that we view as a form of reward hacking. Since Classifier-Free Guidance (CFG) is known to improve visual clarity, prompt alignment, and perceptual quality in generation, we investigate whether its underlying structure can serve as a useful prior during RL. We present a unified geometric view that interprets both CFG and RL as correction vectors in a common prediction space, and identify the projection of the RL-induced correction onto the pretrained CFG correction as a useful diagnostic of quality-related structural preservation. Geometric analysis and rotation intervention further show that the pretrained CFG direction carries information useful for generation quality that reward-driven RL updates do not necessarily preserve. Based on this insight, we propose Conditional Contrast Regularization (CCR), which uses the frozen reference model's conditional contrast as a local structural prior during RL. Experiments across multiple reward settings and backbones show that CCR more consistently preserves generation quality while maintaining competitive reward, yielding a better reward-quality trade-off than standard RL and generic regularization methods.

2611.27959.abs: Hyperparameter optimization (HPO) is essential for high predictive performance, but its computational cost becomes prohibitive when candidate configurations require repeated training on large datasets. This paper proposes a ranking-preserving coreset (RPC) selection framework for accelerating evolutionary HPO. The method constructs a compact coreset that preserves the relative ranking of hyperparameter configurations observed on the full training data. Coreset selection is formulated as an evolutionary optimization problem that maximizes Spearman rank correlation between full-data and subset-based configuration rankings while penalizing subset size. The selected coreset is then used for HPO with three evolutionary algorithms: Genetic Algorithm (GA), Cross-generational elitist Selection, Heterogeneous Recombination and Cataclysmic Mutation (CHC), and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). Experiments on seven tabular, two text, and two image benchmark datasets show that RPC substantially reduces HPO time while maintaining test accuracy comparable to full-dataset HPO across decision tree, text classification, and image classification tasks. Across datasets and optimizers, HPO-stage speedups range from approximately 1.14x to 8.80x, while the one-time coreset construction cost is accounted for separately through end-to-end runtime and break-even analysis. On 20 held-out configurations excluded from coreset construction, RPC achieves higher ranking correlation than same-size random sampling on 8 of 11 datasets (dataset-level Wilcoxon signed-rank test, p = 0.014). These results show…

2611.27951.abs: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. Building on block-wise tail refinement and fixed-support transport topology (arXiv:2605.08123, arXiv:2609.07954), we introduce Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT): (1) bounded-support capacity gating via simplex sparsemax ($O(L\log L)$) or sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$), driving excess distractor mass to zero; (2) a three-sweep $1+2$ annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule that damps bipartite residuals; (3) an exact rank-$(D+2R+1)$ One-Reference-Tile adjoint in batched split-factor Triton kernels (BF16 Tensor Cores, FP32 potentials); and (4) a chunked exclusive-prefix causal variant with verified zero future leakage. On NVIDIA L4, sparsemax THOT trained at $L=128$ reaches 97.40% zero-shot recall of fixed bindings at $L=262{,}144$ under pure task loss ($α=0$) and 98.83% at $α=0.05$ (matched by $O(L)$ thresholded ReLU at $α=0.05$, vs. 80.60% at $α=0$), while softmax-gated hub OT drops to 3.52%. In bidirectional operator microbenchmarks, our kernel runs forward+VJP in 100.1 ms at $H=8, D=64, L=262\mathrm{K}$ (2.2x faster with 4.0x smaller compiler temporaries than latent softmax) and 1.34 ms vs. 4.37 ms for cuDNN FlashAttention at $L=4{,}096$; multi-layer LM…

2611.27931.abs: Video corpus moment retrieval asks a system to find, in a large collection of untrimmed videos with subtitles, the video and the time interval that a natural-language query describes. We find that most top-ranked errors of a strong corpus-level scorer come from choosing the wrong video, not from imprecise boundaries, and that re-weighting the evidence the scorer already uses does not fix them. We present DiTraR, which addresses video selection from two complementary directions. A witness-interval scorer decomposes the query into probes and scores every candidate interval of every corpus video exactly; a multi-scorer energy ensemble averages the energies of independently trained scorers before one exhaustive search; and a transcript verifier, a frozen language model that reads the time-stamped dialogue of the highest-ranked videos, re-orders the moments without changing their boundaries. With all settings frozen on development data and a single evaluation, DiTraR reaches 24.36 and 13.55 R@1 at IoU 0.5 and 0.7 on the TVR validation split. The ensemble improves queries about visual content, the verifier improves queries about dialogue, and their gains largely add up.

2611.27905.abs: Anthropomorphic non-human characters have long been used to convey hateful messages targeting human groups, from Nazi-era propaganda to recent AI-generated imagery on social media. However, the safety risks posed by such imagery remain largely unexplored. We thus conduct the first systematic study of hateful image generation and detection involving anthropomorphic non-human characters. We construct a benchmark from conservatively screened source scenes, covering five character types and three image generation tasks: text-to-image generation, image editing, and conversational image generation. Across 14,250 scheduled queries, image generation systems produce images for 92.1\% of queries, of which 95.9\% contain hateful content. We further collect 4,370 hateful images and evaluate five popular hateful-content detectors. Even the strongest detector, GPT-5.5, identifies only 73.9\% of hateful images, while most detect fewer than 58\%. Our analysis reveals that existing detectors often misclassify hateful images as benign when their main subjects are non-human characters. We explore two effective mitigation approaches: a training-free pipeline that maps non-human characters back to human representations before classification and a detector fine-tuned for this type of hateful content. These approaches achieve F1 scores of 0.962 and 0.979, respectively. Our findings expose significant safety gaps in both image generation and hateful-content detection. Disclaimer: This paper contains hateful text and imagery.

2611.27491.abs: Tokenization represents one of the most crucial steps in mulilingual NLP pipelines. Yet, tokenizers routinely under-allocate vocabulary to low-resource languages. While improved allocation leads to better performance, it remains poorly understood how tokenization shapes cross-lingual representations and transfer during pretraining. To address this, we pretrain 39 mono- and bilingual 1B decoder-only models on FineWeb2-HQ across English, German, French, Arabic and Chinese, varying only the tokenizer. Our results demonstrate that improved vocabulary allocation (i) substantially raises cross-lingual representation alignment in early-to-mid layers, an effect that prior work measuring only the output layer could not observe, (ii) increases cross-lingual parametric knowledge sharing in feed-forward neurons, supported by correlational and causal evidence, and (iii) an alignment-transfer dissociation, where cross-lingual transfer remains essentially unchanged despite higher alignment. Moreover, transfer is significantly lower for cross-script bilinguals even under fair vocabulary allocation, indicating that the script barrier is not merely a tokenizer artifact. All of our checkpoints and code are publicly available.

ov.problema: I tokenizer allocano poca vocabolaria alle lingue a basse risorse, ma non è chiaro come la tokenizzazione plasmi le rappresentazioni cross-lingua e il transfer durante il pretraining.
ov.idea: Gli autori pre-addestrano 39 modelli decoder-only da 1B mono- e bilingue su FineWeb2-HQ in inglese, tedesco, francese, arabo e cinese, variando solo il tokenizer. Misurano allineamento delle rappresentazioni, condivisione di conoscenza nei neuroni feed-forward e transfer cross-lingua.
ov.risultati: Una migliore allocazione della vocabolaria (i) aumenta sostanzialmente l'allineamento cross-lingua negli strati iniziali e intermedi, (ii) aumenta la condivisione di conoscenza parametrica nei neuroni feed-forward, con evidenza correlazionale e causale, e (iii) mostra una dissociazione allineamento-transfer: il transfer resta essenzialmente invariato nonostante l'allineamento maggiore. Il transfer è significativamente più basso per le coppie bilingui con scritture diverse anche con allocazione equa.
ov.limiti: Lo studio copre cinque lingue e modelli da 1B; i risultati potrebbero non estendersi ad altre lingue o scale.

glossario.d: componente che divide il testo in unità (token) e assegna loro un indice
capacità di usare conoscenza appresa in una lingua su un'altra
quanto rappresentazioni di significati simili in lingue diverse si somigliano

2611.27891.abs: Speculative decoding accelerates language-model inference by preparing candidate continuations before the target model generates them. Its efficiency depends on how well limited drafting computation anticipates the path the target will actually follow. Anticipating this path involves two sources of uncertainty: the target model's predictions and the randomness of sampling. Yet the former requires a target-model forward pass, while the latter can be fixed before drafting. Building on this observation, we introduce DICE (Draw-Informed Candidate Selection), which pre-samples and synchronizes verification randomness across drafting and verification. By combining these known draws with predictions from an existing drafter, DICE allocates computation toward continuations more likely to be used in the current sampling run. This principle guides node selection throughout draft-tree construction and extends to asynchronous prefetching, where DICE predicts which next-round drafts to prepare. Without additional drafter training or changes to the target sampling distribution, DICE achieves state-of-the-art decoding throughput across diverse settings, with speedups of up to 24.6pp over strong baselines.

ov.problema: Il speculative decoding accelera l'inferenza preparando continuazioni candidate prima che il modello target le generi. L'efficienza dipende da quanto bene la bozza anticipa il percorso del target, ma ci sono due fonti di incertezza: le previsioni del target e la casualità del campionamento.
ov.idea: DICE (Draw-Informed Candidate Selection) pre-campiona e sincronizza la casualità della verifica tra drafting e verifica. Combinando questi campioni noti con le previsioni del drafter, alloca la computazione verso continuazioni più probabili nella run di campionamento corrente. Questo principio guida la selezione dei nodi nell'albero di bozza e il prefetching asincrono.
ov.risultati: Senza addestramento aggiuntivo del drafter né modifiche alla distribuzione di campionamento del target, DICE raggiunge throughput di decodifica allo stato dell'arte, con speedup fino a 24,6 punti percentuali rispetto a forti baseline.
ov.limiti: Non specificato nel testo.

glossario.d: Tecnica che usa un modello piccolo (drafter) per proporre token che il modello grande verifica in parallelo.
Modello leggero che genera bozze di continuazione per accelerare il modello target.
Preparazione anticipata delle bozze per il round successivo, sovrapposta alla computazione corrente.

2611.27822.abs: Underwater imaging suffers from wavelength-dependent absorption and scattering that distort scenes and obscure spectral signatures. While RGB restoration improves visual clarity, the outputs remain broadband and tied to the sensor's color space. We introduce a physically grounded framework that lifts underwater restoration to continuous spectral radiance using multi-view hyperspectral imaging. By representing continuous spectra via low-rank basis functions and leveraging multi-distance observations, our framework jointly constrains scene radiance and water parameters. We employ a robust sparse-to-dense pipeline: water parameters are estimated from consistent multi-view matches and then applied globally to invert the light transport model across the full images.
