Memory-based video generation methods preserve what they have already seen, but have no anchor beyond it, where the camera drifts from its path and a text prompt can name objects but not place them. Layout-conditioned methods provide such an anchor and precise control over what appears where, but rely on layouts that are typically authored by hand. Both limitations arise because, beyond what was captured, nothing anchors the video model unless a human authors one. To overcome both, we propose Lyris, a long video generation framework that never leaves the video model without an anchor: a persistent point-cloud memory where the scene has been observed or generated, and a 3D layout that a vision-language model authors where it has not. Our key insight is that the interface between the two models can be surprisingly coarse. A layout of one labeled 3D box per object is simple enough for a vision-language model to author (and for a user to edit), yet expressive enough for a video model to follow once rendered along the camera path. We demonstrate walkthroughs of over three minutes and 50 meters from a single photo, passing through doorways into rooms it never shows. When evaluated on minute-long round trips across four datasets, Lyris outperforms state-of-the-art methods by a wide margin, reducing camera error by 3.8x and improving consistency upon return by 22% on average.

2611.31237.abs: Recent unified multimodal models aim to combine visual understanding and generation within a single model, yet effectively integrating the two capabilities remains challenging. Leveraging pretrained vision-language models offers a way to build on already learned multimodal knowledge, but making this knowledge effectively accessible to visual generation remains nontrivial. We find that a central challenge lies in the heterogeneous visual representations used for understanding and generation. To address this challenge, we introduce Integral, which converts a pretrained vision-language model into a unified multimodal model by constructing a shared visual representation space across the two capabilities. Integral implements this design through two complementary components. Abstraction Fusion constructs shared visual tokens by aggregating hierarchical representations from the frozen vision encoder, while Block-wise MoT introduces a lightweight generative stream that interacts with the vision-language model only at block boundaries. Our approach effectively preserves the pretrained understanding capability while extending it to strong visual generation. Controlled comparisons further demonstrate that sharing visual representations between understanding and generation substantially improves generative learning compared with using a separate visual representation space, despite comparable reconstruction fidelity. These results suggest that representations learned by pretrained vision-language models already provide an effective foundation for visual generation.

ov.problema: I modelli multimodali unificati recenti mirano a combinare comprensione e generazione visiva in un unico modello, ma integrare efficacemente le due capacità resta difficile.
ov.idea: Integral converte un VLM pre-addestrato in un modello multimodale unificato costruendo uno spazio di rappresentazione visiva condiviso tra le due capacità. Usa due componenti: Abstraction Fusion, che costruisce token visivi condivisi aggregando rappresentazioni gerarchiche dall'encoder visivo congelato, e Block-wise MoT, un flusso generativo leggero che interagisce con il VLM solo ai confini dei blocchi.
ov.risultati: L'approccio preserva efficacemente la capacità di comprensione pre-addestrata estendendola a una forte generazione visiva. Confronti controllati mostrano che condividere le rappresentazioni visive tra comprensione e generazione migliora sostanzialmente l'apprendimento generativo rispetto a usare spazi separati, nonostante una fedeltà di ricostruzione comparabile.
ov.limiti: Il testo si interrompe prima di completare le conclusioni e non riporta limiti espliciti.

glossario.d: Modello che comprende sia immagini che testo
Rete che trasforma immagini in rappresentazioni numeriche
Unità elementari in cui un'immagine viene suddivisa per il modello

2611.31233.abs: CLIP-style dual encoders map images and text through two separate towers into a shared embedding space, where the two modalities occupy distinct regions separated by a modality gap. Retrieval fails when wrong matches, or hard negatives, outrank the correct one, and the gap is the usual suspect. Yet removing it post hoc degrades retrieval on every CLIP checkpoint we test. We introduce a paired statistic that identifies directions where the two towers agree more on hard negatives than on matched pairs. Mildly attenuating these directions improves retrieval while largely preserving the gap. We arrive at this correction through weight-space programming: guided by the statistic, an LLM agent inspects both towers and writes closed-form weight edits without backpropagation. Free to edit any component, the agent improves COCO test retrieval on all 13 CLIP checkpoints and edits an output projection in 12 of the 13. We distill and refine its recurring correction into TowerBridge, a closed-form recipe motivated by a first-order analysis of the hard-negative margin. Computed in seconds from 25,000 labelled pairs, it requires no model-specific tuning and leaves the architecture and inference cost unchanged. TowerBridge improves COCO test retrieval by 16.8 RSUM and Flickr30k test retrieval by 6.6 on average across all 21 evaluated CLIP checkpoints, including 8 unseen by the agent, while limiting any drop in ImageNet zero-shot accuracy to 0.5 points. It also reduces hubness on all 21 checkpoints and improves retrieval on 4 of 5 dual encoders from other families.

ov.problema: Nei modelli CLIP (che mappano immagini e testo in uno spazio condiviso), immagini e testo occupano regioni separate (modality gap), causando errori di retrieval quando i negativi difficili superano il match corretto. Rimuovere il gap a posteriori peggiora il retrieval.
ov.idea: Introducono una statistica accoppiata che identifica direzioni in cui i due tower sono più d'accordo sui negativi difficili che sulle coppie corrette. Attenuando lievemente queste direzioni si migliora il retrieval preservando il gap. La correzione è trovata tramite weight-space programming: un agente LLM ispeziona i tower e scrive modifiche ai pesi in forma chiusa, senza backpropagation. Poi distillano la correzione in TowerBridge, una ricetta closed-form basata su un'analisi del margine dei negativi difficili.
ov.risultati: TowerBridge migliora il retrieval su COCO test di 16.8 RSUM e su Flickr30k test di 6.6 in media su 21 checkpoint CLIP, con una perdita massima di 0.5 punti su ImageNet zero-shot. Riduce anche l'hubness su tutti i 21 checkpoint.
ov.limiti: Richiede 25.000 coppie etichettate per il calcolo, ma non necessita di tuning specifico per modello e non cambia architettura o costo di inferenza.

glossario.d: Separazione tra le regioni occupate da immagini e testo nello spazio di embedding condiviso.
Esempi negativi simili al positivo che il modello fatica a distinguere.
Metrica di retrieval che somma i recall su più cutoff.

2611.31225.abs: Dataset distillation (DD) aims to compress a large dataset into a small synthetic one that remains effective for training neural networks. Despite its success in supervised learning, DD remains underexplored in self-supervised learning (SSL), where distilled data must preserve the information needed to learn representations that remain consistent across augmentations. To bridge this gap, we introduce Mutual Information Prototype Alignment (MIPA), an efficient SSL dataset distillation approach that optimizes synthetic images to preserve augmentation-invariant information. Specifically, MIPA treats synthetic images as learnable prototypes and uses a frozen encoder to assign real samples to them based on feature similarity. A synthetic dataset that preserves such augmentation invariance should yield stable prototype assignments across multiple augmented views of the same real image. MIPA encourages this by maximizing mutual information between cross-view assignments while avoiding trivial solutions in which all real samples are assigned to only a few synthetic prototypes. Evaluations on image classification benchmarks show that synthetic data generated by MIPA yield higher-quality representations than existing distillation approaches while reducing time and storage demands during distillation.

2611.31212.abs: High-resolution flood forecasting with full two-dimensional shallow water equation (SWE) solvers remains computationally expensive, even on GPUs. We develop a conditional denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) that forecasts the evolution of 30 m water-depth fields over a four-day horizon for the Des Plaines River watershed, Illinois. The model is trained on SynxFlow SWE simulations of 113 historical storms observed across twelve Midwestern states (2003-2024), each under three antecedent-wetness scenarios, and can optionally be conditioned on coarse 100 m or 150 m hydrodynamic simulations. Because reverse diffusion is stochastic, every forecast is a 20-member ensemble drawn from the same trained model. Coarse conditioning reduces the four-day mean water-depth RMSE of the ensemble mean from 0.170 m to 0.054 m (100 m) and 0.048 m (150 m). The coarser 150 m conditioning also gives the best critical success index (0.839), false alarm ratio, CRPS and Brier score at lower cost, so finer conditioning does not guarantee better skill. Averaging members reduces error by 5-11% relative to a single realization, and the ensemble provides spatially explicit exceedance probabilities, although the ensembles are under-dispersive (spread-to-error ratios 0.35-0.73). On a single GPU, a four-day forecast over 26 non-overlapping patches is 7.8x, 11.0x and 16.3x faster than the 30 m simulation for the 100 m, 150 m and unconditioned configurations, and projected speedups for a 14-day forecast reach 12-49x for one member and 48-58x for 20 members. Physics-guided diffusion models are thus…

2611.31184.abs: Modern visual generative models operate on tokens, and every visual asset they receive, whether an identity, a scribble, a depth map, or a motion video, is tokenized and appended to the input token sequence. Consequently, conditioning quickly dominates the computation cost. Yet most of these tokens carry redundant spatiotemporal information. Our key insight is that identifying what is genuinely new is exactly the problem that classical video codecs have long solved. Thus, we first introduce a codec-based token pruning method that discards redundant tokens. Then, we propose an on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) strategy to train a DiT adapter capable of learning the codec pruning pattern well without quality degradation. Together, they form On-Policy Codec Distillation (CodecOPSD). We scale CodecOPSD to 16 condition modalities on our own video diffusion model, where it prunes 66% of the condition tokens on average with almost no quality drop. Therefore, denoising becomes 2x faster, and the cache memory shrinks by up to 73% in KV cache mode. CodecOPSD also extends to other state-of-the-art pretrained image and video generative models, where its benefit grows further with more conditions, longer frames, and higher resolution.

ov.problema: Nei modelli generativi visivi moderni, ogni condizione (identità, scarabocchio, mappa di profondità, video di movimento) viene tokenizzata e aggiunta alla sequenza di input, facendo crescere rapidamente il costo computazionale. Tuttavia, molti di questi token contengono informazione ridondante.
ov.idea: Gli autori sfruttano l'idea che i codec video classici sanno già identificare l'informazione nuova. Introducono un metodo di pruning (potatura) dei token basato su codec che scarta i token ridondanti, e una strategia di on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) per addestrare un adattatore DiT (Diffusion Transformer) che apprenda il pattern di pruning senza degradare la qualità.
ov.risultati: Su 16 modalità di condizione, CodecOPSD pota in media il 66% dei token di condizione con quasi nessun calo di qualità. Il denoising diventa 2x più veloce e la memoria cache si riduce fino al 73% in modalità KV cache. I benefici crescono con più condizioni, frame più lunghi e risoluzione più alta.
ov.limiti: I risultati sono mostrati su modelli proprietari e alcuni pre-addestrati; non è chiaro se il metodo si applichi senza modifiche a modelli open-weight con quantizzazione.

glossario.d: unità elementare in cui viene suddiviso un input (es. pixel o patch) per il modello
algoritmo di compressione video che rimuove informazione ridondante tra frame
Diffusion Transformer, architettura che usa transformer per modelli diffusivi

2611.31171.abs: Electroencephalography (EEG) decoding is a central route toward brain-computer interfaces for communication, rehabilitation, cognitive assessment, and neurological monitoring. Recent EEG foundation models have substantially advanced reusable signal representations, but their downstream use still typically requires a task-specific decoder, gradient-based adaptation, and validation-driven model selection. We investigate a complementary foundation-model paradigm based on in-context learning: labeled EEG recordings define the decoding task as context, and new recordings are predicted without updating model parameters. We first pair raw EEG features with a pretrained general-purpose in-context predictor. This direct formulation provides a promising starting point, but its performance remains limited and unstable and does not generalize reliably across EEG paradigms. We find that suitable context construction can address these limitations by improving the effective signal-to-noise ratio and exposing temporal and spatial structure. Building on this insight, we introduce a general framework that combines EEG-specific context construction with a frozen in-context predictor and a metric-based context adaptation mechanism, which matches each downstream task to an appropriate context representation without relying on validation data. Across ten datasets spanning seven EEG decoding paradigms, our method achieves the highest mean BAcc among eleven specialized and fine-tuned EEG baselines, without task-specific parameter updates or validation-based model selection. This framework…

2611.31166.abs: The post-training of pretrained large language models, including supervised finetuning (SFT), direct preference optimization (DPO), and reinforcement learning with verifiable reward (RLVR), is very sensitive to the learning rate, and tuning it through grid search is costly in both computation and memory. In this work, we propose \textbf{TipSweep}, a method to transfer the learning rate across the number of trainable transformer blocks. To do so efficiently, we search for the best learning rate by training only the last $k_0$ blocks (in our experiments, typically $k_0=1$), and provide scaling rules that predict the optimal learning rate when training any set of $k$ blocks, including when $k=L$ (the full transformer). Across experiments with models ranging from 1 to 7 billion parameters, we observe that the optimal learning rate follows precision-dependent scaling rules: the optimal rate scales approximately as $k^{-1}$ with float32 (FP32) master weights, but as $k^{-1/2}$ when updates are applied directly to bfloat16 (BF16) weights without a master copy. We explain both rules using an analytical model that accounts for update rounding, under assumptions supported by profiling experiments. Finally, we develop two prototypes of the learning rate search for a 6.7-billion-parameter model. The first fits the search on a single consumer GPU with 16 GiB of memory. The second speeds up the search on a high-end GPU by evaluating all candidate learning rates in a single pass over the data, so that a five-candidate search takes about half the GPU hours of one full-depth ($k=L$) run.

ov.problema: Il post-training di LLM (SFT, DPO, RLVR) è molto sensibile al learning rate, ma trovare quello giusto con grid search costa molta memoria e calcolo.
ov.idea: TipSweep cerca il learning rate ottimale addestrando solo gli ultimi k0 blocchi (tipicamente 1) e poi usa regole di scala per prevedere il learning rate ottimale quando si addestrano k blocchi, incluso il modello completo. Le regole dipendono dalla precisione: con pesi master FP32 scala come k^{-1}, con aggiornamenti diretti in BF16 scala come k^{-1/2}.
ov.risultati: Sperimentato su modelli da 1 a 7 miliardi di parametri. Due prototipi per un modello da 6.7B: uno su GPU consumer da 16 GiB, l'altro più veloce su GPU high-end valutando tutti i learning rate in un singolo passaggio.

glossario.d: Iperparametro che controlla quanto il modello aggiorna i pesi ad ogni passo.
Supervised Fine-Tuning: addestramento supervisionato su esempi etichettati.
Formato numerico a 16 bit con esponente a 8 bit, usato per ridurre memoria.

2611.31139.abs: Laya is a 421M-parameter encoder that answers a question about a text in one pass: each answer option, written as a name plus a description, gets a marker token, and one score is read from the network at each marker. We first confirm that such models can follow an option's name when it contradicts the description; the question is where in the network this happens. We locate it. On 951 synthetic questions we move each name onto another option's description and count how often the model picks the option with the right name (the name shortcut): 53% for the released checkpoint, 59% for our fine-tune v1, 11% for a fine-tune with name randomisation. On a 320-item sample, blocking attention from each marker to its own name tokens in layers 14 to 17 of 28 cuts v1's shortcut from 67% to 16% (19% on two schemas held out from component selection) while accuracy with the original names stays at 90%; blocking marker edges to the question, other options or text has no effect. No single head matters (largest effect 9 points), and restoring clean marker states undoes the swap from layer 16. Attention mass tracks the window by layer but not by head. Repeated on 5 checkpoints (released, fine-tuned, name-randomised, and a pair trained without two schemas), the knockout finds similar layers; in the name-randomised ones, blocking the description edges instead brings the shortcut back to 56-58%, so the read persists and is outvoted. Marker states decode the name from layer 0; a one-direction probe erasure changed nothing but was weaker than a random edit. Copying layers 0-13 or 14-27 of a…

ov.problema: Laya è un encoder da 421M parametri che risponde a una domanda su un testo in un solo passaggio: ogni opzione di risposta, scritta come nome più descrizione, riceve un token marcatore e un punteggio viene letto dalla rete a ciascun marcatore. Gli autori vogliono capire dove nella rete il modello segue il nome dell'opzione quando contraddice la descrizione.
ov.idea: Su 951 domande sintetiche spostano ogni nome sulla descrizione di un'altra opzione e contano quanto spesso il modello sceglie l'opzione con il nome giusto (scorciatoia del nome). Poi bloccano l'attenzione da ciascun marcatore ai propri token del nome nei layer 14-17 di 28 per localizzare il fenomeno.
ov.risultati: La scorciatoia del nome è del 53% per il checkpoint rilasciato, 59% per il fine-tune v1, 11% per un fine-tune con randomizzazione dei nomi. Su un campione di 320 elementi, bloccare l'attenzione dai marcatori ai propri token del nome nei layer 14-17 riduce la scorciatoia di v1 dal 67% al 16% (19% su due schemi tenuti fuori dalla selezione dei componenti), mentre l'accuratezza con i nomi originali resta al 90%.
ov.limiti: Il testo si interrompe prima di completare le conclusioni e non riporta limiti espliciti.

glossario.d: Rete che trasforma un input in una rappresentazione numerica
Token speciale inserito prima di ogni opzione di risposta
Uno dei livelli che compongono una rete neurale

2611.31079.abs: A generalist manipulation policy should perform new tasks, operate in unfamiliar scenes, and transfer skills across robot embodiments. We present Wrist Video Policy (WVP), a closed-loop manipulation framework that learns how manipulation unfolds through video prediction and recovers executable motion through geometric estimation. Our key idea is to represent robot motion through wrist-camera trajectories, which determine the corresponding end-effector poses through a fixed hand-eye transformation. We pair a video generator that predicts future wrist views with a pose estimator adapted from a pretrained 3D model to recover the corresponding camera trajectories. Model stitching maps the generator's predicted latents directly into the estimator's intermediate feature space, bypassing RGB decoding. This decomposition allows task knowledge to expand through broad human and robot video data while reusing geometric motion estimation across tasks and embodiments. The resulting pose estimator transfers across Franka Panda, PiPER-X, and Galaxea R1 Pro without further fine-tuning. Across tabletop and laundry-room settings, WVP generalizes to tasks ranging from precise grasping and inserting to handling deformable objects, achieving a success rate of over 50% in zero-shot out-of-distribution evaluations. Our project page is at https://wrist-video-policy.github.io.

2611.31051.abs: Annually 1.9 million deaths and 89.7 million disability-adjusted life years are caused by exposure to agents during work (e.g., welding fumes, silica dust, and noise pollution). To improve worker health, high-quality exposure assessments are crucial. Therefore, free-text job descriptions from large-scale occupational cohorts are manually standardized through occupational classifications and linked to hazardous exposures using Job Exposure Matrices (JEM). However, manual coding is slow, unreliable (i.e., 44-89% inter-coder reliability), and costly, due to i) short, ambiguous free-text job descriptions, ii) classifications containing hundreds to thousands of categories, and iii) the absence of gold standards. With 46%-79% accuracy, state-of-the-art automatic occupational coding tools achieve classification performance on human level. However, their performance drops to 17-26% on out-of-distribution datasets. Furthermore, their supervised architectures limit them to occupational classifications present in the training set. Consequently, JEM using other classifications are incompatible, leaving vital exposure-response associations unexplored. Our Retrieval-Augmented Generation framework, OPERAG, enables classification into any occupational classification without expert-labelled databases. It retrieves coding index information and combines this with Large Language Model-based classification. Validated on AsiaLymph's 36,062 real-world job descriptions, OPERAG achieved 42.6% occupational classification accuracy on the 4th coding level, substantially outperforming existing tools…

2611.30907.abs: World models facilitate planning and control in robotic manipulation by enabling agents to anticipate the consequences of their actions. However, they typically rely on action-labelled interaction data that is costly to acquire and difficult to scale. These models are also often tied to the specific embodiment they were trained on, limiting transferability to previously unseen robot morphologies. We introduce a 3D latent-action world model that learns continuous action representations directly from point-cloud observations of retargeted human manipulation demonstrations. A contrastive objective is used to encourage consistent representations of motion across embodiments. The resulting unified latent action space serves directly as the search space for model-predictive control, where sampled latent actions condition particle-based future predictions. Executable robot commands are then recovered from the predicted geometric motion without requiring an embodiment-specific action decoder. Through extensive evaluations, we demonstrate that the learned latent actions exhibit controllable and compositional motion, transfer to unseen robot embodiments, and support zero-shot manipulation with unseen gripper geometries. Following task-agnostic adaptation, our model achieves 90%, 92%, and 60% success on reaching, grasping, and placing, respectively, compared with DexWM's reported 72%, 58%, and 28%. Finally, we demonstrate zero-shot real-world manipulation with an unseen dexterous hand, achieving an 86% success rate across 50 trials on five diverse tasks involving pushing, grasping,…

2611.30006.abs: Selecting a strategy by testing it against an opponent is common in game-playing AI, red-teaming of language models, and safety evaluations of AI agents. In many of these settings, the opponent adapts to what it observes, so a strategy that keeps winning in practice may already have stopped working by the time it is used. Motivated by these settings, we study a player who tries strategies in practice games against an adaptive opponent, decides when to stop, and then either selects one strategy for the next game or abstains. The goal is to select a strategy that meets a target win probability while rarely selecting one that has already fallen below it. For a single strategy, we propose the Sequential Private Accumulated-excess Rule (SPAR), which accumulates evidence through a capped likelihood ratio and selects the strategy once this evidence reaches a privately drawn uniform threshold. We show that the stopping time must involve such private randomness. The number of games SPAR needs is inversely proportional to the error tolerance, and this rate is optimal even when the opponent happens not to adapt. To select among multiple strategies, we introduce Screen-then-SPAR, which screens candidates in stages before applying SPAR. The procedure adapts to the best strategy's unknown initial margin above the target and achieves the minimax rate up to logarithmic factors. The performance of Screen-then-SPAR is demonstrated through simulations and two real-data studies, one using recorded coding-agent attacks from MonitoringBench and the other using rock-paper-scissors matches…

2611.31126.abs: Vision-language-action (VLA) models leverage pretrained vision-language representations for instruction-conditioned robot control, yet their understanding of task-relevant 3D relations and how these relations evolve during manipulation remains largely implicit. To address this challenge, we introduce WeaveVLA, a framework that enhances VLA action generation by explicitly modeling task-relevant relative 3D relations and maintaining relational context across observations. WeaveVLA employs a task-conditioned sparse graph neural network to encode relative 3D relations among objects, the gripper, and nearby references. Pair-specific recurrent edge states integrate geometric evidence across observations to maintain evolving spatial context. A learned-query readout summarizes the updated graph representations into compact relational tokens, which condition the action expert alongside the original vision-language context. An auxiliary geometry reconstruction objective further encourages spatial structure preservation. We instantiate WeaveVLA on StarVLA-GR00T and π_{0.5}, achieving over 98\% average success on LIBERO with both backbones. On LIBERO-Plus, WeaveVLA improves success from 74.9\% to 82.0\% and from 85.7\% to 87.8\%, respectively, with additional improvements on CALVIN DrightarrowD. On three real-world tasks, the StarVLA-GR00T-based variant improves average success from 55.6\% to 70.0\% under standard conditions and from 33.3\% to 53.3\% under OOD perturbations, surpassing the π_{0.5} baseline in both settings.

2611.31165.abs: When should additional reasoning or verification replace a majority-vote answer? We call such a replacement an override. We examine two obstacles: the availability of correct alternatives and the reliability of methods that produce or select them. We compare additional reasoning, executed programs, and cross-model reasoning on 150 competition-mathematics questions with three open reasoning models. Starting from a majority vote over 16 responses, we measure how often overrides occur and how many errors they correct or introduce across agreement thresholds. When the vote is incorrect, the correct answer is often absent from the original responses. Additional same-model reasoning rarely overrides, while executed programs correct more errors than they introduce at every evaluated threshold. Cross-model overrides improve some weaker baselines but do not establish an advantage over the more accurate model alone, even with only eight standalone responses. Stricter agreement reduces how often overrides occur but does not consistently increase the fraction that correct errors. At the strictest thresholds, overrides occur on few distinct questions, limiting conclusions about their reliability.

2611.31215.abs: Humans explore unfamiliar spaces with purpose, deciding where to look until they have gathered the evidence a spatial question requires. However, can vision-language models (VLMs), which reason increasingly well over curated images and videos, also seek in space when the evidence is not handed to them? We present ActSpace-Bench, a benchmark of 994 questions across 234 exploration episodes in 72 real-scanned indoor scenes, where a model starts from a single view, navigates real captured frames, and must gather evidence before answering. To assess whether such exploration is purposeful, we introduce a controlled evaluation protocol that fixes each model as the reasoner and compares its own exploration against a same-budget random walk and an oracle route, separating evidence seeking from spatial reasoning. Every question is verified to require exploration and answered from 3D annotations, masked-evidence questions test whether models know when to abstain, and over 95% of sampled questions are confirmed correct by human verification. Evaluations of 23 proprietary, open-weight, and spatially specialized VLMs reveal that the strongest models do seek evidence with purpose but lose much of it to limited memory, whereas weaker and specialized models explore no better than a random walk or fail to reason over the evidence they are given, pointing to memory and evidence-grounded reasoning as the next targets for active spatial intelligence.

2611.31228.abs: Prompting language models to verbalize stepwise numerical confidence during generation is an increasingly popular approach for triggering backtracking and error correction in agentic reasoning. This strategy presupposes two capabilities: (1) in-situ monitoring fidelity (does confidence drop when an error occurs?) and (2) downstream steering control (does an uncertainty token causally steer the model to repair its error?). We evaluated four open-weights models (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, Mistral-7B, and Phi-4, 14.7B) across 15,200 math benchmark attempts, isolating 2,017 reasoning errors within each model's capability frontier. Applying 27,568 counterfactual continuations across these failure points, we demonstrate a consistent decoupling between monitoring and control. On monitoring, all four models fail to detect their own errors. Verbalized confidence does not distinguish mistake steps from sound reasoning, yielding near-chance within-position AUROCs between 0.500 and 0.561. Even at a model's first reasoning error, trajectory confidence remains saturated at 95.1% to 99.9%, with noticeable drops ($\ge 10$ points) appearing on fewer than 9% of errors in Llama and under 1.6% in the other three models. In contrast, models respond readily to external uncertainty: injecting a low-confidence tag (10%) at the error step significantly increases downstream correction across all models (+3.7 to +22.5 points over format-matched 95% certainty; all $p \le 0.0022$), reaching up to 38.5% under active rethinking instructions. However, injecting doubt onto already-correct steps causes…

ov.problema: Si assume che i modelli linguistici possano monitorare la propria incertezza durante la generazione per correggere errori, ma non è chiaro se ci riescano davvero.
ov.idea: Gli autori testano quattro modelli open-weight su 15.200 tentativi di problemi matematici, isolando 2.017 errori di ragionamento. Applicano 27.568 continuazioni controfattuali per verificare se la confidenza verbale cala in caso di errore e se un token di incertezza iniettato dall'esterno può guidare la correzione.
ov.risultati: Tutti i modelli falliscono nel rilevare i propri errori: AUROC vicino al caso (0.500-0.561) e confidenza satura al 95.1%-99.9% anche al primo errore. Iniettando un tag di bassa confidenza (10%) al passo errato, la correzione aumenta da +3.7 a +22.5 punti rispetto a un tag di certezza al 95%.
ov.limiti: I modelli non riescono a monitorare la propria incertezza in situ, ma rispondono a segnali esterni di incertezza.

glossario.d: Area sotto la curva ROC: misura la capacità di distinguere due classi.
Simbolo o tag che indica bassa confidenza, usato per guidare il modello.

2611.31205.abs: Coding agents can construct and revise robot behavior during execution, but using one agent for the whole robot can delay otherwise independent work. We introduce Asynchronous Coding Agents as Policy (ACAP), an asynchronous framework that organizes one robot as a team of persistent agents. Each member reasons and acts for a configurable control group, such as an arm with its gripper or the torso and chassis, enabling asynchronous reasoning and execution. However, different robot components often have physical dependencies that require coordination. To address this challenge, ACAP introduces a hyper-agent that assigns tasks, coordinates dependencies, and dynamically allocates control between the lead and member agents. This allows independent work to progress concurrently while supporting tightly coupled manipulation when necessary. Across 72 real-world rollouts covering 25 task/platform settings, ACAP reduces task-balanced time cost by 28.2% compared with a single-agent Direct Policy, with improvements across Fully Parallel, Parallel-Sequential, and Collaborative tasks. Across all eight Collaborative settings, ACAP also achieves lower mean time cost than Fixed Delegation, where only member agents can control their assigned groups. An additional 90-rollout study shows lower mean 30-minute-capped time cost than Direct on all six tasks. We further demonstrate mobile manipulation using the same member interface for chassis and torso control. We present the framework and a real-world rollout dataset containing observations, generated programs, actions, and feedback to support…

ov.problema: Gli agenti di coding possono costruire e rivedere il comportamento di un robot durante l'esecuzione, ma usare un solo agente per tutto il robot può ritardare lavori altrimenti indipendenti.
ov.idea: ACAP organizza un robot come una squadra di agenti persistenti: ogni membro ragiona e agisce per un gruppo di controllo configurabile (es. braccio con pinza, o torso e chassis), abilitando ragionamento ed esecuzione asincroni. Un 'hyper-agent' assegna i task, coordina le dipendenze fisiche e alloca dinamicamente il controllo tra agente lead e membri.
ov.risultati: Su 72 rollout reali in 25 configurazioni task/piattaforma, ACAP riduce il costo temporale bilanciato per task del 28,2% rispetto a una Direct Policy a singolo agente, con miglioramenti su task Fully Parallel, Parallel-Sequential e Collaborative. In tutti gli otto setting Collaborative ha costo medio inferiore a Fixed Delegation; uno studio aggiuntivo di 90 rollout mostra costo medio inferiore a Direct in tutti e sei i task.

glossario.d: Agente coordinatore che assegna task e gestisce dipendenze tra i membri.
Una singola esecuzione completa di un task da parte del sistema.
Baseline in cui solo agenti membri controllano i gruppi assegnati, senza riallocazione.

2611.31208.abs: We study how to represent and randomize points in $d$-dimensional Euclidean space to obtain accurate bipartite matchings under metric privacy. Given $n$ private and $n$ public points, we analyze local mechanisms that randomize each private point or its distances to the public points. Using the public points' affine span, we construct a smaller representation that preserves all matching costs. When a trusted server receives the private points, we establish privacy and utility guarantees for Gumbel matching, which randomizes edge costs and releases only the assignment. Through upper bounds and worst-case constructions, we establish the tight rate $Θ\!\left(n\min\{d,\log n\}/\varepsilon\right)$ for expected cost above the nonprivate optimum. Benchmark experiments support $d\approx\log n$ as a practical guide to the transition between directly randomizing point coordinates and using Gumbel matching. Extensions to squared Euclidean costs enable private nonparametric two-sample hypothesis testing. These results show how the application's trust model guides representation and dimension choices for better utility: under local privacy, low-dimensional point representations reduce excess cost, while under central privacy, distance representations achieve the optimal rate even in high dimension.

2611.31195.abs: World action model (WAM) is a promising paradigm for visuomotor control by jointly modeling world dynamics and actions. Notably, existing WAMs often rely on large generative models and iterative sampling which incur substantial latency for action generation, limiting real-time deployment. In particular, there are two root causes of inefficiency in conventional flow matching or diffusion based action models in WAMs: 1) transporting uninformative Gaussian noise into precise actions necessitating multiple ODE steps, and 2) repeatedly injecting task context through expensive cross-attention modules. Our key insight is that jointly learning and aligning the source and action manifolds streamlines the transport between them, substantially accelerating action generation. Building on this insight, we introduce VITA-WAM, a WAM architecture with manifold-aligned flow-matching (VITA flow matching) that directly transports latent observation representations containing visual, language, and proprioceptive information into latent actions. More specifically, a flow latent alignment (FLA) mechanism is employed to facilitate manifold alignment between latent observation and action representations, enabling accurate generation with few ODE steps. The resulting architecture also eliminates costly attention for observation conditioning during repeated denoising steps. Notably, with a single ODE step, VITA-WAM outperforms 10-step FastWAM by 21.47 pp on LIBERO-Plus and by 1.65 pp on LIBERO, achieving these gains through the FLA objective without distillation, while inferring at 55.67~ms…

2611.31112.abs: Parallel speculative decoders propose an entire token block at once, yet one early inconsistency can cause the target to reject its remaining suffix. We introduce Corrective Prefix Attention (CPA), which combines prefix-aware selection with autoregressive supervision to improve these parallel drafts. CPA lets each candidate attend to earlier choices within the block. Fixed candidate shortlists allow all pairwise interactions to be computed before selection, reducing the sequential walk to table lookups, accumulation and lightweight scoring rather than repeated neural evaluations. An auxiliary autoregressive loss trains the shared backbone on clean prefixes without adding an inference pass. Across eight math, code and dialogue benchmarks with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B targets on Ascend NPUs, CPA commits 13--15\% more tokens per verification round than DSpark and 25--26\% more than DFlash. Its mean speedups reach $3.35\times$ and $3.37\times$ under greedy decoding and $2.86\times$ under sampling for both targets. Ablations support both components, while capacity sweeps demonstrate that greater acceptance alone does not guarantee faster decoding. These results motivate correcting parallel proposals with causal information while keeping sequential computation inexpensive.

ov.problema: I decoder speculativi paralleli propongono un blocco di token in una volta, ma un'incoerenza iniziale può far scartare il resto del blocco dal modello target.
ov.idea: Corrective Prefix Attention (CPA) combina selezione consapevole del prefisso con supervisione autoregressiva. Ogni candidato può attendere alle scelte precedenti nel blocco; con shortlist fisse, tutte le interazioni a coppie sono precalcolate, riducendo il costo a look-up e scoring leggero. Una loss autoregressiva ausiliaria addestra il backbone su prefissi puliti senza passaggi extra in inferenza.
ov.risultati: Su otto benchmark (matematica, codice, dialogo) con target Qwen3-4B e Qwen3-8B su NPU Ascend, CPA commette il 13-15% in più di token per round di verifica rispetto a DSpark e il 25-26% in più rispetto a DFlash. Speedup medio: 3.35x e 3.37x in greedy, 2.86x in sampling.

glossario.d: Tecnica per accelerare la generazione proponendo più token e verificandoli in parallelo.
Neural Processing Unit: processore specializzato per reti neurali.

2611.31132.abs: Antimicrobial resistance in Escherichia coli is established in routine practice by culture-based susceptibility testing, which is slow relative to the clinical need for an early treatment decision. Resistance status also leaves a measurable trace in cell morphology, and whole-genome sequencing of clinical isolates is increasingly available, which raises the question of whether colony appearance can be predicted directly from an isolate's genome. We formulate this as a conditional image-generation problem. The assembled contigs of each isolate are encoded into a single 768-dimensional vector by a frozen genomic language model through a segment-contig-isolate aggregation hierarchy, and a conditional Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty synthesizes colony images from this embedding together with the applied antibiotic and the resistance label. We train on 167,356 single-cell images from 22 clinical blood isolates imaged under azithromycin, ciprofloxacin, tetracycline, and a no-drug control, compare seven pretrained convolutional backbones inside the generator, and select ConvNeXt-Tiny on distributional image-quality metrics. The synthetic images are then assessed extrinsically: added to a reduced real training set, they improve per-antibiotic resistance classification, with a significant gain in resistant-class recall.

2611.31163.abs: Preference tuning of text-to-image diffusion models spends most of its compute generating candidate images, yet training prompts are typically sampled uniformly at random, wasting compute generating images that provide too little signal for model alignment. To best utilize the available compute, we study prompt selection, where at each iteration we identify the most useful prompts for preference tuning. We separate prompt selection into a utility score, an estimator of that utility score, and batch selection. Within this framework, we propose Selection by PRedicting Objective-grounded UTility (SPROUT). The utility score is predicted on every prompt in the pool, including unseen prompts, by a text-only model, refit after every iteration on all utilities observed so far. A randomized acceptance rule then turns these predictions into a batch, so no images are generated beyond those used for training. For direct group preference optimization (DGPO), the objective-grounded utility is the norm of the gradient that the objective produces from a prompt's group of images. Fine-tuning Stable Diffusion 1.5 with DGPO on GenEval, SPROUT matches the final score of uniform sampling in about 44% of the iterations and improves the area under the learning curve with respect to both uniform sampling and CGPO, a recent variance-based prompt sampler. The efficiency gains hold under four held-out reward models never used in training, and the ranking of methods carries over to DPG-Bench and T2I-CompBench++. Our code is available at https://github.com/ADDAPT-ML/SPROUT.

2611.31110.abs: Software dependencies execute within the trust boundary of downstream applications, yet provenance, static analysis, and package-level behavioral approaches do not directly determine how a released artifact behaves for a specific program. We present Preflight, a program-scoped pre-execution verifier for Python dependencies that extracts application-referenced symbols, iteratively synthesizes and validates function-level harnesses, executes resolved artifacts in a restricted environment, records behavioral fingerprints, and compares target behavior against prior versions when suitable baselines exist. We evaluate Preflight on four real software-supply-chain incidents under five application contexts, a 100-package benign corpus, and a controlled function-level versus import-only ablation. Preflight returns malicious verdicts in four incident contexts and a clean verdict in the LiteLLM client context, where the affected proxy-server path is not exercised. All 100 evaluated benign packages receive clean verdicts, with zero observed false positives. In a controlled ablation on Ultralytics and ctx, function-level harnesses expose malicious behavior in both incidents, whereas import-only probing exposes neither. Together, these results show that conditioning behavioral verification on the downstream program can expose security-relevant dependency behavior while remaining selective on benign workloads.

2611.29547.abs: Representation alignment markedly accelerates diffusion training, but one-step generators raise a question that diffusion does not: \emph{which training path should receive the loss?} A one-step generator sees two kinds of inputs. Corrupted real images come with their clean counterpart, which provides an instance-paired target. Samples generated from pure noise have no corresponding real image, yet this is where the final model operates. We study this question on Priming, which trains one-step generators from scratch by reconstructing corrupted images and then matching feature distributions with optimal transport. Aligning the generative path, the natural choice, collapses recall ($0.45\!\to\!0.15$--$0.25$) in all 17 configurations we test, including five target constructions and loss weights down to $0.05$. Aligning the paired reconstruction path with a frozen DINOv2 encoder instead helps in every setting we test. A short analysis explains this asymmetry: when the target carries no instance information about the input, the optimal aligned feature is constant within each class, so the loss pulls samples toward class prototypes. A control confirms this: aligning the paired path to a random same-class image instead of the input's own image removes most of the gain. Inside the generator, paired-path alignment creates an interface block through which post-training routes noise, and the image semantics carried through it predict sample quality across 16 models. The resulting recipe, \method, accelerates \emph{both} training stages on ImageNet $256\!\times\!256$: it matches the…

2611.30588.abs: In the manufacturing domain, equipment maintenance tasks depend on expert knowledge. Their documentation is often stored in heterogeneous formats and sources. The enhancement of LLMs with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is promising for bridging the scattered knowledge, but traditional vector-based RAG shows weaknesses with two characteristics which are common in real maintenance queries: complex causal chains and cross-domain synthesis. To address this, we propose SuSi-RAG, a hybrid Graph RAG solution, that matches a user query and each maintenance record using subgraph similarity. This work shows an in-use system: SuSi-RAG has run on an active Bosch production line for more than eight months, handling 10,664 question-answer interactions and demonstrates upper bound answer accuracy of 96.25% (confirmed error rate 3.75%). In a proof-of-concept, SuSi-RAG improves top-1 retrieval accuracy from 61.5% to 96.2% and expert-rated answer quality from 44.9% to 84.1% against a vector-based baseline. We present an integrated operational feedback loop to update SuSi-RAG.

ov.problema: Nella manutenzione industriale, la documentazione è eterogenea e le query reali richiedono catene causali complesse e sintesi tra domini, dove il RAG vettoriale tradizionale mostra debolezze.
ov.idea: SuSi-RAG è una soluzione Graph RAG ibrida che confronta la query utente con ogni record di manutenzione usando la similarità tra sottografi. È un sistema in uso, con un ciclo di feedback operativo per aggiornarlo.
ov.risultati: Ha operato su una linea di produzione Bosch attiva per oltre otto mesi, gestendo 10.664 interazioni domanda-risposta, con accuratezza massima del 96.25% (tasso di errore confermato 3.75%). In un proof-of-concept, migliora l'accuratezza top-1 da 61.5% a 96.2% e la qualità delle risposte valutata da esperti da 44.9% a 84.1% rispetto a una baseline vettoriale.
ov.limiti: I risultati sono specifici al dominio della manutenzione e a una singola linea di produzione; la generalizzabilità ad altri contesti non è dimostrata.

glossario.d: RAG che usa un grafo di conoscenza per recuperare informazioni strutturate.
Porzione di un grafo composta da un sottoinsieme di nodi e archi.
Il primo risultato recuperato dal sistema.

2611.30836.abs: Embodied vision systems rely on complementary sensors to perceive and act as conditions change. Even models that accept arbitrary sensor subsets can exhibit negative fusion: adding a sensor increases prediction error. We propose MakeSense, a multimodal fusion framework that preserves sensor-specific evidence in private streams and combines information through shared bottleneck tokens. Training pairs full and subset views of the same degraded observations, penalizing higher error with more sensors. Where geometry permits, the distance readout uses range measurements alone, while the rest of the prediction draws on all available inputs. Paired tests across five datasets reveal helpful and harmful sensor additions. MakeSense reduces negative fusion on MM-Fi. With lightweight adapters and per-dataset training, the same design improves UAV localization on MMAUD, cooperative 3D detection on V2X-Real, few-shot pose transfer to RELI11D, and command prediction on Humanoid-Everyday, where a world model trained on the frozen core's outputs forecasts future fused states more accurately than a linear baseline at longer tested horizons. MakeSense supports embodied sensing across human activity, aerial systems, robotics, and autonomous driving.

2611.29960.abs: Reinforcement learning can increase the success of automated red teaming but it also narrows the attack vector. This study asks where in the attacker-defender-judge learning loop does the narrowing begin and which mechanisms lead to a narrowing attack. Six mechanisms (defender adaptation, success edge, reward reinforcement, row cap, update size, and measurement) are tested across three experiment arms (co-trained, frozen defender, half learning rate) for twenty-four iterations. A frozen defender narrows attack diversity retention (ADR) earlier 0.496 relative to co-trained 0.891 at iteration twelve. Defender updates delay narrowing but dont prevent it. Successful attacks ("winners") have narrower attack diversity than the full set of generated attacks. Attacks closest to previous winners succeed 10-15 percentage points more often than those closest to previous failures. This winner-neighbor advantage holds after a defender update and for a fixed defender too. Attacks with a common opening have a common-opening advantage of 5-16 percentage points. The training row cap and update size account for little impact on ADR, and attack length accounts for only part of the ADR decrease. Narrowing appears to originate from the success only reward through the group-relative training advantage to the attacker update, with a persistent success edge setting the direction.

2611.31053.abs: Long-horizon embodied tasks involve physical dependencies that may only become clear through interaction. As task understanding deepens, past trials can reveal new information for adaptation and transfer. However, coarse progress feedback cannot identify which physical preconditions held, leaving search unguided, while task-specific optimization easily overfits to individual scenes, making cross-task transfer brittle. We introduce ReWeave, a framework that jointly optimizes an embodied agent harness and an emergent physical task topology from interaction without updating policy weights. Keeping execution policies and perception frozen, ReWeave co-optimizes coupled context, workflows, and control loops. As new evidence revises the topology, ReWeave reprojects past trials onto the updated task understanding, exposing retained progress, regressions, and bottlenecks that guide parent selection and search width. Across tasks, matching verified local mechanisms to unmet preconditions consolidates 72 specialist units into 44 reusable groups (0.34times full concatenation) within a compact shared harness capable of continual learning. ReWeave improves held-out success from 89.00% to 98.75% on LIBERO-PRO and from 25.50% to 58.25% on RoboDojo, while uncovering retained progress in 89% of 159 failed RoboDojo development trials and translating stronger offline reasoning into higher online performance. On eight unseen LIBERO-PRO tasks, the shared harness reaches 51.3% success versus 41.3% for direct distillation, rising to 75.0% after continual learning.

2611.31015.abs: LLMs typically solve complex tasks with chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning, which is also the main tool for monitoring them for misaligned behavior. However, standard transformers can also solve tasks with complete latent reasoning (CLR), carrying out the whole task internally and outputting only the final answer. Theory bounds the depth of CLR, the number of sequential steps it can carry out, and recent work measured it to be shallow. In this work, we ask whether CLR is deep enough for a model to pursue a hidden objective that requires reasoning. Such a model would generate a CoT that appears to solve the given task, while a latent multi-step computation decides its answer based on the hidden objective. First, we show that a simple auxiliary loss allows models to solve a multi-step task latently at least 5x deeper than previously reported. Then, in two common tasks, decision-making and code generation, we train a model to pursue such a hidden objective, which decides a loan or plants a vulnerability. The model's CoT justifies the output with no trace of the hidden objective, and a strong LLM monitor does not flag it. Finally, using activation patching, we find that the latent computation is completed before the model generates its CoT, which takes no part in it. Altogether, we show that a hidden objective that requires reasoning can go unseen by a monitor that reads only the output.

ov.problema: I modelli linguistici di solito mostrano il ragionamento (chain-of-thought, CoT) e questo permette di controllarli. Ma possono anche ragionare internamente senza mostrarlo (CLR). La domanda è: questo ragionamento nascosto è abbastanza profondo da perseguire un obiettivo segreto?
ov.idea: Gli autori usano una semplice perdita ausiliaria per rendere il ragionamento latente (interno) molto più profondo (almeno 5 volte). Poi addestrano il modello a perseguire un obiettivo nascosto (es. decidere un prestito o inserire una vulnerabilità) mentre il CoT generato giustifica l'output senza traccia dell'obiettivo.
ov.risultati: Il ragionamento latente raggiunge profondità 5 volte maggiore del precedente. In due compiti (decisione e generazione di codice) il modello nasconde l'obiettivo: il CoT non lo rivela e un forte monitor LLM non lo segnala. L'activation patching mostra che il calcolo latente è completato prima del CoT.
ov.limiti: Il monitoraggio basato solo sull'output non rileva l'obiettivo nascosto, ma non è chiaro se altri metodi (es. analisi interna) potrebbero farlo.

glossario.d: Ragionamento passo-passo scritto dal modello prima della risposta finale.
Calcolo interno al modello che non produce testo intermedio visibile.
Tecnica per capire quali parti della rete influenzano un output modificando attivazioni interne.

2611.31173.abs: Long-horizon robotic manipulation demands reliable execution across interdependent stages, yet standalone World-Action Models (WAMs) suffer from compounding physical errors, while stateless Vision-Language Model (VLM) supervision incurs prohibitive chunkwise latency and lacks 3D spatial persistence. We present EmboEagle, a closed-loop agentic framework that unifies subtask-conditioned WAM control, latent-space adaptive supervision, and memory-guided geometric recovery. First, we adapt sequential WAMs via decoupled two-stage flow matching that preserves cross-stage visual history while calibrating truncated action supervision at subtask boundaries. Second, without an auxiliary vision encoder, we distill teacher intervention decisions into a lightweight routing gate driven solely by the WAM Action Expert's pre- and post-chunk latent transitions and subtask embeddings. Third, upon invocation, the VLM decouples diagnostic status from discrete routing actions and executes parameterized recovery primitives grounded in structured memory (initial references, active grasp bindings, and tool traces), followed by mandatory post-repair verification. Across RMBench and LIBERO-Mem, EmboEagle achieves 91.3\% and 90.6\% average success, surpassing the strongest baselines by 8.0 and 9.8 percentage points, while boosting real-world success over VoLoAgent under identical executor weights. Moreover, adaptive gating cuts VLM calls by 74.2\% versus chunkwise monitoring (91.3\% vs. 93.7\% success).

2611.31209.abs: Generative Pre-Training (GPT) represents a profound milestone in natural language processing, serving as the foundation for most of today's state-of-the-art large language models. By casting diverse understanding and generation problems into a shared token representation, GPT enables a single architecture and unified optimization loop to master heterogeneous tasks across massive corpora, giving rise to powerful foundation models for natural language. In contrast, 4D spatiotemporal vision lacks a common representational protocol: perception (such as depth and camera estimation) and generation are either handled by separate one-way pipelines or bolted together from unaligned single-modality spaces. In this work, we introduce WorldLatent, a framework that formulates a unified 4D latent space as a common protocol for both world perception and generation. Rather than relying on fragmented, task-specific models or stacked single-modality representations, our framework proposes a multimodal VAE architecture that compresses and fuses complex 4D visual appearance, geometry, and dynamics into a single structured latent representation. Within this formulation, perception and generation operate as complementary denoising processes over the same latent space, enabling one generative model to learn both capabilities simultaneously within a single training loop. Experiments across representative 4D benchmarks verify that our fused latent protocol achieves specialist-level zero-shot 4D perception, coherent 4D generation, and controllable editing from a single model. By demonstrating that…

ov.problema: La visione spazio-temporale 4D manca di una rappresentazione comune: percezione (profondità, camera) e generazione sono gestite da pipeline separate o modelli non allineati, a differenza del linguaggio naturale dove un unico spazio di token unifica i compiti.
ov.idea: WorldLatent propone un VAE multimodale che comprime e fonde aspetto visivo, geometria e dinamiche 4D in un unico spazio latente strutturato. Percezione e generazione diventano processi di denoising complementari sullo stesso spazio latente, permettendo a un solo modello generativo di apprendere entrambe le capacità in un unico ciclo di addestramento.
ov.risultati: Sui benchmark 4D rappresentativi, il protocollo latente fuso raggiunge prestazioni di livello specialistico in percezione 4D zero-shot.
ov.limiti: Il testo non specifica dettagli su architettura, dataset o confronti quantitativi; la valutazione è limitata a benchmark rappresentativi.

glossario.d: Autoencoder variazionale: modello che comprime dati in uno spazio latente probabilistico.
Processo di rimozione progressiva di rumore per generare o ricostruire dati.
Capacità di generalizzare a compiti non visti durante l'addestramento.

2611.31105.abs: Updating an LLM adapter should not require replaying the full interaction history of every active session. Yet reusing key-value (KV) cache entries computed under an earlier version mixes model versions, while full-history re-prefill becomes increasingly costly as histories and session fleets grow. We introduce LiveLora, a model-runtime co-design for exact final-block KV cache migration. Frozen lower decoder blocks and fixed K/V adapter down-projections preserve each token's base projections and low-rank coordinates across adapter versions. The runtime reconstructs candidate K/V, reevaluates the latest token through the final block, and commits the adapter, cache, and next-token logits together. We prove continuation equivalence to full-history re-prefill in exact arithmetic under the stated model assumptions. On Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, median paired publication speedups over full-history re-prefill average $68.98\times$ across five runs for 32 active sessions with 8K tokens each. Serving benchmarks show approximately 4.8% decoding overhead relative to native cached decoding. Compared with retained-boundary replay, compact retention gives a $3.42\times$ reduction in additional session storage at 8K, with similar measured publication-plus-decoding cost. LiveLora allows persistent LLM agents to adopt new adapter versions without replaying their full interaction histories.

ov.problema: Quando un agente LLM persistente aggiorna il proprio adapter LoRA, riusare la KV cache calcolata con la versione precedente mescola versioni del modello, mentre rifare il prefill dell'intera cronologia diventa sempre più costoso al crescere delle sessioni.
ov.idea: LiveLoRA sfrutta il fatto che i blocchi inferiori del decoder sono congelati e le down-projection K/V dell'adapter sono fisse: così le proiezioni base e le coordinate low-rank di ogni token restano valide tra versioni. Il runtime ricostruisce K/V candidati, rivaluta l'ultimo token attraverso il blocco finale e committa insieme adapter, cache e logits del prossimo token.
ov.risultati: Su Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, con 32 sessioni attive da 8K token, il guadagno mediano di velocità rispetto al re-prefill completo è in media 68,98× su cinque run; l'overhead di decoding è circa 4,8% rispetto al decoding nativo con cache. La ritenzione compatta riduce di 3,42× lo storage aggiuntivo a 8K rispetto al retained-boundary replay.
ov.limiti: La garanzia di equivalenza vale in aritmetica esatta e sotto le assunzioni dichiarate sul modello (blocchi inferiori congelati, down-projection K/V fisse).

glossario.d: Coppie chiave-valore salvate per ogni token già processato, così il modello non ricalcola il passato.
Adapter a basso rango che modifica un modello congelato con pochi parametri aggiuntivi.
Fase in cui il modello processa l'intera sequenza di input prima di generare.

2611.31198.abs: Recent multimodal search agents use reasoning, vision, and live web search across many turns to answer questions beyond parametric knowledge by orchestrating a small library of hand-crafted search and visual tools. However, the library is laborious to create and maintain, and frozen when new query types, evidence formats, and failure modes are encountered in the wild. Human practitioners, by contrast, cope with insufficient tools by fashioning new ones from familiar parts and reusing them across tasks. Inspired by this, we propose ToolSmith, an automatic tool-generation framework that grows and reuses modules on top of a lean base tool library. We evaluate ToolSmith on three in-domain multimodal search benchmarks and ten out-of-domain benchmarks under a VLM-as-a-Judge protocol. ToolSmith consistently improves over the base library across deployed agents of varying scales, with larger backbones reaping greater gains, demonstrating the scalability of the approach. Our code and data are available at https://threesr.github.io/toolsmith/.

ov.problema: Gli agenti di ricerca multimodale usano una piccola libreria di strumenti di ricerca e visuali creati a mano, che è laboriosa da mantenere e non si adatta a nuovi tipi di query, formati di evidenza o modalità di fallimento.
ov.idea: ToolSmith è un framework automatico di generazione di strumenti che cresce e riutilizza moduli sopra una libreria base snella. Ispirato a come gli umani creano nuovi strumenti da parti familiari, genera automaticamente nuovi strumenti e li riutilizza.
ov.risultati: ToolSmith migliora costantemente rispetto alla libreria base su tre benchmark di ricerca multimodale in-domain e dieci out-of-domain, con guadagni maggiori per backbone più grandi.

glossario.d: Uso di un modello linguistico-visivo per valutare le risposte.
Modello di base su cui si costruiscono componenti aggiuntivi.
Dati o task diversi da quelli visti durante lo sviluppo.

2611.31164.abs: FlowMap distillation offers a natural route to few-step generative modeling by directly learning a teacher's denoising trajectories. Yet for autoregressive (AR) video generation, existing few-step models still rely on distribution matching distillation (DMD) to remain competitive, sacrificing sample diversity and requiring a large bidirectional teacher. In this work, we analyze what limits standalone AR FlowMap distillation and introduce two complementary guidance mechanisms to close this gap: (1) anti-drifting guidance, which helps the AR teacher correct drifted student rollouts by training an auxiliary model to mimic student drift and using it as a negative guidance branch; and (2) motion-aware guidance, which makes motion easier for a FlowMap student to learn by locating motion patches and selectively applying skip-layer guidance. Empirically, our approach applies to $π$-Flow, MeanFlow, and consistency distillation with 1.3B AR teachers, improving generation quality and reducing drift over 30 s rollouts. Notably, our 4-step $π$-Flow students match DMD students distilled from 14B teachers on VBench while preserving the sample diversity of their AR teachers, demonstrating that pure FlowMap distillation is effective for few-step autoregressive video generation.

2611.31089.abs: LLM quantization reduces storage but often degrades predictive fidelity at low bit rates. We propose a training-free, CDF-free, Gaussian-CLT-motivated progressive residual-sign quantization framework that uses randomized orthogonal mixing to promote Gaussian-like residual distributions and improve sign based reconstruction of Transformer weights. Each stage independently normalizes residuals and analytically calibrates reconstruction, progressively recovering quantization errors. The framework enables flexible storage-fidelity trade-offs without learned codebooks, empirical CDFs, or trellis optimization. We evaluate GPT-2 Large and Llama-3-8B across attention and MLP projections. At five residual stages, joint quantization preserves near-baseline predictive fidelity, achieving perplexities of 32.16 and 12.73, compared with full-precision values of 29.89 and 11.07, respectively. Ablations further demonstrate that orthogonal mixing substantially improves reconstruction over identity-based sign coding, while activation-aware scaling improves output fidelity and reduced-precision statistics lower storage overhead with negligible perplexity degradation. Comparisons with conventional quantizers establish the method's progressive fidelity recovery and characterize its storage-quality and runtime trade-offs. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of orthogonally mixed residual-sign coding for flexible, training-free Transformer weight compression.

ov.problema: La quantizzazione dei LLM riduce lo storage ma degrada la fedeltà predittiva a bassi bit rate. I metodi esistenti spesso richiedono codebook appresi, CDF empiriche o ottimizzazione trellis.
ov.idea: Si propone un framework progressivo di quantizzazione residuo-segno, senza addestramento né CDF, motivato dal CLT gaussiano. Usa mescolamento ortogonale randomizzato per rendere i residui più gaussiani e migliorare la ricostruzione basata sul segno. Ogni stadio normalizza i residui e calibra analiticamente la ricostruzione, recuperando progressivamente l'errore.
ov.risultati: Su GPT-2 Large e Llama-3-8B, con cinque stadi residui, la perplessità congiunta è 32,16 e 12,73, contro 29,89 e 11,07 a piena precisione. Le ablazioni mostrano che il mescolamento ortogonale migliora la ricostruzione rispetto al sign coding identitario, e lo scaling activation-aware migliora la fedeltà.
ov.limiti: Il metodo è testato solo su GPT-2 Large e Llama-3-8B; non è chiaro come si comporti su modelli più grandi o su altri tipi di layer.

glossario.d: codifica dei pesi usando il segno dei residui dopo aver sottratto una stima
teorema del limite centrale: somme di variabili indipendenti tendono a una gaussiana
metrica che misura quanto un modello è incerto nel predire il prossimo token

2611.31113.abs: A training-time attention change is usually judged for zero-shot context extension against a dense baseline beyond the training length at the default temperature, $τ= 1$. The outcome depends on how miscalibrated the baseline is there: the share of perplexity it recovers when its logits are sharpened by one scalar. Under the standard recipe (fp32 master weights), an 8k-trained baseline is 8-15% miscalibrated at 30k in three seed-paired 365M twins; in one of them this makes the block-sparse-trained twin look 7% better, which calibration removes. In pure-bf16 training without master weights the miscalibration is several times larger: an AdamW step ($β_2 = 0.95$) on a gain initialised at 1.0 is below half the bf16 spacing at peak learning rates under $1.7\times10^{-3}$, so gains never move (22 checkpoints), the baseline is 37-58% miscalibrated, and block-sparse pretraining, attention dropout and ALiBi look 6-35% better. Calibrating one temperature per model and length removes all three advantages, leaves ALiBi 5% behind RoPE and keeps part of the gain of a positive control, NTK-aware scaling. Unfreezing the gains reverses the block-sparse advantage at 365M and removes 71-89% of it at 1.2B. We recommend reporting extension results at calibrated temperatures and checking that normalisation gains moved.

2611.30472.abs: Part-aware 3D generation requires not only globally plausible objects but also complete, well-separated semantic parts, yet high-quality part decompositions remain too scarce to support large-scale supervised fine-tuning. We study whether preference fine-tuning based on Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) can adapt a pretrained part-aware generator from limited part-annotated data without architectural changes. We rank candidates generated with different random seeds against ground-truth (GT) geometric metrics, and select the (object, target-part) examples with the largest across-seed quality gap. Each selected example stores a seed pair whose two flow trajectories share one clean GT compositional latent and differ only in Gaussian noise. We derive a reference-relative target-block preference loss from FlowDPO that compares the two trajectories against a frozen reference model. GT flow-matching losses on the target block and complete part set provide absolute supervision, while only the diffusion transformer (DiT) is updated. Human-ranked controls test an alternative ordering source, and synthetic cropping provides controlled loser targets that are incomplete by construction. Among the three training-set scales, the medium-scale setting gives the strongest result on held-out Objaverse and outperforms both the pretrained generator and the reported direct supervised fine-tuning baseline on the multi-part aggregate. Further analysis shows sensitivity to pair ordering, target-part coverage, and the balance between pairwise and GT supervision. Cross-dataset experiments show…

2611.31021.abs: Spatial reasoning across multiple views requires inferring the 3D relations between objects and the camera from 2D observations, which depends on cross-view correspondence and scene geometry that vision-language models (VLMs) do not reliably extract. Pretrained vision encoders already capture this information in their latent features, with CLIP linking objects to image regions, DINOv3 matching semantics across views, and VGGT encoding multi-view geometry. However, VLMs do not benefit from these features when we present them directly in context as grayscale feature images. We therefore propose LatentParse, a training-free framework that parses latent features into explicit spatial evidence for VLMs. In LatentParse, an analyst VLM probes the features of all three encoders with predefined tools that locate objects, track them across views, and measure motion between views. It then distills the results into a concise text report, which is provided together with the images to the VLM to answer the question. We evaluate LatentParse on MMSI-Bench, MV-RoboBench and SPAR-Bench, where it improves all five VLMs over the photo-only baseline by 0.7-2.4 percentage points on average. On MMSI-Bench, it raises Qwen3.8-27B from 34.4% to 39.5%, with the largest improvements of 19.2 percentage points on the camera-related questions. These results suggest that latent features become useful for spatial reasoning once they are parsed into relation evidence, without training. Code is available at https://github.com/Harvard-AI-and-Robotics-Lab/LatentParse.

ov.problema: I modelli visione-linguaggio (VLM) faticano a ragionare sulle relazioni 3D tra oggetti e camera da più viste 2D, perché non estraggono in modo affidabile le corrispondenze tra viste e la geometria della scena.
ov.idea: LatentParse è un framework training-free che usa un VLM 'analista' per interrogare le feature latenti di tre encoder (CLIP, DINOv3, VGGT) con strumenti predefiniti che localizzano oggetti, li tracciano tra viste e misurano il movimento. I risultati vengono distillati in un breve report testuale, fornito insieme alle immagini al VLM per rispondere.
ov.risultati: Su MMSI-Bench, MV-RoboBench e SPAR-Bench migliora tutti e cinque i VLM rispetto alla baseline solo-foto di 0.7-2.4 punti percentuali in media. Su MMSI-Bench, Qwen3.8-27B passa da 34.4% a 39.5%, con il miglioramento maggiore di 19.2 punti sulle domande relative alla camera.
ov.limiti: Il metodo è training-free e si basa su un VLM analista e su strumenti predefiniti; non è chiaro quanto generalizzi oltre i benchmark testati.

glossario.d: Modello che combina visione e linguaggio per rispondere a domande su immagini.
Rappresentazioni interne estratte da un encoder, non direttamente interpretabili.
Metodo che non richiede addestramento aggiuntivo del modello.

2611.29483.abs: Recent works align the intermediate features of vision-language-action (VLA) models with frozen vision encoders during fine-tuning, hoping to inject additional priors such as 3D awareness or affordances. Unlike in image generation, where teachers for representation alignment (REPA) are assessed with encoder-intrinsic metrics, teachers for VLAs are still chosen largely by heuristics. We show that this practice is unreliable: across 14 teachers and 16 manipulation tasks, under matched training budgets, no off-the-shelf vision encoder improves the clean success rate of $π_{0.5}$ by more than 1 point, and all of them reduce its success rate under perturbations by 10 to 39 points. Neither global semantics nor spatial structure, the criteria used in image generation, predicts which teachers help. We therefore propose the behavioral structure metric (BSM), which measures whether states that are close in a teacher's feature space are followed by similar expert actions within the same task. BSM correlates strongly with success rate under perturbations ($r=0.87$), and every off-the-shelf vision encoder scores below $π_{0.5}$ itself. Based on it, we introduce Behavior-Aware VLA Alignment (BAVA), a general VLA alignment protocol that favors vision encoders whose BSM exceeds the student's and stops alignment early according to the student's BSM during training. On SmolVLA, BAVA matches continuous alignment with one third of the alignment budget, and improves the average success rate by 4.6 points over unaligned fine-tuning. Our results suggest that representation alignment benefits…

ov.problema: Nei modelli vision-language-action (VLA), recenti lavori allineano le feature intermedie con encoder visivi congelati durante il fine-tuning, sperando di iniettare prior come consapevolezza 3D o affordance. A differenza della generazione di immagini, dove i teacher per l'allineamento delle rappresentazioni (REPA) sono valutati con metriche intrinseche all'encoder, per i VLA i teacher sono ancora scelti in gran parte con euristiche.
ov.idea: Gli autori mostrano che questa pratica non è affidabile: su 14 teacher e 16 task di manipolazione, con budget di addestramento uguali, nessun encoder visivo off-the-shelf migliora il tasso di successo pulito di π_{0.5} di più di 1 punto, e tutti riducono il tasso di successo sotto perturbazioni da 10 a 39 punti. Propongono la metrica behavioral structure metric (BSM), che misura se stati vicini nello spazio delle feature di un teacher sono seguiti da azioni esperte simili nello stesso task. Basandosi su di essa, introducono Behavior-Aware VLA Alignment (BAVA), un protocollo che favorisce…
ov.risultati: BSM correla fortemente con il tasso di successo sotto perturbazioni (r=0.87), e ogni encoder visivo off-the-shelf ha punteggio inferiore a π_{0.5} stesso. Su SmolVLA, BAVA eguaglia l'allineamento continuo con un terzo del budget di allineamento e migliora il tasso di successo medio di 4.

glossario.d: Modello che collega visione, linguaggio e azioni per il controllo robotico.
Allineamento delle rappresentazioni tramite un teacher pre-addestrato.
Metrica che misura se feature vicine corrispondono ad azioni esperte simili.

2611.30469.abs: Few-shot detectors struggle to distinguish categories that look alike but differ in local components, because a few examples rarely reveal which differences determine category identity. Category descriptions specify components and relations but do not establish their presence in an image. We propose Struct2Det, which uses category structure to guide detection and verify candidates in three stages. Relational Structure Encoding maps category graphs to component embeddings and a global condition. Component-Grounded Detection uses component queries to retrieve multi-scale image evidence that, with the global condition, modulates category text embeddings for initial detection. Verification-Guided Refinement matches candidate regions with components expected by their top-scoring categories; when class scores are close and matches are reliable, matched pairs correct region features before the shared detector predicts again.
