ov.risultati: Nella classifica pubblica a novembre 2026 (19 modelli, tre tentativi per task), Claude Fable 5.2 passa il 52,2% dei tentativi, Claude Sonnet 5.5 il 50,6% e Claude Opus 5.5 il 46,1%; GPT-6.1 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1 e GPT-6 Astra passano il 31-34%, gli altri 13 modelli al massimo il 18,9%. In uno studio di etichette umane, tre grader modello concordano con un ingegnere sull'85-86% dei verdetti, circa quanto due ingegneri tra loro.
ov.limiti: Il testo è troncato e non descrive in dettaglio i casi d'esempio.

glossario.d: Sistema che scrive ed esegue codice in autonomia per risolvere un task.
Insieme di criteri espliciti usati per valutare se un tentativo è riuscito.
L'ambiente o framework che esegue l'agente e ne raccoglie le azioni.

2611.30592.abs: Text-to-image diffusion models can generate harmful or sensitive content, such as pornographic or violent imagery, raising serious security concerns. Model editing has recently emerged as an efficient approach to mitigate this issue. It modifies pretrained models with minimal parameter updates to alter specific concepts while preserving overall model capabilities. However, due to the entangled representations of different concepts in diffusion models, direct modifications inevitably disrupt non-target concepts. Meanwhile, U-Net's hierarchical heterogeneity hinders unified strategies from balancing erasure and quality. To address these issues, we propose Hierarchical Orthogonal Subspace Erasure (HOSE). This method projects parameter updates into the subspace orthogonal to general knowledge, thereby eliminating interference with non-target concepts. Considering the hierarchical heterogeneity of the U-Net architecture, we further propose a hierarchical adaptive mechanism, constructing differentiated subspace projections for different layers to precisely adapt to the model's hierarchical structure, thereby resolving the inherent trade-off between erasure and image quality in unified constraints. Experimental results demonstrate the proposed method reduces harmful content generation by 80% compared with the unedited model. While it inevitably incurs some image quality degradation, it still outperforms other editing-based baselines in terms of quality preservation, and achieves a significantly better trade-off between harmful content suppression and quality loss than these…

2611.30173.abs: Dense visual SLAM built on learned two-view geometry is evaluated in good light; in low light it fails silently. Two frames of 9-level quantized noise, no scene at all, give MASt3R-SLAM's network a cross-view geometric self-consistency of 0.936; a real dark frame pair gives 0.935. Starved of structure, the network invents the same geometry for both views and the system trusts the agreement: on a dark sequence it consumes 1,605 frames, emits 7 keyframes, rejects no factor-graph edges and reports full frame rate, while over 95% of the correspondences it accepts violate the ground-truth epipolar geometry. One inflated statistic is read by two subsystems against thresholds in opposite directions, so keyframing starves while relocalization accepts almost every candidate. The same statistic, read at keyframe-pair baselines, separates the confident collapse from working runs on the ETH3D dark sequences without ground truth or extra computation (in-sample). Low-light-adapted weights take tracked trajectories from 1/6 to 5/6, as does retuning two thresholds; neither yields accurate ones, because the adaptation withdraws confidence from wrong geometry rather than finding right geometry. Replayed on a Jetson AGX Orin carried by a legged robot, the mechanism's signature reproduces on the two darkest of four routes, and which of its faces appears varies with route geometry and sensor encoding. The network does not lose confidence in the dark; it manufactures it.

2611.30117.abs: Concept erasure aims to remove selected visual concepts from text-to-image diffusion models while preserving the generation of non-target concepts. Evaluation typically measures target suppression and non-target preservation in generated images, but a concept's absence from these outputs does not establish its removal from the model. We introduce SAE-Audit, a white-box audit using sparse autoencoder (SAE) probes to test whether activation interventions can restore target-concept generation without changing model weights or test prompts. After verifying target suppression, we compare the original and edited models using a shared SAE representation learned from original-model activations, identifying features whose target-related responses weaken after erasure. We inject sparse directions derived from the original-model responses into the edited model, keeping these directions fixed across test prompts, and evaluate recovery on held-out scene families. Experiments span six erasure methods and four domains: objects, artistic styles, copyrighted content, and nudity. Interventions using a few dozen selected SAE features yield higher average recovery rates than matched random-feature interventions, with recovery concentrated in objects and nudity following cross-attention edits. Most styles and copyrighted concepts show limited recovery under the tested intervention settings. These findings show that output suppression can coexist with responsiveness to sparse concept directions supplied from the original model.

ov.problema: La cancellazione di concetti (concept erasure) nei modelli di diffusione testo-immagine mira a rimuovere concetti visivi specifici, ma valutare se il concetto è davvero rimosso dal modello è difficile: l'assenza dall'output non garantisce che il modello non possa rigenerarlo.
ov.idea: SAE-Audit usa sonde basate su sparse autoencoder (SAE, reti che scompongono attivazioni in feature sparse) per verificare se interventi sulle attivazioni possono ripristinare la generazione del concetto target senza modificare pesi o prompt. Dopo aver confermato la soppressione, confronta modello originale ed editato con un SAE condiviso, identifica feature indebolite e inietta direzioni sparse derivate dal modello originale in quello editato, tenendole fisse su prompt di test.
ov.risultati: Su sei metodi di cancellazione e quattro domini (oggetti, stili artistici, contenuti protetti da copyright, nudità), interventi con poche decine di feature SAE selezionate danno tassi di recupero medi più alti rispetto a feature casuali; il recupero è concentrato su oggetti e nudità dopo edit cross-attention, mentre stili e concetti copyright mostrano recupero limitato.
ov.limiti: Il recupero è limitato per stili e concetti copyright nelle condizioni testate, quindi la soppressione dell'output può coesistere con reattività a direzioni sparse solo in alcuni domini.

glossario.d: Rimozione di concetti visivi specifici da modelli di diffusione testo-immagine.
Rete che scompone attivazioni in feature sparse e interpretabili.
Meccanismo che collega testo e immagine nei modelli di diffusione.

2611.29286.abs: This study investigates whether domain grounding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can enhance the accuracy and reliability of pet care advice generated by large language models (LLMs). We curated a dataset of breed-specific dog care information and used it to develop two systems: a RAG pipeline based on TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0, and a fine-tuned LLaMA-3.2-1B model adapted using LoRA. Both systems were evaluated on 15 dog care questions. The RAG model achieved a perfect average score of 2.0, outperforming the fine-tuned model (mean = 1.47). Statistical analyses, including Welch's t-test, Mann-Whitney U, and Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (all p < 0.05), confirmed the significance of the performance gap. Our findings suggest that retrieval-based domain grounding leads to more accurate, consistent, and trustworthy responses than standalone fine-tuning in specialized LLM applications.

2611.30372.abs: Navigation systems in colonoscopy are advancing from guiding the endoscopist to steering the scope autonomously. Since an incorrect motion can injure the patient, developing and evaluating these systems calls for a world model of colonoscopy. Such a model must follow a commanded scope motion, keep the colon anatomy consistent, and show lesions and procedural events. Yet camera-controlled generators trained on general scenes lose the colon's structure under motion, and endoscopic generators offer no camera control. We present ColonoWorld, a colonoscopy world model conditioned on a camera trajectory and a coarse 3D tube of the colon, trained on in vivo videos. From a whole-colon tube, it generates a full cecum-to-rectum procedure, even for unseen colon shapes. It also places polyps, instruments, and irrigation at specified locations and times. ColonoWorld outperforms state-of-the-art video generators, reducing camera trajectory error by 32% and FVD by 29%. Our code and annotations will be released at https://aidaslab.github.io/ColonoWorld.

2611.28227.abs: Feeding each position's top-layer hidden state back into the next position's input improves Transformer performance. However, this feedback breaks speculative decoding, since verifying a drafted token requires the top-layer state from its preceding position, which forces the draft to rely on an approximate stand-in. Training the model to adapt to this stand-in can lower the exact-decoding performance ceiling, while using it at inference time further introduces approximation error. We propose Feedback Shortcut to address both bottlenecks. First, state alignment trains a lightweight projection from multi-token prediction head states to stand-ins, leaving base model training untouched. Second, pipelined correction re-evaluates each draft using its predecessor's newly computed state, a much closer proxy to true feedback. Running this correction inside the verification pass of subsequent drafts improves accuracy with zero extra calls. Across 135M and 780M scales, Feedback Shortcut stays within 10^{-4} bits per byte of the exact-decoding ceiling on Paloma and accelerates decoding by 2.4-2.8x with about 2% more training compute than the latent feedback Transformer. At large batch sizes, skipping correction still preserves Transformer speed and over 80% of latent feedback's gains.

ov.problema: I Transformer con feedback latente (che rimandano lo stato nascosto del token precedente in input) migliorano le prestazioni, ma rompono il speculative decoding (generazione speculativa) perché per verificare una bozza serve lo stato del token precedente, non ancora calcolato.
ov.idea: Feedback Shortcut risolve con due mosse: (1) state alignment addestra una proiezione leggera dagli stati multi-token prediction a stand-in approssimati, senza toccare il training base; (2) pipelined correction rivaluta ogni bozza usando lo stato appena calcolato del predecessore, dentro la verifica delle bozze successive, senza chiamate extra.
ov.risultati: Su scale 135M e 780M, Feedback Shortcut resta entro 10^{-4} bit per byte dal ceiling di decodifica esatta su Paloma e accelera di 2.4–2.8x con circa il 2% di compute di training in più rispetto al Transformer a feedback latente. A batch grandi, saltare la correzione mantiene la velocità del Transformer e oltre l'80% dei guadagni del feedback latente.
ov.limiti: A batch grandi saltare la correzione perde parte dei guadagni (mantiene >80%); testato solo su modelli fino a 780M.

glossario.d: Tecnica per accelerare la generazione: un modello piccolo propone token, uno grande li verifica in blocco.
Reimmettere lo stato nascosto del token precedente come input del token successivo.
Misura di quanto bene un modello comprime il testo: più basso è, meglio è.

2611.29628.abs: Advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) have enabled a wide range of applications. However, their ability to simulate human-like behavior and reasoning remains unclear. While emotion detection is a better-established Natural Language Processing (NLP) task, existing approaches primarily focus on directly classifying text into predefined emotion classes, often overlooking the appraisal process that explains why an individual experiences a particular emotion in a given situation. In this work, we propose Psychology-based Chain-of-Thought (PsyCoT) reasoning, a theory-driven prompting strategy grounded in the Schachter-Singer and Cognitive Appraisal theories of emotion. We propose and evaluate PsyCoT for subjective NLP tasks, including emotion analysis, emotion intensity prediction, stress analysis, and depression severity identification. Our evaluation covers four levels of classification complexity: binary, multiclass, multi-label, and ordinal scaling, spanning 11 languages. We assess the performance of five state-of-the-art LLMs across these selected subjective NLP tasks. Experimental results demonstrate that PsyCoT prompt variants improve the standard chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting across the evaluated tasks. Across all evaluated tasks, PsyCoT yields F1 score gains ranging from 0.5% to 28.1%, depending on the model, task, and language configuration.

2611.30480.abs: Recent work on Large Language Models (LLMs) suggests that reasoning capabilities can be enhanced at test time not only through longer token-level reasoning traces, but also through additional computation in latent space. This raises a natural question for Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs): can additional computation in latent space improve visual perception at test time? In this work, we first verify that MLLMs contain stable reusable layers that can be re-forwarded at inference time without disrupting normal generation. Based on this observation, we propose \textbf{Lo}ok \textbf{Ba}ck in the \textbf{L}atent \textbf{S}pace (\textbf{Lobals}), a training-free decoding method that identifies the contiguous layer window with the strongest visual-token attention and re-forwards through it, allowing the model to revisit visual evidence in latent space. We demonstrate that this latent-space revisit strategy can improve MLLMs' performance across diverse multimodal settings, including general vision-language tasks, visual hallucination tasks, and vision-centric tasks.

2611.31025.abs: Vision Transformers (ViTs) are a predominant architecture for computer vision, with token reduction emerging as a popular paradigm to improve their efficiency. Prior work compares reduction algorithms, but not how models respond to them, nor how their response changes with model depth. We propose Monte Carlo Token Pruning (MCTP), which estimates each token's impact on the prediction when tokens are explicitly removed during the forward pass. Applying MCTP to recent pretrained models, we observe that most, such as DINOv3, maintain a similar ranking of token importance at every depth (high Coherent Aggregation), while SigLIP 2 does not. This coherence requires predictions to survive pruning, which depends on keeping high-norm "sink" tokens: prefix tokens are kept by design, while prefix-free SigLIP 2 forms them on patch tokens, which pruning may remove. We show that in removing DINOv3's prefix tokens, its predictions and coherence collapse, while protecting only 5 tokens for SigLIP 2 cuts the token impact outside the object's bounding box by up to 62%. Beyond this, MCTP offers a post-hoc method to evaluate how a pretrained ViT responds to pruning, and suggests that token reduction methods should keep "sinks".

ov.problema: I Vision Transformers (ViT) sono modelli per la visione artificiale; ridurre i token (unità di elaborazione) migliora l'efficienza, ma non si sa come i modelli rispondono a questa riduzione e come cambia con la profondità.
ov.idea: MCTP (Monte Carlo Token Pruning) stima l'impatto di ogni token sulla previsione quando i token vengono rimossi esplicitamente durante il forward pass. Applicandolo a modelli pre-addestrati, si osserva che DINOv3 mantiene un ranking simile di importanza dei token a ogni profondità (alta Coherent Aggregation), mentre SigLIP 2 no. Questo richiede di mantenere token 'sink' ad alta norma: i token di prefisso sono mantenuti per design, mentre SigLIP 2 li forma su token patch che la potatura può rimuovere.
ov.risultati: Rimuovendo i token di prefisso di DINOv3, le sue previsioni e coerenza collassano; proteggendo solo 5 token per SigLIP 2 si riduce l'impatto dei token fuori dal bounding box dell'oggetto fino al 62%.
ov.limiti: Il metodo è post-hoc e potrebbe non generalizzare a tutti i modelli ViT.

glossario.d: Riduzione del numero di token elaborati per migliorare l'efficienza.
Token con norma alta che aiutano a mantenere le previsioni stabili.
Capacità di mantenere un ranking simile di importanza dei token a diverse profondità.

2611.30422.abs: Hardware benchmarks for LLM agents all run the design flow forward, from a specification to RTL, a layout or a bug fix. We ask the reverse question: given an implemented artifact, such as a layout, a gate-level netlist or a protected simulation model, can an agent work out what it does well enough to act on that knowledge? We introduce HWRE-Bench, a benchmark for agentic hardware reverse engineering built on one observation. Each step of the forward flow discards information (names, hierarchy, word-level structure, generator parameters, the programming model), and a reverse-engineering task asks the agent to recover what was lost and to prove it with an executable deliverable that the artifact alone cannot supply. Since layout extraction is now mechanical and a correct netlist is already a cycle-exact model, every task carries a mandatory copy-the-netlist control that must score zero. HWRE-Bench spans five tracks (Extract, Abstract, Audit, Interoperate, Modify), four information-loss levels and white- versus black-box access, all on original designs. We report a pilot of 148 rollouts from two agents on four seed tasks under 16 conditions, with stage-annotated trajectories. Agents built their own layout extractors and audited a sanitized layout as reliably as a netlist, at about 27% more turns. Keyless, equivalence-preserving obfuscation changed neither pass rates nor defect-repair scores. Whether agents read the structure at all depended on task framing rather than on necessity, so pass rate alone does not show understanding. Provider safety filters stopped 16% of one…

2611.30532.abs: Diffusion models memorize training images and reproduce them almost verbatim when prompted, creating copyright and privacy liabilities. Data unlearning erases the influence of specific training samples from a trained model without retraining, and is two-sided: it must forget the targets while preserving generation quality on everything else. Prior methods use the squared-L2 diffusion loss, at most with a hand-set frequency mask; however, it is known that every Bregman divergence is a mathematically valid choice and the squared-L2 is only the simplest example. BEND is the first to search this family: it fits a spectral Bregman divergence to the unlearning task through a bilevel loop, so the loss itself is shaped to forget thoroughly while protecting quality. It also redirects a memorized image to the mean of its retain images, where ReTrack, the state of the art, redirects it to a single near-copy. On Stable Diffusion, a single BEND model erases all 48 verifiably memorized benchmark images at once. It forgets at least as much as per-target, sequential, and jointly trained ReTrack (SSCD 0.084 versus 0.094-0.120), at the quality of the model before unlearning (CLIP-IQA 0.81 versus 0.64-0.69). BEND also outperforms the state of the art on CelebA-HQ in all three measures of the benchmark, and matches or exceeds it on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

2611.30170.abs: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents enable automated interactions with mobile, web, and desktop interfaces. However, their large memory footprint and repeated model calls hinder deployment on resource-constrained devices, motivating post-training quantization (PTQ) without full retraining. Quantization can degrade GUI response accuracy and distort the instruction-vision affinities and local spatial relations needed for GUI target selection. Small coordinate errors can cause missed clicks, while early action errors can alter subsequent interface states and disrupt task execution. Local reconstruction error alone does not directly assess whether these responses and relations are preserved. We propose GUI-Q, a PTQ framework that targets response and relation preservation with 4-bit weights and 16-bit activations (W4A16). Task-Sensitive Granularity Allocation (TSGA) allocates finer groups under a scale-byte budget by combining response sensitivity with the measured reduction in activation-weighted distortion. Relation-Preserving Symmetry Selection (RPSS) then selects symmetric or asymmetric grids to preserve instruction-vision affinities and local spatial relations in GUIs. Across three GUI-capable models, GUI-Q improves mean grounding TargetHit by 8.04 to 12.55 points over the strongest evaluated 4-bit configurations, while reducing static peak graphics processing unit (GPU) memory by 49.9% to 56.2% relative to bfloat16 (BF16). Fixed-output replay with packed 4-bit execution provides 1.7 to 2.8 times model-call speedups. The code will be released.

ov.problema: Gli agenti GUI hanno un grande footprint di memoria e richiedono molte chiamate al modello, ostacolando il deployment su dispositivi con risorse limitate. La quantizzazione post-addestramento (PTQ) può degradare l'accuratezza delle risposte GUI e distorcere le affinità istruzione-visione e le relazioni spaziali locali necessarie per selezionare i target.
ov.idea: GUI-Q è un framework PTQ che mira a preservare risposte e relazioni con pesi a 4 bit e attivazioni a 16 bit (W4A16). Task-Sensitive Granularity Allocation (TSGA) assegna gruppi più fini sotto un budget di byte di scala, combinando sensibilità della risposta e riduzione misurata della distorsione pesata dalle attivazioni. Relation-Preserving Symmetry Selection (RPSS) seleziona griglie simmetriche o asimmetriche per preservare affinità istruzione-visione e relazioni spaziali locali.
ov.risultati: Su tre modelli GUI-capable, GUI-Q migliora il TargetHit medio di grounding da 8,04 a 12,55 punti rispetto alle migliori configurazioni a 4 bit valutate, riducendo la memoria GPU di picco statica dal 49,9% al 56,2% rispetto a bfloat16 (BF16).
ov.limiti: Il metodo è valutato solo su tre modelli GUI-capable; non è chiaro come si comporti su altri tipi di modelli o con quantizzazione a bit inferiori.

glossario.d: quantizzazione post-addestramento, riduce la precisione senza riaddestrare
pesi a 4 bit e attivazioni a 16 bit
metrica che misura se il target GUI selezionato è corretto

2611.30094.abs: Linear probes recover character properties of a word from a language model's hidden states, but a probe at the answer position cannot say whether the property was stored with the word or produced because the prompt asked for it. We separate the two with a word-position baseline: the same held-out-word probe applied to the query word's own tokens in a sentence that asks nothing. Across 16 open-weight models from seven families (0.6B--14B) and eleven character tasks, the word tokens encode \texttt{first\_letter}, \texttt{last\_letter} and \texttt{most\_frequent\_letter} above a word-only nuisance floor in all 16 models, and about 70\% of that signal is already present in the token embedding. Asking the question adds a second signal at the answer position. Its size grows with model scale for all four prompt-sensitive tasks (Holm-corrected permutation $p \leq 0.018$, also within model families), and the growth is confined to the late layers: restricted to the first quarter of the network, the slope is indistinguishable from zero. Small models' answer positions hold less linearly decodable signal than their word-level store; large models' hold more. Four controls bound these claims. Measured against the nuisance floor, the question-free signal that a majority-baseline analysis counts as retained largely disappears (\texttt{last\_letter}: $-0.01$). Count tasks become measurable only after length, repetition and query-letter shortcuts are removed by design. A pre-registered test finds that a question placed before the word does not change the word's own encoding beyond what an…

ov.problema: Non è chiaro se le proprietà dei caratteri delle parole (es. prima lettera) siano immagazzinate nel modello o emergano solo quando la domanda le richiede. Distinguere è importante per capire come i modelli rappresentano la conoscenza.
ov.idea: Gli autori usano una baseline alla posizione della parola: applicano una sonda (classificatore lineare) ai token della parola stessa in una frase che non fa domande. Confrontano questo con il segnale alla posizione della risposta. Analizzano 16 modelli open-weight (0.6B-14B) e 11 compiti sui caratteri.
ov.risultati: I token della parola codificano first_letter, last_letter e most_frequent_letter in tutti i 16 modelli, e circa il 70% del segnale è già presente nell'embedding del token. Il segnale alla posizione della risposta cresce con la scala del modello per i compiti sensibili al prompt, ma solo negli strati tardivi; nei primi quarti di rete la pendenza è indistinguibile da zero.
ov.limiti: Quattro controlli limitano le conclusioni: il segnale senza domanda che un'analisi baseline conta come retained svanisce in gran parte (last_letter: -0.01); i compiti di conteggio diventano misurabili solo dopo aver rimosso scorciatoie di lunghezza, ripetizione e query-letter.

glossario.d: Classificatore lineare addestrato su rappresentazioni interne per estrarre informazioni.
Rappresentazione vettoriale di un token appresa dal modello.
Ultimi strati della rete neurale, più vicini all'output.

2611.29249.abs: With the increasing adoption of geographic artificial intelligence, location encoders are widely used to map geographic coordinates to learned embeddings for tasks in Earth observation and geospatial modeling. Similar to map projections, location encoders can distort geographic space, that is, equal-distance displacements in different directions can result in unequal embedding changes. However, such distortion remains largely unexamined, and it can propagate into downstream applications. We adapt Tissot's indicatrix, a cartographic tool for map projection distortion, to characterize this distortion. At each location, we compare encoder outputs at equal distances in 32 directions and fit a tensor, represented by an ellipse, whose elongation (anisotropy) and orientation describe the local distortion. The fit requires only encoder outputs without access to model internals and is validated against references with known geometry. By applying the method to thirteen released checkpoints of five encoder families, we find that distortions vary across space and inherit the input geometry to varying degrees, closely in GeoCLIP with its Equal Earth input (anisotropy correlation of 0.88) and weakly or moderately in the other encoders. The distortion also affects the locations an encoder treats as neighbors. Within 1km of 20 query sites, the 40 nearest neighbors in geographic and embedding space overlap by a median of only 57.5--87.5% across the checkpoints, while the fitted ellipses select exactly the same embedding neighbors in 265 of 299 comparisons. These findings provide a…

2611.27490.abs: Most established instance-retrieval benchmarks emphasise landmarks; small sculptures from visually similar series offer a complementary challenge. We introduce Doppeldwarf-306: 1,691 openly licensed photographs of 306 bronze dwarf statues in Wrocław, Poland, many made in themed series that share one style, with the photographer of each image recorded. With no training, nearest-neighbour search over frozen DINOv2 features names the right statue first for 93.1% of leave-one-out queries, and the best of thirteen backbones from seven pretraining paradigms reaches 94.7%. Accuracy falls slowly as candidates are added: for DINOv2, by about 0.8 points each time their number doubles. A natural design for a phone guide compares a photograph only with statues near the user. In simulation this helps, but less than an equal number of randomly chosen statues does, so random subsampling overstates its value; a permutation test ties the penalty to the real layout (p = 0.005). Used as a weight instead of a filter, location raises DINOv2 from 93.4% to 98.7% for a simulated user 25 m from the statue. With the query's photographer withheld, learned local-feature matching raises DINOv2 accuracy from 81.8% to 85.5% and also improves DINOv3. Comparing the two best candidates cuts DINOv2's false acceptance of unknown statues from 38.3% to 19.6% at 90% known acceptance.

2611.29566.abs: Test-time compute has become an important paradigm in computer vision and language modeling, where additional computation at inference time enables models to explore multiple candidate solutions and select or refine the most reliable one. However, time series forecasting models typically produce predictions through a single forward pass, leaving them vulnerable to distribution shifts and non-stationarity that frequently arise in real-world temporal data. We propose Time Test Compute for Time Series (TTC4TS), an architecture-agnostic framework that improves the predictive performance of frozen forecasting models at inference time. Given a pretrained backbone, the generator produces multiple candidate forecast trajectories using augmentation, retrieval, adapter. The synthesizer then selects or combines these candidates using aggregation, classification, or candidate-scoring and ranking methods to produce the final forecast. By increasing the number of candidates, TTC4TS scales test-time compute without retraining the forecasting backbone. Beyond improving point-forecast accuracy, TTC4TS can exploit candidate forecasts for uncertainty quantification, which supports improved interval forecasts. We also theoretically analyze when additional test-time computation improves forecasting. Experiments across diverse datasets and backbones demonstrate consistent gains in accuracy and calibration. Code is provided in https://github.com/Anoise/TTC4TS.

2611.30460.abs: Contrastive decoding (CD) mitigates object hallucination in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by contrasting token distributions under different conditions to adjust token scores. However, existing generative and discriminative benchmarks primarily measure final task scores, which can be confounded by candidate filtering, changes in generation trajectories, and response biases, making it difficult to isolate the effects of the underlying contrastive adjustments. To address these limitations while complementing existing evaluations, we introduce CONCOR (Contrastive Correction Evaluation), a controlled benchmark that directly evaluates the competition between ground-truth and different types of hallucinated candidates using the Contrastive Grounding Margin (CGM). CGM also enables analysis of directional consistency, composition, and reliability of contrastive corrections. Our evaluation reveals that existing CD methods exhibit distinct correction behaviors: some consistently favor ground-truth candidates, whereas others produce strong corrections but also introduce more errors. Crucially, these differences help explain their contrasting responses to increased contrast strength, which improves some methods while degrading others. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating the contrastive correction itself, rather than relying solely on final-output performance, and CONCOR provides a controlled and interpretable framework for understanding and improving CD methods for hallucination mitigation.

2611.30997.abs: Building general-purpose robots is a central goal in robotics. Agentic robotics pursues this goal with planners that control robots through tool calls. However, existing methods either rely on proprietary models accessed through APIs, which incur high costs and latency, or post-train a planner with reinforcement learning (RL) in a single domain, requiring a separate specialist for each domain with incompatible tools. In large language model (LLM) post-training, multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) has been used to consolidate domain specialists into a single generalist. Yet whether MOPD can build a generalist planner for agentic robotics, how well it performs, and how it compares with other consolidation methods remain unexplored. In this paper, we systematically study these questions: we introduce Robo-MOPD, which trains a single student on closed-loop rollouts in simulation under token-level supervision from matching frozen specialists, and compare it with weight merging, off-policy specialist supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and multi-domain online RL. Experiments on LIBERO-PRO and RoboCasa365 show that a single 9B Robo-MOPD planner reaches 72.9% and 44.8% success (58.9% average), surpassing all consolidated baselines in average success and both 9B specialists on their respective benchmarks. Robo-MOPD excels on long-horizon tasks, outperforming multi-domain online RL by 13.0 percentage points on LIBERO-10.

2611.30399.abs: Determining action reversibility requires checking whether the effects of an action can be undone. Recent work has extended reversibility to fully observable non-deterministic (FOND) planning. It distinguishes weak reversibility, where reversal may succeed, from strong-cyclic reversibility, where reversal is guaranteed under fairness. These notions are qualitative: they say whether reversal is possible, but not how costly it is. We introduce cost-sensitive reversibility for non-deterministic actions. Given positive action costs, we define weak and strong reversal budgets, $k$-bounded reversibility, and a distinction between finite strong reversal and strong-cyclic reversal with unbounded worst-case cost. We relate the resulting notions in a reversibility lattice, prove cost-aware policy-merging results, and show how to compute restricted weak and strong universal uniform reversal budgets using cost-optimal classical planning and worst-case-optimal FOND search, respectively. We also give an admissible lower-bound test for rejecting $k$-bounded reversibility. These notions support finer-grained safety decisions: a small finite strong budget bounds recovery cost, whereas a small weak budget certifies only a cheap possible recovery path. Actions without an acceptable strong bound may therefore warrant human approval, as in tool-using agent systems.

2611.30531.abs: The diffusion model has been successfully applied to various detection tasks. However, it still faces several challenges when used for oriented object detection: objects that are arbitrarily rotated require the diffusion model to encode their orientation information; uncontrollable random boxes inaccurately locate objects with dense arrangements and extreme aspect ratios; oriented boxes result in the misalignment between them and image features. To overcome these limitations, we propose ReDiffDet, a framework that formulates oriented object detection as a rotation-equivariant denoising diffusion process. First, we represent an oriented box as a 2D Gaussian distribution, forming the basis of the denoising paradigm. The reverse process can be proven to be rotation-equivariant within this representation and model framework. Second, we design a conditional encoder with conditional boxes to prevent boxes from being randomly placed across the entire image. Third, we propose an aligned decoder for alignment between oriented boxes and image features. The extensive experiments demonstrate ReDiffDet achieves promising performance and significantly outperforms the diffusion model baseline.

2611.30027.abs: A 4-bit KV cache reads about half the bytes of FP8, but Hopper GPUs have no FP4 hardware and little instruction-issue capacity per byte of memory bandwidth, so 4-bit values must be decoded in software. On H200, vLLM's NVFP4 KV path (FlashInfer's decode) reaches 10-20% of memory bandwidth and is up to 1.7x slower than FP8. NVBit instruction counts show two causes: the kernels behind vLLM's 4-bit paths (FlashInfer NVFP4, Triton UltraQuant) execute 2-6x Hopper's issue budget per byte and serialize loading, decoding and matrix multiplies. Our Hopper-native decode kernel overlaps a TMA producer warp with two compute warpgroups, lays the cache out at write time so decoded values feed the tensor cores from registers, and swaps the matrix operands so small query groups need no padding. On H200 it reaches 67-75% of peak bandwidth at batch 32-128 and at all 11 shapes is 1.12-1.49x faster than the faster of XQA and FlashAttention-4's proposed native FP8. Inside vLLM, with an accuracy recipe (K mean removal and rotation, 4 BF16 sink tokens, BF16 layer 0), it decodes 1.12-1.64x faster per step on Llama-3.1-8B than vLLM's FlashInfer FP8 path at batch 8 and above (1.04-1.24x over FlashAttention-4's FP8), is level at batch 1, and holds 1.63x as many tokens. On one H200 under a reasoning-like request stream, the highest rate at which 99% of requests meet the latency targets is 1.23-1.32x FP8's on Llama-3.1-8B and 1.67-2.20x on Qwen2.5-72B, as the cache becomes the limit; prefill-heavy streams are worse (7% slower prefill). On five 7B-32B models, repeated runs show no significant accuracy…

ov.problema: Una KV cache a 4 bit legge circa metà dei byte di FP8, ma le GPU Hopper non hanno hardware FP4 e poca capacità di emissione di istruzioni per byte di banda, quindi i valori a 4 bit vanno decodificati in software. Su H200 il percorso NVFP4 di vLLM raggiunge il 10-20% della banda di memoria ed è fino a 1,7x più lento di FP8.
ov.idea: Un kernel di decodifica nativo per Hopper sovrappone un warp produttore TMA con due gruppi di warp di calcolo, dispone la cache in scrittura così i valori decodificati arrivano ai tensor core dai registri, e scambia gli operandi della matrice per evitare padding con piccoli gruppi di query.
ov.risultati: Su H200 raggiunge il 67-75% della banda di picco con batch 32-128 e su tutte le 11 forme è 1,12-1,49x più veloce del più veloce tra XQA e FP8 nativo proposto di FlashAttention-4. Dentro vLLM decodifica 1,12-1,64x più veloce per passo su Llama-3.1-8B rispetto a FP8 di FlashInfer con batch 8 e oltre, e tiene 1,63x più token.
ov.limiti: I risultati sono specifici per GPU Hopper (H200) e richiedono una ricetta di accuratezza (rimozione della media K, rotazione, token sink BF16); il testo è troncato sui flussi prefill-heavy.

glossario.d: Memoria delle chiavi e valori passati usata per generare token senza ricalcolare tutto.
Copia asincrona di dati tra memoria e unità di calcolo nelle GPU Hopper.
Unità hardware specializzate per moltiplicazioni di matrici nelle GPU.

2611.29936.abs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has demonstrated strong performance in improving large language model (LLM) reasoning, yet its credit-assignment signal remains coarse. Outcome verifiers provide scalable supervision by judging whether a completed response is correct, but they do not directly indicate which intermediate reasoning tokens contribute to success or failure. As a result, policy optimization can be inefficient, especially when training base models directly from sparse outcome feedback. In this paper, we introduce SAEPO, a Sparse AutoEncoder-guided token-level credit assignment method for outcome-supervised Policy Optimization. Rather than treating correctness only as a rollout-level (sequence-level) signal, SAEPO uses a pretrained sparse autoencoder (SAE) to build token-level semantic representations within reasoning trajectories; it scores each token based on the SAE concepts (e.g., penalizing wrong "final-answer" tokens but rewarding correct "reasoning-process" tokens), learned in an unsupervised manner, to achieve fine-grained credit assignment. SAEPO is a plug-in advantage-shaping module compatible with various policy optimization algorithms. We instantiate SAEPO with both GRPO and GSPO, covering token-ratio and sequence-ratio policy-gradient objectives, and evaluate SAEPO across three LLM backbones on six math and two code benchmarks. Empirical results show that SAEPO improves both the math and code benchmark averages over the matched baselines, with gains of up to 6.63% and 5.57%, respectively. On Qwen3-1.7B-Base, training curves also…

ov.problema: In RLVR (Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards), il segnale di ricompensa è a livello di sequenza e non indica quali token intermedi contribuiscono al successo. Questo rende l'ottimizzazione inefficiente, specialmente partendo da modelli base con feedback sparso.
ov.idea: SAEPO usa un sparse autoencoder (SAE) pre-addestrato per costruire rappresentazioni semantiche a livello di token nei percorsi di ragionamento. Assegna un punteggio a ogni token in base ai concetti SAE (es. penalizza token di risposta finale sbagliati, premia token di processo di ragionamento corretti). È un modulo di advantage shaping compatibile con vari algoritmi di policy optimization.
ov.risultati: SAEPO migliora le medie sui benchmark di matematica e codice rispetto alle baseline corrispondenti, istanziato con GRPO e GSPO su tre backbone LLM e sei benchmark di matematica e due di codice.
ov.limiti: Non specificati nel testo.

glossario.d: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards: apprendimento per rinforzo con ricompense verificabili.
Sparse Autoencoder: rete che impara rappresentazioni sparse e interpretabili.
Modifica del vantaggio (advantage) per guidare meglio l'apprendimento.

2611.29155.abs: Agents built on large language models must maintain continuity across repeated interactions with users. However, long-term conversations scatter facts across turns and sessions, making it difficult to retrieve the right evidence with enough context. Memory for such conversations must therefore preserve facts with their context while keeping evidence selectively accessible. We first study how memory construction and retrieval-unit boundaries affect answerability and evidence access. Reading the entire memory bank reveals gaps that cannot be resolved by retrieval selection alone, showing that some context must be preserved during memory construction. Adjacent-turn grouping improves evidence access at matched unique-turn budgets, while wider windows do not consistently help. This motivates keeping fact-specific context local while organizing cross-session evidence separately. We propose ContextFact, which links context-preserving fact memories with source-grounded entity representations. Within sessions, it gathers the context needed to interpret each fact. Across sessions, it aligns recurring referents and revisits the source dialogue to reconstruct coherent entity representations linked to the supporting facts. At query time, ContextFact retrieves fact and entity views, reranks them independently, and uses entity-linked expansion to surface related facts; complete entity representations then provide organized cross-session evidence. With Qwen3.5-27B as the backbone, ContextFact achieves state-of-the-art performance while using only $21\%$ of the evidence tokens consumed by…

ov.problema: Gli agenti basati su LLM devono mantenere continuità tra interazioni ripetute con gli utenti, ma le conversazioni a lungo termine sparpagliano i fatti tra turni e sessioni, rendendo difficile recuperare l'evidenza giusta con sufficiente contesto.
ov.idea: ContextFact collega memorie di fatti che preservano il contesto con rappresentazioni di entità ancorate alla fonte. Dentro le sessioni raccoglie il contesto necessario a interpretare ogni fatto; tra sessioni allinea i riferimenti ricorrenti e rivisita il dialogo originale per ricostruire rappresentazioni coerenti di entità collegate ai fatti di supporto. Al momento della query recupera viste di fatti ed entità, le riordina separatamente e usa l'espansione collegata alle entità per far emergere fatti correlati.
ov.risultati: Con Qwen3.5-27B come backbone, ContextFact (il testo si interrompe prima di riportare i numeri).
ov.limiti: Il testo si interrompe prima di completare i risultati e non riporta limiti espliciti.

glossario.d: Archivio di fatti e contesto che l'agente consulta tra sessioni
Persona, luogo o cosa ricorrente a cui i fatti si riferiscono
Riordinare i risultati recuperati in base alla rilevanza

2611.26745.abs: Robotic manipulation often requires remembering visual information that is no longer observable, such as the original location of an object. Existing approaches typically rely on full observation histories, which become redundant over long horizons, or text summaries, which may omit precise visual details. We study visual moment memory, the ability to retain such details from key moments for subsequent manipulation. To support this study, we introduce VMBench, a suite of long-horizon manipulation tasks requiring memory of spatial locations, visual appearances, and their associations. We further propose MomentMem, a hierarchical architecture in which a VLM-based memorizer selects keyframes and an executor predicts actions conditioned on the selected memories. This separation enables us to evaluate memory selection alongside closed-loop task success and to study memorizer generalization independently of the executor. On VMBench, MomentMem achieves 49.9% average success, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 31.7 percentage points. Moreover, we find that the memorizer transfers well to unseen appearances zero-shot. It can also adapt to an unseen task with only a few memory annotations, reaching 43.7% success, close to the 44.3% obtained with full memory supervision. Further experiments show competitive performance on RMBench and improvements in real-robot manipulation. These results highlight the value of retaining sparse visual evidence for memory-dependent manipulation. Our code is available at https://github.com/PKU-VaLuE-Lab/MomentMem.

ov.problema: Nella manipolazione robotica, spesso serve ricordare informazioni visive non più osservabili, come la posizione originale di un oggetto. Gli approcci esistenti usano intere cronologie di osservazioni (ridondanti) o riassunti testuali (che perdono dettagli visivi precisi).
ov.idea: MomentMem è un'architettura gerarchica in cui un memorizzatore basato su VLM seleziona fotogrammi chiave e un esecutore predice azioni condizionate su tali memorie. Questa separazione permette di valutare la selezione della memoria e la generalizzazione del memorizzatore indipendentemente dall'esecutore.
ov.risultati: Su VMBench, MomentMem raggiunge il 49.9% di successo medio, superando il miglior baseline di 31.7 punti percentuali. Il memorizzatore si trasferisce zero-shot a nuove apparenze e si adatta a un nuovo task con poche annotazioni, raggiungendo il 43.7% di successo (vicino al 44.3% con supervisione completa).

glossario.d: Modello linguistico-visivo, che elabora insieme testo e immagini.
Capacità di generalizzare a situazioni mai viste durante l'addestramento.
Controllo in cui le azioni influenzano lo stato e le osservazioni successive.

2611.29339.abs: Latent reasoning lets Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models deliberate at a fraction of the cost of explicit chain-of-thought, increasingly through visual foresight, which we show to be indispensable for predicting actions. Yet this paradigm is inherited from Vision-Language Models, where it serves understanding rather than action: each latent is aligned with an isolated future frame, often enriched with further modalities of that frame. We find that this binds the policy to the appearance of its training scenes, so that it degrades sharply once the scene changes. We argue that visual latents for action should capture not what a future frame looks like, but how the scene evolves toward the goal. We therefore propose Motion-Oriented Latent Reasoning, which redirects visual latents from the whole frame to the interaction that the action must bring about. Semantic latents, following the stages of embodied chain-of-thought, first establish what to accomplish and how. Conditioned on them, motion-oriented latents anticipate each future step from coarse to fine: from the global scene, to the interaction region spanned by the manipulated object and its destination, to the robot state. Relative to the state-of-the-art latent VLA LaST$_0$, our method raises the mean success rate on SimplerEnv-WidowX from 37.5% to 55.2% in distribution and from 22.4% to 30.2% under out-of-distribution shifts, and on an AgileX Piper dual-arm platform from 60.8% to 90.8% in training scenes and from 6.7% to 37.5% under environmental changes.

2611.30458.abs: Automated 3D CT report generation could support radiology workflows, yet medical vision-language models (MedVLMs) often omit diagnostic findings from generated reports. We ask whether the diagnostic ability of these models carries over to free-form reporting. Across five MedVLMs, diagnostic VQA achieves higher macro-F1 than reports generated from the same CT studies and evaluated on the same disease categories. We call this task-dependent discrepancy the diagnosis-to-report gap. Conventional Report Adaptation improves reporting for most models but does not close the gap. To investigate and narrow it, we introduce DeCAD (Decompose CT Analysis and Describe), which progressively decomposes CT report generation at diagnostic, regional textual, and regional visual levels. The model identifies positive findings before writing a report, organizes diagnosis and description into regional tasks, and restricts each task to visual tokens from the corresponding region. Diagnostic and regional textual decomposition improve report-level diagnostic performance across the five MedVLMs, whereas regional visual decomposition provides limited additional gains. In a standard VLM without medical VQA pretraining, the first two levels remain effective; regional visual decomposition also provides further gains with a region-level contrastively pretrained encoder. Full DeCAD achieves state-of-the-art performance on CT-RATE and Merlin. Analyses show greater CT-token attention during diagnosis and higher recall of reference-positive findings in both the diagnostic output and final report than with…

2611.30964.abs: Text-to-image diffusion models still struggle with complex prompts containing many elements and interactions. Existing attention-control methods mainly focus on controlling where elements appear, but often ignore how objects interact with each other. As a result, relation tokens describing interactions between elements may assign high attention to irrelevant regions, leading to missing or incorrect interactions. In this paper, we propose Graph2Scene, a training-free framework that treats scene graphs as a core control signal for diffusion generation. It represents elements as nodes and their relations as edges, and translates these element-relation dependencies into selective attention guidance. It grounds each element to its corresponding region and guides relational interactions among the involved elements. To achieve appropriate relation control without over-constraining the generation process, Graph2Scene further adapts the control duration to scene complexity and progressively relaxes graph guidance during denoising. Experiments on T2I-CompBench and ConceptMix show clear improvements in compositional generation, especially for object relations. On ConceptMix, Graph2Scene improves relationship accuracy from 0.59 to 0.84 over the strongest FLUX.1-based regional-control baseline. Results on LongBench-T2I further show its advantage on long and complex prompts.

2611.30350.abs: Large language model (LLM) agents have demonstrated strong repository-level programming capabilities. However, as software evolves, repository code may become redundant or obsolete, increasing maintenance costs and potentially introducing functional issues. Agents must therefore identify and remove unnecessary code safely, yet autonomous repository-level code cleanup remains insufficiently evaluated in isolation. To evaluate this capability, we introduce RepoClean, a benchmark of 200 cleanup tasks from 34 popular open-source Python repositories. RepoClean is constructed by automatically reintroducing deleted code from real repository histories into newer versions, preserving current implementations and retaining instances where previously passing tests consequently fail. To restore existing functionality without new feature development, agents must use repository interfaces and cross-file dependencies to determine which historical code to remove and which implementations to preserve. Evaluation of seven models shows that even the best-performing model, GPT-6 Astra, resolves only 23% of tasks. Further analysis reveals that agents remove substantially less obsolete code when cleanup is not explicitly requested. RepoClean provides a foundation for systematically studying these cleanup challenges and advancing coding agents toward autonomous software maintenance.

ov.problema: Con l'evoluzione del software il codice può diventare ridondante o obsoleto, aumentando i costi di manutenzione e causando problemi funzionali. Gli agenti devono identificare e rimuovere il codice inutile in sicurezza, ma la pulizia autonoma a livello di repository è poco valutata in modo isolato.
ov.idea: RepoClean è un benchmark di 200 task di pulizia da 34 popolari repository Python open source. È costruito reintroducendo automaticamente codice cancellato dalla storia reale del repository in versioni più recenti, preservando le implementazioni attuali e mantenendo i casi in cui i test prima passanti falliscono di conseguenza. Per ripristinare la funzionalità senza aggiungere feature, l'agente deve usare interfacce e dipendenze tra file per capire quale codice storico rimuovere e quale preservare.
ov.risultati: Su sette modelli valutati, il migliore (GPT-6 Astra) risolve solo il 23% dei task. L'analisi mostra inoltre che gli agenti rimuovono molto meno codice obsoleto quando la pulizia non è richiesta esplicitamente.
ov.limiti: Il benchmark copre solo repository Python e la valutazione è su sette modelli.

glossario.d: Codice non più necessario o superato da implementazioni successive.
Legami tra file: una modifica in un file può rompere codice in un altro.

2611.30461.abs: Diffusion virtual try-on (VTO) models produce convincing garment transfers from a single product photograph, but at hundreds of milliseconds to seconds per image every deployment today is offline or falls back to AR mirrors that need a rigged 3D asset per product. We present LiveMirror, a live-camera try-on mirror that renders a flat garment photograph onto a moving person with a diffusion model on one 16 GB consumer GPU. Its core is asynchronous keyframe try-on: generation never blocks the display, every displayed frame is an optical-flow warp of the latest generated keyframe, and keyframes are replaced only through a cross-fade. The display runs at camera rate (25 FPS at 720p) while a new try-on arrives every 370-490 ms; we measure the residual flicker, give a stage-by-stage latency budget, and report which accelerations (step count, consistency LoRA, tiny decoder, compilation) keep garment prints intact. We then show that the same GPU fixes the model's biggest cultural blind spot: try-on models trained on VITON-HD and DressCode render a knee-length kurta or sherwani as a torso-length top or a dress over bare legs. A thigh-covering mask, self-supervised pairs built automatically from 24.9k on-model e-commerce photographs, and 3.2 GPU-hours of attention-only fine-tuning of CatVTON halve the perceptual error on ethnic wear (LPIPS 0.137 to 0.077 on IndoFashion, 0.135 to 0.073 on Atlas; 200 held-out pairs per source) with no regression on Western tops. A two-pass hem-aware mask then removes the remaining failure, recoloured trousers below the hem, on all but 3-4% of pairs at…

2611.29914.abs: Image Coding for Machines (ICM) aims to preserve task-relevant information for machine vision under limited bitrates. However, most ICM models are trained for a fixed operating point, and extending them to variable-rate compression is challenging because their training objectives differ across tasks and model designs. In this paper, we propose a loss-agnostic distillation framework for variable-rate ICM. A pretrained fixed-rate ICM model is used as a frozen teacher, while a student model learns variable-rate behavior through importance-adaptive quantization and distillation-based optimization. This enables continuous bitrate control with a single model while preserving task-relevant latent components, without requiring the original task-specific loss or downstream task labels. Experiments based on existing ICM models demonstrate that the proposed method provides continuous bitrate control and achieves competitive recognition performance compared with the fixed-rate models.

2611.29909.abs: A frozen language model can give a wrong answer because a fact is unavailable, a reliable passage is ignored, or an unsupported claim survives generation. We review 116 works on inference-time hallucination intervention and its foundations. We trace the development from retrieval and controllable generation to methods that act on input evidence, token scores, internal representations, completed claims, or the decision to answer. For each family we compare its source of evidence, model access, preparation cost, and the task on which a correction can be established. For activation steering, we distinguish estimating a subspace from applying a state-dependent edit and separate interventions on the prompt from those on the generated prefix. Published comparisons show why faithfulness to a source, factual correctness, informativeness, and answer coverage must be measured separately. Applications in time-sensitive question answering, document synthesis, and visual grounding identify when source authority, evidence availability, or capability preservation limits a reported gain.

ov.problema: Un modello linguistico congelato può dare risposte sbagliate perché un fatto non è disponibile, un passaggio affidabile viene ignorato, o un'affermazione non supportata sopravvive alla generazione. Serve una panoramica dei metodi di intervento a inferenza per l'allucinazione.
ov.idea: Rassegna 116 lavori su interventi a inferenza contro l'allucinazione. Traccia lo sviluppo da retrieval e generazione controllabile a metodi che agiscono su evidenza in input, punteggi dei token, rappresentazioni interne, affermazioni completate o decisione di rispondere. Per ogni famiglia confronta fonte di evidenza, accesso al modello, costo di preparazione e task su cui si stabilisce la correzione. Per activation steering distingue stima di sottospazio e applicazione di modifica dipendente dallo stato, e separa interventi su prompt da quelli su prefisso generato.
ov.risultati: Confronti pubblicati mostrano che fedeltà alla fonte, correttezza fattuale, informatività e copertura delle risposte devono essere misurate separatamente. Applicazioni in QA time-sensitive, sintesi di documenti e grounding visivo identificano quando autorità della fonte, disponibilità di evidenza o preservazione delle capacità limitano il guadagno riportato.
ov.limiti: Non specificati nel testo.

glossario.d: Modifica delle attivazioni interne del modello per guidare il comportamento.
Collegare il testo a elementi visivi in un'immagine o video.

2611.28995.abs: Multi-step retrieval over long contexts is a key capability for retrieval-augmented generation, but strong existing approaches are costly and complex to train. Supervised retrievers are far simpler and cheaper, yet they fall well behind in this setting. We show that this gap stems not from supervised training itself, but from three misalignments between training and inference: easy training negatives, noisy retrieval prefixes, and position-agnostic scoring. Guided by this analysis, we introduce S$^2$LMR, a simple yet effective supervised sequential retriever that models multi-step retrieval as the evolution of an explicit textual state encoded by a single shared Transformer. On long-context reasoning, multi-hop QA, and needle-in-a-haystack benchmarks with context lengths ranging from 4K to 10M tokens, S$^2$LMR achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art methods, substantially outperforming prior supervised retrievers. Notably, it requires only $\sim$2 hours of training on a single A6000 for contexts of up to 10M tokens, while remaining robust across a wide range of hyperparameter settings.

ov.problema: Il recupero multi-step su contesti lunghi è importante per il RAG, ma i metodi esistenti sono costosi e complessi da addestrare. I retriever supervisionati sono più semplici ed economici, ma in questo scenario sono molto indietro.
ov.idea: Gli autori mostrano che il divario non deriva dall'addestramento supervisionato in sé, ma da tre disallineamenti tra training e inferenza: negativi di training troppo facili, prefissi di recupero rumorosi e scoring indipendente dalla posizione. Introducono S²LMR, un retriever sequenziale supervisionato che modella il recupero multi-step come evoluzione di uno stato testuale esplicito, codificato da un singolo Transformer condiviso.
ov.risultati: Su benchmark di ragionamento su contesti lunghi, QA multi-hop e needle-in-a-haystack con contesti da 4K a 10M token, S²LMR raggiunge prestazioni comparabili allo stato dell'arte, superando nettamente i precedenti retriever supervisionati. Richiede solo ~2 ore di addestramento su una singola A6000 per contesti fino a 10M token ed è robusto a un'ampia gamma di iperparametri.

glossario.d: Modello addestrato con esempi etichettati per trovare documenti rilevanti.
Test in cui si cerca un'informazione specifica in un contesto molto lungo.
Rappresentazione del progresso del recupero come testo, non solo vettori.

2611.26254.abs: Hierarchical text detection aims to localize words, text lines, and paragraphs while parsing their structural relationships. It provides essential structural cues for visual text understanding. To maximize accuracy, existing methods typically rely on complex multi-scale feature fusion necks and heavy-weight heads, resulting in bloated architectures and low inference efficiency. In this paper, we argue that a sufficiently pre-trained backbone can effectively replace these sophisticated external modules, while simple geometric inclusion suffices for hierarchical text structural parsing. Thus, we propose Prism, a minimalist framework for hierarchical text detection. Prism performs multi-granularity detection by attaching parallel lightweight heads to a single-scale backbone feature map, covering words, text lines, and paragraphs, and reconstructs the structural hierarchy via an efficient geometric inclusion algorithm. In addition, we systematically compare representative lightweight head archetypes and show that pixel-level regression offers the best accuracy-efficiency trade-off in this setting. Experiments on multiple public benchmarks show that our significantly simplified architecture achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance with remarkable efficiency. Specifically, it runs 1.7times faster than LRANet on CTW1500 while achieving higher accuracy, and surpasses the current SOTA method, OmniParser V2, by over 6 PQ points on the hierarchical HierText dataset. Code will be released soon.

2611.29309.abs: Today's MLLMs can count objects in natural images. However, when asking them how many bolt holes appear in a mechanical drawing or how many nitrogen atoms are in a chemical structure, they often struggle. Counting in technical drawings remains challenging, as objects can be small, densely packed, or even implied by drawing conventions. To study this problem, we introduce CountDrawBench, a benchmark including floor plans, electrical schematics, mechanical drawings, and molecular structures, with 1,574 counting questions and instance-level annotations where available. Besides evaluation, we introduce Code-Verified RL, a reinforcement learning framework that teaches MLLMs to count with executable feedback. Our method combines three complementary rewards: a count reward that checks the final answer, an instance-matching reward that verifies object locations, and a zoom-based reward that checks counting consistency across local image regions. All three are integrated into a unified GRPO objective. Extensive experiments reveal that even leading MLLMs struggle on CountDrawBench, with the best evaluated model achieving only 59.3% accuracy. Our method improves Qwen3.5-9B from 49.3% to 54.3% accuracy, outperforming all evaluated open-source baselines. These results establish CountDrawBench as a challenging testbed for technical drawing understanding and demonstrate the value of code-verified rewards in these tasks. Code and data will be released upon acceptance.

ov.problema: I MLLM (modelli multimodali linguistici e visivi) sanno contare oggetti in immagini naturali, ma faticano su disegni tecnici come fori in disegni meccanici o atomi di azoto in strutture chimiche, dove gli oggetti possono essere piccoli, densi o impliciti nelle convenzioni di disegno.
ov.idea: CountDrawBench è un benchmark con planimetrie, schemi elettrici, disegni meccanici e strutture molecolari, con 1.574 domande di conteggio e annotazioni a livello di istanza dove disponibili. Code-Verified RL è un framework di reinforcement learning che insegna ai MLLM a contare con feedback eseguibile, combinando tre reward: conteggio finale, corrispondenza delle istanze (posizioni) e zoom (coerenza su regioni locali), integrati in un obiettivo GRPO unificato.
ov.risultati: Anche i migliori MLLM valutati faticano su CountDrawBench, con il miglior modello che raggiunge solo il 59,3% di accuratezza. Il metodo migliora Qwen3.5-9B dal 49,3% al 54,3%, superando tutti i baseline open-source valutati.
ov.limiti: Il miglior modello valutato raggiunge solo il 59,3%, quindi il problema resta difficile; codice e dati saranno rilasciati all'accettazione.

glossario.d: Modello linguistico multimodale che elabora testo e immagini.
Metodo di reinforcement learning per ottimizzare modelli linguistici con reward.
Segnale di ricompensa che guida l'apprendimento per rinforzo.

2611.30449.abs: Coordinating locomotion and dexterous manipulation is fundamental to humanoid robots operating in human environments. A key challenge is learning motion priors from diverse data and using them effectively for coordinated robot control. We present CHAMP, a unified framework for humanoid loco-manipulation that combines whole-body motion pretraining with adaptive feature extraction. CHAMP pretrains a vision-language model to predict future body and hand motion from approximately 2,298 hours of heterogeneous human and robot data. A shared motion representation enables unified whole-body motion learning across embodiments from datasets with body annotations, hand annotations, or both. To ground these motion priors in robot control, we introduce a Coordination-oriented Action Expert (CAE) and train it on replay data generated using the target controller. Through sparse routing, CAE adaptively selects, transforms, and fuses features from multiple layers of the pretrained model to jointly generate body and hand actions. In experiments, CHAMP achieves overall success rates of 84.8% on seven simulated tasks and 91.4% on seven real-world tasks with a Unitree G1, outperforming the evaluated baselines in both settings. In particular, CHAMP achieves 70.0% success on the long-horizon popcorn-serving task, compared with 40.0% for the best-performing baseline.

2611.30934.abs: The search for computationally efficient alternatives to the Transformer has yielded numerous architectures in recent years; however, most exhibit severe weaknesses in associative recall-such as key-value (KV) retrieval-and length extrapolation, where even standard Transformers struggle. This paper introduces LimeTree, a linear-complexity architecture in both memory and compute for sequence modeling. By integrating synthetic KV retrieval tasks directly into standard language modeling training, LimeTree achieves strong perplexity alongside reliable recall. Two variants were evaluated on WikiText-103 and PG-19 under strict compute constraints. On WikiText-103, LimeTree reaches a token-level perplexity of 19 in just 6 hours on four Quadro RTX 8000 GPUs, while maintaining 100\% KV retrieval accuracy even when extrapolating from a training context length of 512 to an evaluation length of 16,384. On PG-19, the model achieves a token-level perplexity of 13 in 35 hours on a single RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU with minimal hyperparameter tuning. These results position LimeTree as a competitive linear-complexity alternative to Transformers, combining superior perplexity and training throughput with robust in-context retrieval and length extrapolation.

ov.problema: Le alternative efficienti al Transformer spesso falliscono nel richiamo associativo (recupero di coppie chiave-valore) e nell'estrapolazione di lunghezza, cioè la capacità di generalizzare a contesti più lunghi di quelli visti in training.
ov.idea: LimeTree è un'architettura a complessità lineare in memoria e calcolo per sequenze, basata su grafi ad albero. Integra task sintetici di recupero chiave-valore direttamente nel training di language modeling, ottenendo buona perplessità e recall affidabile.
ov.risultati: Su WikiText-103 raggiunge perplessità a livello di token di 19 in 6 ore su quattro GPU Quadro RTX 8000, con accuratezza di recupero KV del 100% estrapolando da lunghezza di training 512 a 16.384. Su PG-19 raggiunge perplessità 13 in 35 ore su una singola GPU RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell.
ov.limiti: I risultati sono su due dataset e con vincoli di calcolo specifici; non è chiaro come si comporti su task più complessi o su scala maggiore.

glossario.d: Misura di quanto un modello è incerto nel predire il prossimo token; più bassa è meglio.
Capacità di recuperare un valore associato a una chiave vista in precedenza nel contesto.
Generalizzare a sequenze più lunghe di quelle usate in addestramento.

2611.30259.abs: Security benchmarks for LLM agents record whether each attack succeeded and compare agents, attacks, and defenses by attack success rate (ASR). Such comparisons are valid only if the agent, the attack, and the defense cause each verdict. We show that verdicts also depend on content-free state: details of a run that carry no information about the system under test, such as the Python hash seed, the order of tools or evidence, and the scoring of failed runs. We require that this state influence no verdict (decision noninterference) and treat it as untrusted input, because evaluators and requesters of LLM-based gates can choose it. Our framework, TARE (Testing Attribution of Reported Effects), attributes a reported effect to the agent, attack, or defense only if it exceeds the measured influence of content-free state. On Agent Security Bench (ASB), runs with a fixed hash seed are identical for seven agents from four model families, yet changing the seed changes up to 17% of an agent's verdicts while the ASR moves by at most 5 points. The seed acts through the tool order: sorting the tool list instead of reverse-sorting it raises the ASR by up to 19 points, because ASB's naming convention places attacker tools first. When the same evidence is reordered, six of seven LLM judges change their decision on 17-91% of 98 proposed actions. Across eighteen agent-defense combinations, TARE's worst-case test attributes effects to two of three defenses, one of them in opposite directions on two agents, and a test fixed in advance confirms a 4.8-point decrease from the third; in the…

ov.problema: I benchmark di sicurezza per agenti LLM confrontano agenti, attacchi e difese tramite tasso di successo dell'attacco (ASR), ma i verdetti possono dipendere da dettagli irrilevanti (es. seed hash, ordine strumenti).
ov.idea: Gli autori richiedono che lo stato senza contenuto non influenzi i verdetti (non interferenza decisionale) e lo trattano come input non fidato. Il framework TARE attribuisce un effetto all'agente, attacco o difesa solo se supera l'influenza misurata dello stato senza contenuto.
ov.risultati: Su Agent Security Bench, con seed fisso sette agenti sono identici, ma cambiare seed cambia fino al 17% dei verdetti e l'ASR fino a 5 punti. Ordinare la lista strumenti invece di invertirla alza l'ASR fino a 19 punti. Riordinando le stesse evidenze, sei giudici LLM su sette cambiano decisione sul 17-91% di 98 azioni. TARE attribuisce effetti a due difese su tre, una in direzioni opposte.
ov.limiti: Il framework richiede di misurare l'influenza dello stato senza contenuto, che può essere costoso o difficile da definire completamente.

glossario.d: Attack Success Rate: percentuale di attacchi riusciti.
Dettagli di un'esecuzione che non dipendono dal sistema testato, come seed o ordine.
Proprietà per cui lo stato senza contenuto non deve cambiare i verdetti.

2611.29847.abs: Runtime guardrails protect mobile GUI agents by assessing each proposed action before execution, but existing guardrails rely on cloud hosted large multimodal models, exposing every screen to a remote server, including private information such as payments, messages, and medical records. We propose MobileGrail, an on-device deployable model that addresses both. It maintains a recurrent task state that retains only the evidence subsequent safety decisions depend on, so that authorization and execution progress persist beyond the short context. To intervene early while keeping the safety boundary precise, it learns two labels, unsafe and block: unsafe marks the action that commits a violation, whereas block may be issued at any step of an intervention window, which spans from the first action that the user's authorization no longer explains to the committing action itself. To support training, we build an environment of 32 applications whose backends verify the effect of every action, supplying verified labels for supervision and rewards for reinforcement learning to calibrate intervention timing. We also build MobileVeto, an offline benchmark of unsafe trajectories largely on held-out applications, each paired with a benign counterpart. On MobileVeto, MobileGrail built on Qwen3.5-2B intercepts 76.2% of violations, up from 64.5% for its prompted backbone, while reducing premature intervention from 58.6% to 5.2%, outperforming the cloud-based OS-Sentinel on both. We further conduct online evaluation on GhostEIBench, where MobileGrail guarding a Qwen3.8-27B agent reduces fully…

ov.problema: I guardrail (filtri di sicurezza) per gli agenti che controllano interfacce grafiche mobili girano su grandi modelli cloud, esponendo ogni schermata a un server remoto, incluse informazioni private come pagamenti, messaggi e cartelle cliniche.
ov.idea: MobileGrail è un modello deployabile on-device che mantiene uno stato ricorrente del task, conservando solo le evidenze necessarie alle decisioni di sicurezza successive. Impara due etichette: 'unsafe' (l'azione che commette la violazione) e 'block' (che può essere emesso in qualsiasi momento della finestra di intervento, dalla prima azione non più giustificata dall'autorizzazione fino all'azione che commette la violazione).
ov.risultati: Su MobileVeto, MobileGrail basato su Qwen3.5-2B intercetta il 76.2% delle violazioni, contro il 64.5% del backbone con prompting, e riduce l'intervento prematuro dal 58.6% al 5.2%, superando il cloud-based OS-Sentinel su entrambe le metriche.
ov.limiti: Il testo si interrompe prima di completare la descrizione dei risultati e non riporta altri limiti espliciti.

glossario.d: Filtro di sicurezza che valuta ogni azione prima dell'esecuzione
Eseguito localmente sul dispositivo, senza inviare dati al cloud
Memoria interna che si aggiorna passo per passo mantenendo solo le informazioni rilevanti

2611.29793.abs: Moving quantum code from Qiskit to NVIDIA CUDA-Q is a practical adoption cost that language models are starting to automate. We ask whether a small open model can learn this translation, and how to measure it so that the result can be trusted. Both programs can be executed and their state vectors compared, so a kernel counts as correct only if it prepares the same state as the Qiskit reference (fidelity >= 0.999), with no text matching and no LLM judge. We build a 640-task benchmark with three test sets (larger circuits, an unseen circuit family, an unseen Qiskit coding style) and a QuantumKatas regression probe, and we test the evaluator before training. Measurement counts miss every phase-only error; a surface rule-based translator solves two of three original splits (text substitution); a converter that executes the Qiskit input and maps the circuit solves all 640 tasks -- so the benchmark measures source-level translation, not whether a circuit can be ported after running it. No base model emits a valid CUDA-Q kernel zero-shot. On Nemotron 3 Nano 4B, LoRA reaches 83.9%, tying a 4-shot prompt (83.1%), but generalizes worse to unseen style (48.5% vs. 65.5%) and cuts QuantumKatas from 23.8% to 8.9%; on Qwen2.5-Coder 7B, LoRA beats the prompt overall (92.0% vs. 82.8%) and on unseen style (78.5% vs. 65.0%), and on the 1.5B model as well, so whether fine-tuning pays off depends on the base model, while the Qiskit regression appears in all three. Mixing two replay formats is the best mitigation trade-off (84.4% translation, Katas 21.5%). On 48 parametric functions that must…

2611.28748.abs: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is known to reduce training-data leakage in single-turn interactions, but whether this protection persists over multi-turn conversations is unclear. We introduce CRELT (Conversational RAG Extraction Leakage Trajectory), a reusable framework that tracks, turn by turn, the real contact details from the training data that a RAG system discloses. CRELT separates retrieval, conversation history, and attack strategy through a full-factorial design, uses a retrieval corpus verified to contain none of the target PII, and counts an item as leaked only when it is absent from the model input at the turn it is produced. In our main experiment, this criterion excludes 29-53% of raw matches that were already present in the input. Across GPT-J-6B, Pythia-6.9B, and Pythia-12B, targeting real Enron contact details, retrieval reduces disclosure under both full and cleared history, consistent with prior single-turn results. A length-matched control with random passages reproduces 91-99.5% of this reduction under cleared history and 47-78% under full history, so much of it comes from the added context rather than from what is retrieved. With retrieval enabled, however, retaining full conversation history increases disclosure by a factor of 3.6-4.9, while retaining only one previous turn already restores disclosure to approximately the full-history level. With retrieval, clearing the history reduces disclosure by 72-79%, but does not eliminate it. These results show that single-turn privacy audits can substantially underestimate training-data leakage in…

ov.problema: Il RAG riduce la fuga di dati di addestramento in singolo turno, ma non è chiaro se la protezione regge in conversazioni multi-turno.
ov.idea: Introducono CRELT, un framework che traccia turno per turno i dettagli di contatto reali rivelati dal sistema RAG.
