ov.risultati: Su Qwen3-8B, Wavefront migliora il throughput rispetto a xPress, DSpark e DFlash del 2.6%, 10.7% e 23.6% in media su benchmark di matematica, codice, chat e agenti, e del 9.6%, 14.3% e 28.9% su prompt long-context di SPEED-Bench. Su Qwen3.8-27B supera DFlash2, DSpark e xPress del 7.6%, 10.6% e 5.0%, e del 7.4%, 5.8% e 6.0% sugli stessi prompt long-context. I guadagni persistono con concorrenza fino a 32.
ov.limiti: I risultati sono misurati solo su Qwen3-8B e Qwen3.8-27B e su specifici benchmark; non è chiaro se i guadagni si mantengano su altri modelli o carichi.

glossario.d: Tecnica in cui un modello piccolo propone token che il modello grande verifica in parallelo.
Strato finale che trasforma gli stati nascosti in probabilità sui token del vocabolario.
Rappresentazione statica di una sequenza di operazioni GPU, eseguita senza overhead di lancio.

2611.31511.abs: Recent work shows that pretrained Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit near-zero forgetting in specific continual learning settings with experience replay. However, robustness to domain shift of learned tasks remains unexplored. In this work, we study the robustness of Pi0 fine-tuned with experience replay under out-of-distribution (OOD) data using the LIBERO and LIBERO-Plus benchmarks. While the in-domain (ID) setup achieves near-zero catastrophic forgetting, OOD performance on previous tasks quickly collapses. Specifically, we show that during the continual learning process, the OOD capabilities of the model degrade, following a shared representational pattern across domain shifts, which is also visible behaviorally in the two simpler suites. Representational analysis shows that drift concentrates in the multimodal and action features. Linear probes indicate that OOD features still retain task-relevant information, but appear unreadable, consistent with representation misalignment. These findings suggest that even when ID stability remains intact, severe OOD forgetting can still occur, accompanied by representational drift during continual learning.

2611.32108.abs: Bimanual manipulation requires each arm to perform distinct motions while coordinating with the other. Common flow-based robotic policies combine both arms' actions into one token per future timestep, giving attention distinct positions across time but not across arms. We introduce Duo, a simple but effective design that models spatial and temporal dependencies within one shared action head. Specifically, Duo separates both arms into two action tokens per timestep, allowing each arm's motion to interact via cross-arm attention during flow matching. On RoboTwin 2.0, Duo improves the overall success of all four base policies, from 0.45B to 3.62B parameters, with gains of 12.55 and 9.02 percentage points for FLOWER (0.89B) and $π_{0.5}$ (3.62B), respectively. Despite its compact size, FLOWER-Duo achieves the best randomized-generalization, precision, and memory scores on RoboDojo. In real-world tasks, it outperforms $π_{0.5}$ in both success rate and execution speed, while scaling effectively with increasing training data. To provide deeper insight into the design of Duo, we conduct systematic ablations on inter-arm coordination, action grouping, and token granularity, confirming that cross-arm attention drives the improvement while arm-wise interaction offers the best accuracy-compute trade-off.

2611.31800.abs: LLM agents commonly use the full interaction history as a proxy for state, retaining all past observations and actions regardless of whether they remain relevant. We instead ask what information an agent actually needs to carry forward. We define agent state as a compact abstraction of interaction history that preserves the competence of a fixed reference agent, with the minimal such abstraction as the ideal. Because matching the reference agent's behavior is unnecessarily restrictive and difficult for black-box policies, we define sufficiency through task performance rather than behavior matching. We represent state abstractions as deterministic recursive programs and search over them using an LLM-guided genetic algorithm. Across ALFWorld and ScienceWorld, the learned abstractions preserve near-reference task success while reducing mean policy input by up to 71% and 57%, respectively. The resulting programs are directly inspectable, providing an explicit account of what information is retained, updated, and discarded during interaction.

2611.31579.abs: This paper investigates Product Quantization (PQ) Optimization with Gaussian data. It offers three key contributions (i) a proof that SVD is the optimal preconditioning rotation for PQ; (ii) a new Extended Zador (EZ) estimator of the $k$-means quantization cost that is accurate in low bit rates and low dimensions; and (iii) a novel segmentation algorithm based on 1-d bin packing of global bit allocations. The result is a simple algorithm (EZPQ) with strong approximation guarantees. It matches OPQ's empirical accuracy while providing a per-instance distortion lower bound certificate under the Gaussian EZ cost model. On typical real embedding spectra, EZPQ with 2 bits per coordinate is often certifiably within 1% of the optimum in this model. It also consistently achieves a lower reconstruction error than all random-rotation-based algorithms such as EDEN, E-RaBitQ, and TurboQuant.

ov.problema: La Product Quantization (PQ) con dati gaussiani è usata per comprimere vettori, ma ottimizzare la quantizzazione e capire quanto sia vicina all'ottimo è difficile, specialmente a bassi bit rate e basse dimensioni.
ov.idea: Il paper dà tre contributi: (i) dimostra che SVD è la rotazione di precondizionamento ottimale per PQ; (ii) introduce un nuovo stimatore Extended Zador (EZ) del costo di quantizzazione k-means, accurato a bassi bit rate e basse dimensioni; (iii) propone un algoritmo di segmentazione basato su bin packing 1-d delle allocazioni globali di bit. Il risultato è EZPQ, un algoritmo semplice con forti garanzie di approssimazione.
ov.risultati: EZPQ eguaglia l'accuratezza empirica di OPQ e fornisce un certificato di limite inferiore di distorsione per istanza sotto il modello gaussiano EZ. Su spettri di embedding reali tipici, EZPQ con 2 bit per coordinata è spesso certificabilmente entro l'1% dall'ottimo in questo modello. Inoltre ottiene consistentemente un errore di ricostruzione inferiore a tutti gli algoritmi basati su rotazioni casuali come EDEN, E-RaBitQ e TurboQuant.
ov.limiti: Le garanzie valgono sotto il modello gaussiano EZ; non è chiaro quanto si estendano a distribuzioni reali non gaussiane.

glossario.d: Tecnica che scompone vettori in sottovettori e li quantizza separatamente per comprimerli.
Decomposizione ai valori singolari, usata per ruotare i dati in modo ottimale.
Problema di allocare oggetti in contenitori di capacità limitata.

2611.31496.abs: Representation quality in pretrained text foundation models is not concentrated at the final layer, yet practitioners routinely probe it there because layer selection without labels has remained an open problem. We present a large-scale empirical study of where layer quality lives across 25 models spanning four architectural families and four pretraining strategies, evaluated on 13 datasets across classification, pair classification, semantic textual similarity, and multiple-choice question answering. Peak probing layers depend systematically on pretraining strategy and architecture: masked encoders peak in late-middle layers, sequence-to-sequence models shift their peak with task type, contrastive sentence encoders concentrate signal at the final layer under CLS and last-token readouts but peak early under mean pooling, and decoder-only models exhibit distinct phase structure tied to depth. We distill these findings into the Stable Geometry Index (SGI), a closed-form, fully label-free selector with no fitted coefficients combining power-law fit quality, effective-rank capacity, spectral stability, and a weak depth prior. Across 383 evaluation groups SGI improves over the last-layer baseline and lifts Hit@3 from 0.39 to 0.52, recovering 40% of the gap to the oracle without using any labels, and exceeds a supervised ELMo-style layer mix on the matched subset despite using strictly less information. Our ablations also reverse a common assumption in the spectral-decay literature: power-law fit quality is a stronger predictor of layer quality than the exponent's proximity to…

ov.problema: La qualità delle rappresentazioni nei modelli di testo pre-addestrati non è concentrata nello strato finale, ma i pratici lo usano comunemente perché selezionare lo strato senza etichette è un problema aperto.
ov.idea: Gli autori presentano uno studio empirico su 25 modelli (quattro famiglie architetturali e quattro strategie di pre-addestramento) valutati su 13 dataset. Distillano i risultati in Stable Geometry Index (SGI), un selettore in forma chiusa, senza etichette e senza coefficienti addestrati, che combina qualità del fit power-law, capacità di rango effettivo, stabilità spettrale e un debole prior sulla profondità.
ov.risultati: Su 383 gruppi di valutazione, SGI migliora rispetto alla baseline dello strato finale e porta Hit@3 da 0.39 a 0.52, recuperando il 40% del divario rispetto all'oracolo senza usare etichette. Supera anche un mix di strati supervisionato in stile ELMo sul sottoinsieme corrispondente, pur usando meno informazione.
ov.limiti: Lo studio è limitato a modelli di testo e a 13 dataset; non è chiaro se SGI generalizzi ad altri domini o architetture non testate.

glossario.d: tecnica per valutare la qualità delle rappresentazioni di uno strato tramite un classificatore semplice
frazione di casi in cui lo strato corretto è tra i primi 3 selezionati
misura della dimensionalità effettiva delle rappresentazioni

2611.32054.abs: Surgical scene understanding is constrained by data scarcity and long-tail class imbalance, as annotating surgical videos demands scarce clinical expertise while rare procedural events remain underrepresented. We tackle this through data generation and propose SurgGenesis, a generative surgical world model that learns future surgical state transitions in a latent space from visual observations and textual procedural descriptions, serving as a scalable surgical data engine. To adapt a large-scale video diffusion model to the data-scarce surgical domain without catastrophic forgetting, we introduce a three-stage progressive LoRA strategy that incrementally injects endoscopic visual priors, procedural semantics, and spatial motion cues. Rather than judging generation by visual fidelity alone, we validate SurgGenesis along two axes that separate a world model from a generic generator: (i) future-awareness, by comparing predicted futures against the real future through a GT-latent prediction gap and temporal-horizon analysis, and (ii) action-faithful usefulness, by checking that generated clips contain the commanded surgical triplet and that using them to rebalance long-tail events and drive downstream understanding (segmentation, triplet recognition, 3D reconstruction) yields action-specific gains. Conditioned futures therefore complement conventional long-tail sampling. Code: https://zh-qr.github.io/SurgGenesis

2611.31794.abs: Frontier models are increasingly used through harnesses as agents, with growing autonomy to do useful work. Agent performance can often be enhanced by the use of skills: reusable workflows, code, and prompts that provide task-related information or guide the behaviour of the model. Skills, being textual in nature, present themselves as another editable surface to be optimized; current methods have improved on handcrafting and one-shot generation by treating skill development as an iterative process, using score-driven search to tweak and improve performance. In this paper, we demonstrate the efficacy of the agents themselves as optimizers: across five benchmarks, a coding agent without guidance substantially improves every target and outperforms published skill-optimization methods. More broadly, this shows the capability of agents to do such work and to refine their own behaviour to provide task-specific context, as long as they are given a metric to measure against.

2611.31520.abs: We introduce an image compression framework with three properties: (i) adaptation of pretrained codecs without retraining or fine-tuning, (ii) cycle-consistent recompression, even of already-encoded images, and (iii) decoding with independently chosen generative priors. We wrap the frozen encoder with non-learned operations so that every continuous latent has a preimage, yielding a surjective pseudo-invertible neural network. A nonlinear right inverse built from the pretrained decoder satisfies $E'(D'(E'(x)))=E'(x)$. To extend consistency to quantized bitstreams, the receiver searches for a continuous latent that reproduces both the transmitted main symbols and entropy side information. A successful search and an exact correction preserve both streams under deterministic coding; the final reconstruction is checked through the actual coding path. The encoder's pseudo-inverse enables a nonlinear counterpart of back-projection. In the linear case, back-projection has the closed-form solution $x'=x+A^\dagger(y-Ax)$, giving the closest reconstruction to $x$ satisfying $Ax'=y$. Our nonlinear formulation enforces the transmitted code on proposals from an independently chosen generative model. Adjusting the starting noise controls the prior's influence without changing that code. 2611.31436.abs: Staging sleep on a wearable device keeps the raw electroencephalogram (EEG) private and saves the energy needed to transmit it. It also requires small, energy-efficient neural networks. We benchmark 13 post-training quantization (PTQ) configurations, from FP16 to the block-scaled 4-bit formats MXFP4 and NVFP4, for five-stage sleep staging from single-channel Fpz-Cz EEG. We use Sleep-EDF-78 (78 subjects), subject-wise cross-validation, three training seeds, value-exact emulation, and per-subject paired statistics. All 8- and 16-bit formats stay within 0.45 percentage points (pp) of FP32 Macro-F1. With 4-bit weights and activations, an epoch-wise CNN loses 1.98 to 3.04 pp, and a temporal-context network loses at most 1.19 pp. A same-encoder ablation shows that temporal context explains little of this gap. At equal block size, NVFP4 outperforms MXFP4. The first layer, which quantizes the raw EEG, is the most sensitive layer in both networks. Keeping the first and last layers in FP8 brings both tested 4-bit formats within 0.48 pp of FP32. This recipe adds at most 2.1% weight storage, needs no retraining, and is equivalent to quantization-aware training (QAT) within an exploratory 1-pp margin. The 4-bit losses fall on the same subjects across architectures (Spearman correlation coefficient = 0.69 to 0.79), and they reduce N3 recall the most. On the nested Sleep-EDF-20 subset, NVFP4 with FP8 first and last layers again stays within 0.25 pp of FP32.
